verses.text:
प्रविश्य तु महारण्यं दण्डकारण्यमात्मवान्।
रामो ददर्श दुर्धर्षस्तापसाश्रममण्डलम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having entered the dense forest of Daṇḍaka, the self-controlled and unassailable Śrī Rāma saw a group of hermitages of sages. (1)

verses.text:
कुशचीरपरिक्षिप्तं ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समावृतम्।
यथा प्रदीप्तं दुर्दर्शं गगने सूर्यमण्डलम्॥ २॥
शरण्यं सर्वभूतानां सुसम्मृष्टाजिरं सदा।
मृगैर्बहुभिराकीर्णं पक्षिसंघैः समावृतम्॥ ३॥
पूजितं चोपनृत्तं च नित्यमप्सरसां गणैः।
विशालैरग्निशरणैः स्रुग्भाण्डैरजिनैः कुशैः॥ ४॥
समिद्भिस्तोयकलशैः फलमूलैश्च शोभितम्।
आरण्यैश्च महावृक्षैः पुण्यैः स्वादुफलैर्वृतम्॥ ५॥
बलिहोमार्चितं पुण्यं ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्।
पुष्पैश्चान्यैः परिक्षिप्तं पद्मिन्या च सपद्मया॥ ६॥
फलमूलाशनैर्दान्तैश्चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरैः।
सूर्यवैश्वानराभैश्च पुराणैर्मुनिभिर्युतम्॥ ७॥
पुण्यैश्च नियताहारैः शोभितं परमर्षिभिः।
तद् ब्रह्मभवनप्रख्यं ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: With the sacred Kuśa grass and bark-garments scattered all around, nay, enveloped in grandeur of the knowledge of Brahma, looking like the dazzling orb of the sun in the sky, difficult to look at, the resort of all beings, with courtyards always well-swept, crowded with several wild beasts and swarmed with groups of birds, always revered and admired with dance by teams of celestial nymphs, decorated with large fire-sanctuaries, sacrificial utensils, skin-carpets, blades of the Kuśa grass and faggots, vessels of water and fruits and roots, surrounded by large sacred forest-trees having sweet fruits, worshipped with oblations and sacrifices, auspicious, resounding with the chanting of Vedic hymns, having ponds with lotuses and scattered all over with other flowers, inhabited by old sages of controlled senses, living on fruits and roots, wearing garments of bark and the skin of black antelopes and shining like the sun and fire, and graced by the greatest of sages auspicious and restrained in diet; it shone like the residence of Lord Brahmā resounding with the chanting to Vedic hymns. (2—8)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मविद्भिर्महाभागैर्ब्राह्मणैरुपशोभितम्।
तद् दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमांस्तापसाश्रममण्डलम्॥ ९॥
अभ्यगच्छन्महातेजा विज्यं कृत्वा महद् धनुः।
दिव्यज्ञानोपपन्नास्ते रामं दृष्ट्वा महर्षयः॥ १०॥
अभिजग्मुस्तदा प्रीता वैदेहीं च यशस्विनीम्।
ते तु सोममिवोद्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा वै धर्मचारिणम्॥ ११॥
लक्ष्मणं चैव दृष्ट्वा तु वैदेहीं च यशस्विनीम्।
मङ्गलानि प्रयुञ्जानाः प्रत्यगृह्णन् दृढव्रताः॥ १२॥
रूपसंहननं लक्ष्मीं सौकुमार्यं सुवेषताम्।
ददृशुर्विस्मिताकारा रामस्य वनवासिनः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Seeing that group of hermitages of sages, adorned with highly blessed Brāhmaṇas, knowers of Brahma, the glorious and highly lustrous Rāma removed the string of his great bow and entered into the hermitages. Then, beholding Rāma, those great sages possessed of divine knowledge approached him and the renowned Vaidehī with pleasure. They saw him given to the practice of virtue and charming like the rising moon and also Lakṣmaṇa and Vaidehī of renown and, being firm observers of vows, welcomed them performing auspicious rites. The forest-dwellers saw with amazement the handsome build of the body, grandeur, tenderness and ascetic dress of Rāma. (9—13)

verses.text:
वैदेहीं लक्ष्मणं रामं नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव।
आश्चर्यभूतान् ददृशुः सर्वे ते वनवासिनः॥ १४॥
verses.m: All those forest dwellers saw Vaidehī, the princess of Videha country, Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma as a wonder with eyes as though steady. (14)

verses.text:
अत्रैनं हि महाभागाः सर्वभूतहिते रताः।
अतिथिं पर्णशालायां राघवं संन्यवेशयन्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Here, indeed, the highly fortunate sages, taking delight in the good of all beings, lodged the scion of Raghu as a guest in a hut made of leaves. (15)

verses.text:
ततो रामस्य सत्कृत्य विधिना पावकोपमाः।
आजह्रुस्ते महाभागाः सलिलं धर्मचारिणः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Then, honouring Rāma with traditional rites, the fire-like righteous sages of great fortune offered water. (16)

verses.text:
मङ्गलानि प्रयुञ्जाना मुदा परमया युताः।
मूलं पुष्पं फलं सर्वमाश्रमं च महात्मनः॥ १७॥
निवेदयित्वा धर्मज्ञास्ते तु प्राञ्जलयोऽब्रुवन्।
धर्मपालो जनस्यास्य शरण्यश्च महायशाः॥ १८॥
पूजनीयश्च मान्यश्च राजा दण्डधरो गुरुः।
इन्द्रस्यैव चतुर्भागः प्रजा रक्षति राघव॥ १९॥
verses.m: Performing auspicious rites with great delight the magnanimous sages offered roots, flowers, fruits and even the whole hermitage and those knowers of the righteous customs, with joined palms, said, “The king being the protector of righteousness and also the resort for these people, famous, revered and respectable holder of the staff of justice, worshipful and the fourth part of Indra himself, protects the subjects, O scion of Raghu ! (17—19)

verses.text:
राजा तस्माद् वरान् भोगान् रम्यान् भुङ्क्ते नमस्कृतः।
ते वयं भवता रक्ष्या भवद्विषयवासिनः।
नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा त्वं नो राजा जनेश्वरः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “It is hence that the king, who is saluted by all, enjoys the foremost, delightful pleasures. We being the residents of your kingdom deserve protection by you. Whether staying in the city or in the forest, you, the lord of the people, are our king. (20)

verses.text:
न्यस्तदण्डा वयं राजञ्जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः।
रक्षणीयास्त्वया शश्वद् गर्भभूतास्तपोधनाः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Having given up punishment, controlled anger and conquered the senses and having the wealth of asceticism, we should always be protected by you as a foetus by the mother.” (21)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा फलैर्मूलैः पुष्पैरन्यैश्च राघवम्।
वन्यैश्च विविधाहारैः सलक्ष्मणमपूजयन्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Thus speaking, they entertained the scion of Raghu, Śrī Rāma and Sītā, together with Lakṣmaṇa, with fruits, roots, flowers and several other forest-products. (22)

verses.text:
तथान्ये तापसाः सिद्धा रामं वैश्वानरोपमाः।
न्यायवृत्ता यथान्यायं तर्पयामासुरीश्वरम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Similarly, other hermits, well-accomplished, comparable with fire and following a just tradition honoured Lord Rāma in accordance with the custom. (23)

verses.text:
कृतातिथ्योऽथ रामस्तु सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति।
आमन्त्र्य स मुनीन् सर्वान् वनमेवान्वगाहत॥ १॥
verses.m: Then, Rāma after receiving the hospitality, took leave of all the sages at sunrise and plunged into the depths of the forest. (1)

verses.text:
नानामृगगणाकीर्णमृक्षशार्दूलसेवितम्।
ध्वस्तवृक्षलतागुल्मं दुर्दर्शसलिलाशयम्॥ २॥
निष्कूजमानशकुनिं झिल्लिकागणनादितम्।
लक्ष्मणानुचरो रामो वनमध्यं ददर्श ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Rāma, with Lakṣmaṇa as his follower, saw the heart of the forest crowded with herds of various deer, resorted to by boars and tigers; the shrubs, trees and creepers in which had been destroyed, the water-reservoirs in which were not visible, in which the birds were not singing and which was made noisy by swarms of crickets. (2-3)

verses.text:
सीतया सह काकुत्स्थस्तस्मिन् घोरमृगायुते।
ददर्श गिरिशृङ्गाभं पुरुषादं महास्वनम्॥ ४॥
गभीराक्षं महावक्त्रं विकटं विकटोदरम्।
बीभत्सं विषमं दीर्घं विकृतं घोरदर्शनम्॥ ५॥
वसानं चर्म वैयाघ्रं वसार्द्रं रुधिरोक्षितम्।
त्रासनं सर्वभूतानां व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम्॥ ६॥
त्रीन् सिंहांश्चतुरो व्याघ्रान् द्वौ वृकौ पृषतान् दश।
सविषाणं वसादिग्धं गजस्य च शिरो महत्॥ ७॥
अवसज्यायसे शूले विनदन्तं महास्वनम्।
स रामं लक्ष्मणं चैव सीतां दृष्ट्वा च मैथिलीम्।
अभ्यधावत् सुसंक्रुद्धः प्रजाः काल इवान्तकः॥ ८॥
स कृत्वा भैरवं नादं चालयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥ ९॥
अङ्केनादाय वैदेहीमपक्रम्य तदाब्रवीत्।
युवां जटाचीरधरौ सभार्यौ क्षीणजीवितौ॥ १०॥
प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यं शरचापासिपाणिनौ।
कथं तापसयोर्वां च वासः प्रमदया सह॥ ११॥
verses.m: Rāma (a descendant of Kakutstha) together with Sītā saw in that forest, full of wild animals, a dreadful man-eating ogre of terrific voice, looking like a mountain-peak, having deep eyes, a huge mouth, a fierce belly, despicable, uneven, tall, abnormal, presenting a terrible sight, wearing a tiger’s skin wet with fat and sprinkled with blood, molesting all beings, resembling the god of death with his mouth wide open, tying three lions, four tigers, two wolves, ten spotted deer and the big head of an elephant with tusks, and wet with fat, to an iron lance, and roaring in a terrific voice. He saw Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and also Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, and attacked them with great anger as Kāla, the destroyer of people, attacks them. He made a terrific sound as though making the earth tremble, took the princess of Videha country, Sītā, in his arms, went afar and then said, “You two having matted hair and wearing a bark-garment, and still having a wife with you, with your life coming to an end, have entered the Daṇḍaka forest, taking arrows, bow and sword in your hands. Again, how are you two ascetics staying with a woman? (4—11)

verses.text:
अधर्मचारिणौ पापौ कौ युवां मुनिदूषकौ।
अहं वनमिदं दुर्गं विराधो नाम राक्षसः॥ १२॥
चरामि सायुधो नित्यमृषिमांसानि भक्षयन्।
इयं नारी वरारोहा मम भार्या भविष्यति॥ १३॥
युवयोः पापयोश्चाहं पास्यामि रुधिरं मृधे।
तस्यैवं ब्रुवतो दुष्टं विराधस्य दुरात्मनः॥ १४॥
श्रुत्वा सगर्वितं वाक्यं सम्भ्रान्ता जनकात्मजा।
सीता प्रवेपितोद्वेगात् प्रवाते कदली यथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Who are you two sinners, doing unrighteous deeds, bringing a blot upon the sages? Armed with weapons, I, an ogre named Virādha, always wander in this forest, which is difficult of access, eating the flesh of sages. This beautiful lady will become my wife and I shall drink the blood of you two sinners on the battlefield.” Hearing thus the wicked and boastful speech of that wicked Virādha, the overawed Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, trembled with fear as does a plantain tree in a storm. (12—15)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा राघवः सीतां विराधाङ्कगतां शुभाम्।
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं मुखेन परिशुष्यता॥ १६॥
verses.m: Beholding that auspicious Sītā in the lap of Virādha, Rāma (a scion of Raghu) said to Lakṣmaṇa with his mouth getting parched : (16)

verses.text:
पश्य सौम्य नरेन्द्रस्य जनकस्यात्मसम्भवाम्।
मम भार्यां शुभाचारां विराधाङ्के प्रवेशिताम्॥ १७॥
अत्यन्तसुखसंवृद्धां राजपुत्रीं यशस्विनीम्।
यदभिप्रेतमस्मासु प्रियं वरवृतं च यत्॥ १८॥
कैकेय्यास्तु सुसंवृत्तं क्षिप्रमद्यैव लक्ष्मण।
या न तुष्यति राज्येन पुत्रार्थे दीर्घदर्शिनी॥ १९॥
ययाहं सर्वभूतानां प्रियः प्रस्थापितो वनम्।
अद्येदानीं सकामा सा या माता मध्यमा मम॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Oh dear ! see this daughter of King Janaka, my wife of good conduct, brought up in great prosperity, a princess of renown, having passed into the lap of Virādha. What the far-sighted Kaikeyī—who was not satisfied with the kingdom for her son, who has sent me, liked by all beings, to the forest—had fondly cherished regarding us, that for which she had asked for two boons has well happened quickly, today only, O Lakṣmaṇa ! Today, know, that mother of mine, Kaikeyī, has her desire fulfilled. (17—20)

verses.text:
परस्पर्शात् तु वैदेह्या न दुःखतरमस्ति मे।
पितुर्विनाशात् सौमित्रे स्वराज्यहरणात् तथा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “There is nothing more sorrowful to me than the princess of the Videha country being touched by another, which is more painful even than the death of my father and the loss of my kingdom, O son of Sumitrā”. (21)

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे बाष्पशोकपरिप्लुतः।
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो रुद्धो नाग इव श्वसन्॥ २२॥
verses.m: While the descendant of Kakutstha, Rāma, was thus speaking, shedding tears of sorrow, Lakṣmaṇa getting angry and hissing like an impeded cobra, said: (22)

verses.text:
अनाथ इव भूतानां नाथस्त्वं वासवोपमः।
मया प्रेष्येण काकुत्स्थ किमर्थं परितप्यसे॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Why are you, the lord of all beings like Indra, with a servant like me, grieving like an orphan, O descendant of Kakutstha? (23)

verses.text:
शरेण निहतस्याद्य मया क्रुद्धेन रक्षसः।
विराधस्य गतासोर्हि मही पास्यति शोणितम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Today, the earth will drink the blood of Virādha, the ogre, losing his life when killed by my angry self with an arrow. (24)

verses.text:
राज्यकामे मम क्रोधो भरते यो बभूव ह।
तं विराधे विमोक्ष्यामि वज्री वज्रमिवाचले॥ २५॥
verses.m: My anger, which was directed against Bharata, having the desire for kingdom, now I shall ventilate against Virādha as did the wielder of the thunderbolt, discharge the thunderbolt against a mountain. (25)

verses.text:
मम भुजबलवेगवेगितः
पततु शरोऽस्य महान् महोरसि।
व्यपनयतु तनोश्च जीवितं
पततु ततश्च महीं विघूर्णितः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Let the great arrow getting impulse from the force exerted by the strength of my arms fall on his huge breast and take away the life from the body and then let him fall down on the earth whirling round.” (26)

verses.text:
अथोवाच पुनर्वाक्यं विराधः पूरयन् वनम्।
पृच्छतो मम हि ब्रूतं कौ युवां क्व गमिष्यथः॥ १॥
verses.m: Then, Virādha again said filling the forest with his voice, “While I am asking you, tell me, who are you two and where will you go?” (1)

verses.text:
तमुवाच ततो रामो राक्षसं ज्वलिताननम्।
पृच्छन्तं सुमहातेजा इक्ष्वाकुकुलमात्मनः॥ २॥
क्षत्रियौ वृत्तसम्पन्नौ विद्धि नौ वनगोचरौ।
त्वां तु वेदितुमिच्छावः कस्त्वं चरसि दण्डकान्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then, Rāma of extraordinary lustre spoke of his own Ikṣwāku dynasty to that demon of flaming mouth, who was inquiring, “Know us two to be Kṣatriyas of character, who have come to the forest. For our part, we want to know you—who are you wandering in the Daṇḍaka forest?” (2-3)

verses.text:
तमुवाच विराधस्तु रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।
हन्त वक्ष्यामि ते राजन् निबोध मम राघव॥ ४॥
verses.m: Virādha for his part said to Rāma of unfailing valour : “Ah ! O king ! I shall tell you. Listen to me, O scion of Raghu ! (4)

verses.text:
पुत्रः किल जवस्याहं माता मम शतह्रदा।
विराध इति मामाहुः पृथिव्यां सर्वराक्षसाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “They say that I am the son of Java; my mother is Śatahradā; all the ogres on earth call me ‘Virādha’. (5)

verses.text:
तपसा चाभिसम्प्राप्ता ब्रह्मणो हि प्रसादजा।
शस्त्रेणावध्यता लोकेऽच्छेद्याभेद्यत्वमेव च॥ ६॥
verses.m: “I have attained, through penance, protection from being killed in the world by a weapon, from being cut or broken, by the grace of Lord Brahmā. (6)

verses.text:
उत्सृज्य प्रमदामेनामनपेक्षौ यथागतम्।
त्वरमाणौ पलायेथां न वां जीवितमाददे॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Run away with haste as you have come, giving up this lady without any expectation; I shall not take your life.” (7)

verses.text:
तं रामः प्रत्युवाचेदं कोपसंरक्तलोचनः।
राक्षसं विकृताकारं विराधं पापचेतसम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Rāma, with his eyes blood-red from anger, replied thus to that ogre, Virādha, of ugly form and sinful mind : (8)

verses.text:
क्षुद्र धिक् त्वां तु हीनार्थं मृत्युमन्वेषसे ध्रुवम्।
रणे प्राप्स्यसि संतिष्ठ न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे॥ ९॥
verses.m: “O petty fellow, fie upon you of vile purpose ! You are certainly seeking death. Wait, you will get it on the battlefield. You will not be left alive by me.” (9)

verses.text:
ततः सज्यं धनुः कृत्वा रामः सुनिशितान् शरान्।
सुशीघ्रमभिसंधाय राक्षसं निजघान ह॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then promptly stringing his bow and fitting very sharp arrows to it, Rāma struck at the ogre. (10)

verses.text:
धनुषा ज्यागुणवता सप्त बाणान् मुमोच ह।
रुक्मपुङ्खान् महावेगान् सुपर्णानिलतुल्यगान्॥ ११॥
verses.m: He discharged, they say, seven arrows with golden feathers, of terrific speed, equal to that of Garuḍa and the wind, with his bow fitted with the string. (11)

verses.text:
ते शरीरं विराधस्य भित्त्वा बर्हिणवाससः।
निपेतुः शोणितादिग्धा धरण्यां पावकोपमाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Decorated with peacock feathers, they pierced the body of Virādha who fell on the earth drenched with blood and looking like fire. (12)

verses.text:
स विद्धो न्यस्य वैदेहीं शूलमुद्यम्य राक्षसः।
अभ्यद्रवत् सुसंक्रुद्धस्तदा रामं सलक्ष्मणम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: When hurt, that ogre put down the princess of the Videha territory and, then, holding up the lance, ran in great fury towards Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. (13)

verses.text:
स विनद्य महानादं शूलं शक्रध्वजोपमम्।
प्रगृह्याशोभत तदा व्यात्तानन इवान्तकः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Making a great roar and holding the lance resembling the banner of Indra, he then appeared like the god of Death with open mouth. (14)

verses.text:
अथ तौ भ्रातरौ दीप्तं शरवर्षं ववर्षतुः।
विराधे राक्षसे तस्मिन् कालान्तकयमोपमे॥ १५॥
verses.m: Then, those two brothers rained a shining shower of arrows on that ogre, Virādha, who looked like the Time-Spirit, death and Yama. (15)

verses.text:
स प्रहस्य महारौद्रः स्थित्वाजृम्भत राक्षसः।
जृम्भमाणस्य ते बाणाः कायान्निष्पेतुराशुगाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: That most terrible ogre laughed, stopped and yawned. While he was yawning, those speedy arrows fell down from his body. (16)

verses.text:
स्पर्शात् तु वरदानेन प्राणान् संरोध्य राक्षसः।
विराधः शूलमुद्यम्य राघवावभ्यधावत॥ १७॥
verses.m: By virtue of the boon, the ogre Virādha held up the vital airs and, lifting up the lance, attacked the two scions of Raghu. (17)

verses.text:
तच्छूलं वज्रसंकाशं गगने ज्वलनोपमम्।
द्वाभ्यां शराभ्यां चिच्छेद रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Rāma, the foremost of warriors, broke with two arrows that lance looking like the thunderbolt and a fire while still in the air.(18)

verses.text:
तद् रामविशिखैश्छिन्नं शूलं तस्यापतद् भुवि।
पपाताशनिना छिन्नं मेरोरिव शिलातलम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: That lance of his, broken by the arrows of Rāma, fell on the earth like the rocky ledge of Mount Meru split by the thunderbolt. (19)

verses.text:
तौ खड्गौ क्षिप्रमुद्यम्य कृष्णसर्पाविवोद्यतौ।
तूर्णमापेततुस्तस्य तदा प्रहरतां बलात्॥ २०॥
verses.m: They two raised their swords like two black snakes getting up, and quickly fell upon him and then struck him with force. (20)

verses.text:
स वध्यमानः सुभृशं भुजाभ्यां परिगृह्य तौ।
अप्रकम्प्यौ नरव्याघ्रौ रौद्रः प्रस्थातुमैच्छत॥ २१॥
verses.m: That terrible one, being violently hurt, took those two unshakable tiger-men by the arms and wanted to move. (21)

verses.text:
तस्याभिप्रायमाज्ञाय रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
वहत्वयमलं तावत् पथानेन तु राक्षसः॥ २२॥
यथा चेच्छति सौमित्रे तथा वहतु राक्षसः।
अयमेव हि नः पन्था येन याति निशाचरः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Reading his mind, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa—“Let this ogre gladly carry us by this way, O son of Sumitrā ! Let the ogre carry us as he will. Indeed this is the path of ours by which the night-wanderer is going.” (22-23)

verses.text:
स तु स्वबलवीर्येण समुत्क्षिप्य निशाचरः।
बालाविव स्कन्धगतौ चकारातिबलोद्धतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: That night-wanderer, for his part, proud of his great strength, lifted them up by dint of his sturdiness and energy like two children and placed them on his shoulders. (24)

verses.text:
तावारोप्य ततः स्कन्धं राघवौ रजनीचरः।
विराधो विनदन् घोरं जगामाभिमुखो वनम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Then placing those two scions of Raghu on his shoulders, that night-wanderer, Virādha, proceeded towards the forest roaring fiercely. (25)

verses.text:
वनं महामेघनिभं प्रविष्टो
द्रुमैर्महद्भिर्विविधैरुपेतम्।
नानाविधैः पक्षिकुलैर्विचित्रं
शिवायुतं व्यालमृगैर्विकीर्णम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: He entered the forest looking like a huge cloud, containing big trees of many species, adorned with flocks of birds of various kinds, having jackals and thronged with beasts of prey. (26)

verses.text:
ह्रियमाणौ तु काकुत्स्थौ दृष्ट्वा सीता रघूत्तमौ।
उच्चैः स्वरेण चुक्रोश प्रगृह्य सुमहाभुजौ॥ १॥
verses.m: Seeing the descendants of Kakutstha, the foremost of Raghu’s race, possessed of very powerful arms, (Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa) being forcibly taken away, Sītā, however, cried in a loud voice : (1)

verses.text:
एष दाशरथी रामः सत्यवाञ्छीलवान् शुचिः।
रक्षसा रौद्ररूपेण ह्रियते सहलक्ष्मणः॥ २॥
verses.m: “This Rāma, son of Daśaratha, truthful, well-behaved and pious, is being taken away together with Lakṣmaṇa by an ogre of terrible form. (2)

verses.text:
मामृक्षा भक्षयिष्यन्ति शार्दूलद्वीपिनस्तथा।
मां हरोत्सृज काकुत्स्थौ नमस्ते राक्षसोत्तम॥ ३॥
verses.m: “O jewel among ogres, hail to you ! Take me away. Bears will eat me up and so will tigers and panthers. Release the descendants of Kakutstha.” (3)

verses.text:
तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा वैदेह्या रामलक्ष्मणौ।
वेगं प्रचक्रतुर्वीरौ वधे तस्य दुरात्मनः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid appeal of that princess of Videha territory, the heroic Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa made haste in killing the wicked ogre. (4)

verses.text:
तस्य रौद्रस्य सौमित्रिः सव्यं बाहुं बभञ्ज ह।
रामस्तु दक्षिणं बाहुं तरसा तस्य रक्षसः॥ ५॥
verses.m: The son of Sumitrā broke the left arm of that terrible one and Rāma for his part the right arm of the said ogre with expedition. (5)

verses.text:
स भग्नबाहुः संविग्नः पपाताशु विमूर्च्छितः।
धरण्यां मेघसंकाशो वज्रभिन्न इवाचलः॥ ६॥
verses.m: He with his arms broken, and frightened fell quickly on the ground in swoon looking like a cloud or a mountain rent asunder by lightning. (6)

verses.text:
मुष्टिभिर्बाहुभिः पद्भिः सूदयन्तौ तु राक्षसम्।
उद्यम्योद्यम्य चाप्येनं स्थण्डिले निष्पिपेषतुः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Those two, while beating the ogre with their fists, arms and kicks, also crushed him on the ground, lifting him again and again. (7)

verses.text:
स विद्धौ बहुभिर्बाणैः खड्गाभ्यां च परिक्षतः।
निष्पिष्टो बहुधा भूमौ न ममार स राक्षसः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Though pierced with many arrows and injured with two swords and crushed several times on the ground, that ogre did not die. (8)

verses.text:
तं प्रेक्ष्य रामः सुभृशमवध्यमचलोपमम्।
भयेष्वभयदः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Seeing him very much incapable of being killed and looking like a mountain, the glorious Rāma, who gave protection in danger, spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa : (9)

verses.text:
तपसा पुरुषव्याघ्र राक्षसोऽयं न शक्यते।
शस्त्रेण युधि निर्जेतुं राक्षसं निखनावहे॥ १०॥
verses.m: “O tiger-man, by virtue of his penance this ogre cannot be conquered in battle with a weapon. We two shall bury him in a pit. (10)

verses.text:
कुञ्जरस्येव रौद्रस्य राक्षसस्यास्य लक्ष्मण।
वनेऽस्मिन् सुमहच्छ्वभ्रं खन्यतां रौद्रवर्चसः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “O Lakṣmaṇa, dig a very big pit in this forest for this terrible ogre of fierce lustre, looking like an elephant.” (11)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा लक्ष्मणं रामः प्रदरः खन्यतामिति।
तस्थौ विराधमाक्रम्य कण्ठे पादेन वीर्यवान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Thus telling Lakṣmaṇa to dig a pit, the valorous Rāma stood stamping his foot on the neck of Virādha. (12)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवेणोक्तं राक्षसः प्रश्रितं वचः।
इदं प्रोवाच काकुत्स्थं विराधः पुरुषर्षभम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Hearing the command given by the scion of Raghu, the ogre Virādha made this polite submission to the descendant of Kakutstha, the best among men : (13)

verses.text:
हतोऽहं पुरुषव्याघ्र शक्रतुल्यबलेन वै।
मया तु पूर्वं त्वं मोहान्न ज्ञातः पुरुषर्षभ॥ १४॥
verses.m: “O tiger-man, I stand killed by you, equal in strength to Indra. However, O jewel among men, earlier due to delusion you were not recognized by me. (14)

verses.text:
कौसल्या सुप्रजास्तात रामस्त्वं विदितो मया।
वैदेही च महाभागा लक्ष्मणश्च महायशाः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “O dear, Kausalyā is possessed of good progeny in you. You are known by me as Rāma, as also the princess of Videha territory, who is very fortunate, and Lakṣmaṇa, who is very well-known. (15)

verses.text:
अभिशापादहं घोरां प्रविष्टो राक्षसीं तनुम्।
तुम्बुरुर्नाम गन्धर्वः शप्तो वैश्रवणेन हि॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Indeed, I am a Gandharva named Tumburu, cursed by Kubera. Due to the curse I entered the fierce form of an ogre. (16)

verses.text:
प्रसाद्यमानश्च मया सोऽब्रवीन्मां महायशाः।
यदा दाशरथी रामस्त्वां वधिष्यति संयुगे॥ १७॥
तदा प्रकृतिमापन्नो भवान् स्वर्गं गमिष्यति।
अनुपस्थीयमानो मां स क्रुद्धो व्याजहार ह॥ १८॥
verses.m: “When requested for grace by me, he, possessed of great fame, said to me, ‘When Rāma, son of Daśaratha, will kill you in battle, then regaining your pristine state you will go to paradise.’ He, not being attended upon by me, angrily addressed me thus. (17-18)

verses.text:
इति वैश्रवणो राजा रम्भासक्तमुवाच ह।
तव प्रसादान्मुक्तोऽहमभिशापात् सुदारुणात्॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘King Kubera spoke thus to me, who was attached to Rambhā. With your grace I stand freed from a very terrible curse. (19)

verses.text:
भुवनं स्वं गमिष्यामि स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु परंतप।
इतो वसति धर्मात्मा शरभङ्गः प्रतापवान्॥ २०॥
अध्यर्धयोजने तात महर्षिः सूर्यसंनिभः।
तं क्षिप्रमभिगच्छ त्वं स ते श्रेयोऽभिधास्यति॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I shall go to my own realm, O tormentor of foes, good luck be to you. There lives the righteous and powerful great sage Śarabhaṅga, effulgent like the sun—just a Yojana and a half from here. Go quickly to him. He will give you good advice. (20-21)

verses.text:
अवटे चापि मां राम निक्षिप्य कुशली व्रज।
रक्षसां गतसत्त्वानामेष धर्मः सनातनः॥ २२॥
अवटे ये निधीयन्ते तेषां लोकाः सनातनाः।
एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थं विराधः शरपीडितः॥ २३॥
बभूव स्वर्गसम्प्राप्तो न्यस्तदेहो महाबलः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं व्यादिदेश ह॥ २४॥
कुञ्जरस्येव रौद्रस्य राक्षसस्यास्य लक्ष्मण।
वनेऽस्मिन्सुमहान् श्वभ्रः खन्यतां रौद्रकर्मणः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Go happily, throwing me into the pit. This is the time-honoured practice for the dead ogres. Eternal worlds exist for them who are interred in a pit.” Thus saying to the descendant of Kakutstha, the mighty Virādha, for his part, being tormented by arrows, left his body and reached heaven. Hearing that speech Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa: “O Lakṣmaṇa, dig a very big pit in this forest for this dreadful ogre of fierce activities like an elephant.” (22—25)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा लक्ष्मणं रामः प्रदरः खन्यतामिति।
तस्थौ विराधमाक्रम्य कण्ठे पादेन वीर्यवान्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Thus telling Lakṣmaṇa to dig a pit, the valorous Rāma stood laying his foot on the neck of Virādha. (26)

verses.text:
ततः खनित्रमादाय लक्ष्मणः श्वभ्रमुत्तमम्।
अखनत् पार्श्वतस्तस्य विराधस्य महात्मनः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Then taking the pick, Lakṣmaṇa dug an excellent pit by the side of that high-souled Virādha. (27)

verses.text:
तं मुक्तकण्ठमुत्क्षिप्य शङ्कुकर्णं महास्वनम्।
विराधं प्राक्षिपच्छ्वभ्रे नदन्तं भैरवस्वनम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Lifting up Virādha, who was possessed of spike-like ears and a sonorous voice, Śrī Rāma threw him into the pit while he was crying in a fearful voice. (28)

verses.text:
तमाहवे दारुणमाशुविक्रमौ
स्थिरावुभौ संयति रामलक्ष्मणौ।
मुदान्वितौ चिक्षिपतुर्भयावहं
नदन्तमुत्क्षिप्य बलेन राक्षसम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Full of joy, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa of quick valour, both firm on the battlefield, threw that fierce, frightening and roaring demon into the pit after lifting him up with force. (29)

verses.text:
अवध्यतां प्रेक्ष्य महासुरस्य तौ
शितेन शस्त्रेण तदा नरर्षभौ।
समर्थ्य चात्यर्थविशारदावुभौ
बिले विराधस्य वधं प्रचक्रतुः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having realized that the great demon could not be killed with a sharp weapon, both those foremost men, highly skilled, then killed Virādha burying him in a pit with full justification. (30)

verses.text:
स्वयं विराधेन हि मृत्युमात्मनः
प्रसह्य रामेण यथार्थमीप्सितः।
निवेदितः काननचारिणा स्वयं
न मे वधः शस्त्रकृतो भवेदिति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: In fact, Virādha himself had desired his own forcible death from Rāma. Hence the forest-wanderer himself said, “My death cannot happen with a weapon.” (31)

verses.text:
तदेव रामेण निशम्य भाषितं
कृता मतिस्तस्य बिलप्रवेशने।
बिलं च तेनातिबलेन रक्षसा
प्रवेश्यमानेन वनं विनादितम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Having heard this very speech, Rāma made up his mind to throw him into a pit and while that mighty ogre was being thrown into the pit he made the forest resound. (32)

verses.text:
प्रहृष्टरूपाविव रामलक्ष्मणौ
विराधमुर्व्यां प्रदरे निपात्य तम्।
ननन्दतुर्वीतभयौ महावने
शिलाभिरन्तर्दधतुश्च राक्षसम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Appearing as though pleased on having thrown that Virādha into a pit in the earth, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa rejoiced in the great forest, their fear being removed, and covered the ogre with rocks. (33)

verses.text:
ततस्तु तौ काञ्चनचित्रकार्मुकौ
निहत्य रक्षः परिगृह्य मैथिलीम्।
विजह्रतुस्तौ मुदितौ महावने
दिवि स्थितौ चन्द्रदिवाकराविव॥ ३४॥
verses.m: And then, having killed the ogre and received Maithilī, those two princes, possessed of lovely golden bows, happily moved about in the great forest, like the moon and the sun in the sky. (34)

verses.text:
हत्वा तु तं भीमबलं विराधं राक्षसं वने।
ततः सीतां परिष्वज्य समाश्वास्य च वीर्यवान्॥ १॥
अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं रामो लक्ष्मणं दीप्ततेजसम्।
कष्टं वनमिदं दुर्गं न च स्मो वनगोचराः॥ २॥
verses.m: Killing in the forest that ogre Virādha of terrible might and then embracing and consoling Sītā, the heroic Rāma spoke to brother Lakṣmaṇa of shining lustre—“This is a very dangerous forest, difficult of access, and we are not accustomed to it. (1-2)

verses.text:
अभिगच्छामहे शीघ्रं शरभङ्गं तपोधनम्।
आश्रमं शरभङ्गस्य राघवोऽभिजगाम ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: “We will quickly visit the ascetic Śarabhaṅga.” Rāghava then went towards the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga. (3)

verses.text:
तस्य देवप्रभावस्य तपसा भावितात्मनः।
समीपे शरभङ्गस्य ददर्श महदद्भुतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: In the vicinity of the said Śarabhaṅga, possessing divine power and purified with penance, he saw a great wonder. (4)

verses.text:
विभ्राजमानं वपुषा सूर्यवैश्वानरप्रभम्।
रथप्रवरमारूढमाकाशे विबुधानुगम्॥ ५॥
असंस्पृशन्तं वसुधां ददर्श विबुधेश्वरम्।
सम्प्रभाभरणं देवं विरजोऽम्बरधारिणम्॥ ६॥
तद्विधैरेव बहुभिः पूज्यमानं महात्मभिः।
हरितैर्वाजिभिर्युक्तमन्तरिक्षगतं रथम्॥ ७॥
ददर्शादूरतस्तस्य तरुणादित्यसंनिभम्।
पाण्डुराभ्रघनप्रख्यं चन्द्रमण्डलसंनिभम्॥ ८॥
अपश्यद् विमलं छत्रं चित्रमाल्योपशोभितम्।
चामरव्यजने चाग्र्ये रुक्मदण्डे महाधने॥ ९॥
गृहीते वरनारीभ्यां धूयमाने च मूर्धनि।
गन्धर्वामरसिद्धाश्च बहवः परमर्षयः॥ १०॥
अन्तरिक्षगतं देवं गीर्भिरग्र्याभिरैडयन्।
सह सम्भाषमाणे तु शरभङ्गेन वासवे॥ ११॥
verses.m: He saw the lord of the gods, shining with his body, possessing a lustre like the sun and the fire, seated in a fine chariot in the sky not touching the earth, followed by gods, wearing shining ornaments and clean garments, being worshipped by many high-souled beings of the same type. Not far from him, he saw a chariot in the sky drawn by green horses, looking like the midday sun. He saw an immaculate canopy resembling a white cloud and possessing the lustre of the orb of the moon and decorated with magnificent garlands. He also saw excellent and very precious whisks having gold handles, held by two beautiful women and being waved over the head. Gandharvas, gods, Siddhas and many great sages praised the god in the sky with excellent verses, while Indra was conversing with Śarabhaṅga. (5—11)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा शतक्रतुं तत्र रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
रामोऽथ रथमुद्दिश्य भ्रातुर्दर्शयताद्भुतम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Seeing Indra there, Rāma addressed Lakṣmaṇa and then pointing to the chariot showed the wonder to his brother. (12)

verses.text:
अर्चिष्मन्तं श्रिया जुष्टमद्भुतं पश्य लक्ष्मण।
प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यमन्तरिक्षगतं रथम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “O Lakṣmaṇa, see in the sky the wonderful chariot possessed of lustre, attended by grandeur and glowing like the sun. (13)

verses.text:
ये हयाः पुरुहूतस्य पुरा शक्रस्य नः श्रुताः।
अन्तरिक्षगता दिव्यास्त इमे हरयो ध्रुवम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Indeed, here in the sky are those celestial horses of Indra—the horses of which we had heard so much earlier. (14)

verses.text:
इमे च पुरुषव्याघ्र ये तिष्ठन्त्यभितो दिशम्।
शतं शतं कुण्डलिनो युवानः खड्गपाणयः॥ १५॥
विस्तीर्णविपुलोरस्काः परिघायतबाहवः।
शोणांशुवसनाः सर्वे व्याघ्रा इव दुरासदाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “And O tiger-man, those who are standing all round in groups of hundreds—youngmen wearing earrings, holding swords in their hands, having very broad chests and large arms resembling iron clubs and wearing red garments—all are unassailable like tigers. (15-16)

verses.text:
उरोदेशेषु सर्वेषां हारा ज्वलनसंनिभाः।
रूपं बिभ्रति सौमित्रे पञ्चविंशतिवार्षिकम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “At the breast-regions of all hang garlands bright as fire. O son of Sumitrā, all are possessed of a form aged twenty-five years. (17)

verses.text:
एतद्धि किल देवानां वयो भवति नित्यदा।
यथेमे पुरुषव्याघ्रा दृश्यन्ते प्रियदर्शनाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Indeed, they say this is the permanent age of gods, as these tiger-men of agreeable looks appear. (18)

verses.text:
इहैव सह वैदेह्या मुहूर्तं तिष्ठ लक्ष्मण।
यावज्जानाम्यहं व्यक्तं क एष द्युतिमान् रथे॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Lakṣmaṇa, stay here only awhile with Vaidehī till I find out clearly who this lustrous being in the chariot is.” (19)

verses.text:
तमेवमुक्त्वा सौमित्रिमिहैव स्थीयतामिति।
अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थः शरभङ्गाश्रमं प्रति॥ २०॥
verses.m: Thus telling the said Saumitri to stay there only, Kākutstha walked towards the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga. (20)

verses.text:
ततः समभिगच्छन्तं प्रेक्ष्य रामं शचीपतिः।
शरभङ्गमनुज्ञाप्य विबुधानिदमब्रवीत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Then, seeing Rāma coming near, the husband of Śacī, Indra, took leave of Śarabhaṅga and said this to the gods: (21)

verses.text:
इहोपयात्यसौ रामो यावन्मां नाभिभाषते।
निष्ठां नयत तावत् तु ततो मां द्रष्टुमर्हति॥ २२॥
जितवन्तं कृतार्थं हि तदाहमचिरादिमम्।
कर्म ह्यनेन कर्तव्यं महदन्यैः सुदुष्करम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Here comes this Rāma; before he speaks to me, make a move, let him not see me. Shortly when he has conquered Rāvaṇa and achieved his purpose, then I shall see him. For, he has to do a great deed which is very difficult to be done by others.” (22-23)

verses.text:
अथ वज्री तमामन्त्र्य मानयित्वा च तापसम्।
रथेन हययुक्तेन ययौ दिवमरिंदमः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Then having taken leave of and having honoured that ascetic, the wielder of the thunderbolt, a subduer of enemies, rose to heaven in his chariot drawn by horses. (24)

verses.text:
प्रयाते तु सहस्राक्षे राघवः सपरिच्छदः।
अग्निहोत्रमुपासीनं शरभङ्गमुपागमत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: When, however, the thousand-eyed one had left, Rāghava together with his followers approached Śarabhaṅga, who was worshipping the fire. (25)

verses.text:
तस्य पादौ च संगृह्य रामः सीता च लक्ष्मणः।
निषेदुस्तदनुज्ञाता लब्धवासा निमन्त्रिताः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa touched his feet and sat down with his permission. He invited them to be his guests and gave them rooms to stay. (26)

verses.text:
ततः शक्रोपयानं तु पर्यपृच्छत्स राघवः।
शरभङ्गश्च तत् सर्वं राघवाय न्यवेदयत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Then Rāma, for his part, asked the purpose of Indra’s visit and Śarabhaṅga related the whole thing to Rāghava. (27)

verses.text:
मामेष वरदो राम ब्रह्मलोकं निनीषति।
जितमुग्रेण तपसा दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “This bestower of boons, Indra, O Rāma, desires to take me to Brahmaloka, which has been won by me through severe penance and which is difficult to be attained by those who are not self-controlled. (28)

verses.text:
अहं ज्ञात्वा नरव्याघ्र वर्तमानमदूरतः।
ब्रह्मलोकं न गच्छामि त्वामदृष्ट्वा प्रियातिथिम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “O tiger-man, I, having known you to be present nearby, decided not to go to Brahmaloka without seeing you, my beloved guest. (29)

verses.text:
त्वयाहं पुरुषव्याघ्र धार्मिकेण महात्मना।
समागम्य गमिष्यामि त्रिदिवं चावरं परम्॥ ३०॥
अक्षया नरशार्दूल जिता लोका मया शुभाः।
ब्राह्म्याश्च नाकपृष्ठ्याश्च प्रतिगृह्णीष्व मामकान्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Having had a meeting with you, a high-souled prince of righteous nature, I shall go to the lower heaven and then to the higher. I have won, O tiger-man, auspicious and unending worlds—heavenly and those of Lord Brahmā; please accept all these my worlds.” (30-31)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो नरव्याघ्रः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः।
ऋषिणा शरभङ्गेन राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: When thus spoken to by Sage Śarabhaṅga, the tiger-man, Rāma, well-versed in all sciences—replied as follows: (32)

verses.text:
अहमेवाहरिष्यामि सर्वाल्ँलोकान् महामुने।
आवासं त्वहमिच्छामि प्रदिष्टमिह कानने॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “O great sage, I shall myself bring all the worlds to you. However, I desire that a place of abode be pointed out to me in this forest.” (33)

verses.text:
राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु शक्रतुल्यबलेन वै।
शरभङ्गो महाप्राज्ञः पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वचः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Thus addressed by Rāghava, equal in might to Indra, the very wise Śarabhaṅga once again uttered the following words :(34)

verses.text:
इह राम महातेजाः सुतीक्ष्णो नाम धार्मिकः।
वसत्यरण्ये नियतः स ते श्रेयो विधास्यति॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Rāma, here in the forest dwells a righteous and self-restrained sage, named Sutīkṣṇa, possessed of great lustre. He will do you good. (35)

verses.text:
सुतीक्ष्णमभिगच्छ त्वं शुचौ देशे तपस्विनम्।
रमणीये वनोद्देशे स ते वासं विधास्यति॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Approach you the ascetic Sutīkṣṇa in that pious region. He will arrange for your residence in a charming region of the forest. (36)

verses.text:
इमां मन्दाकिनीं राम प्रतिस्रोतामनुव्रज।
नदीं पुष्पोडुपवहां ततस्तत्र गमिष्यसि॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Rāma, follow against the current this river Mandākinī carrying boats of flowers; then you will reach there. (37)

verses.text:
एष पन्था नरव्याघ्र मुहूर्तं पश्य तात माम्।
यावज्जहामि गात्राणि जीर्णां त्वचमिवोरगः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “This is the path, O tiger-man ! Dear, look at me for a while as I shed the old and worn-out limbs, just as a serpent casts off its slough.” (38)

verses.text:
ततोऽग्निं स समाधाय हुत्वा चाज्येन मन्त्रवत्।
शरभङ्गो महातेजाः प्रविवेश हुताशनम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Then, kindling the fire and pouring oblations of ghee with chants, that Śarabhaṅga of great lustre entered the fire. (39)

verses.text:
तस्य रोमाणि केशांश्च तदा वह्निर्महात्मनः।
जीर्णां त्वचं तदस्थीनि यच्च मांसं च शोणितम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Presently the fire burnt the hair on the body and head, old skin and bones and whatever flesh and blood that great soul had. (40)

verses.text:
स च पावकसंकाशः कुमारः समपद्यत।
उत्थायाग्निचयात् तस्माच्छरभङ्गो व्यरोचत॥ ४१॥
verses.m: And he appeared as a boy glowing like fire. Rising from that heap of fire, Śarabhaṅga shone bright. (41)

verses.text:
स लोकानाहिताग्नीनामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्।
देवानां च व्यतिक्रम्य ब्रह्मलोकं व्यरोहत॥ ४२॥
verses.m: He crossed the worlds of fire-worshippers, high-souled sages and gods and rose to the Brahmaloka. (42)

verses.text:
स पुण्यकर्मा भुवने द्विजर्षभः
पितामहं सानुचरं ददर्श ह।
पितामहश्चापि समीक्ष्य तं द्विजं
ननन्द सुस्वागतमित्युवाच ह॥ ४३॥
verses.m: That meritorious jewel among the twice-born, Śarabhaṅga, in the world saw the grandfather, Brahmā, with his attendants; the grandfather also was delighted to see that Brāhmaṇa and said “You are fully welcome.” (43)

verses.text:
शरभङ्गे दिवं प्राप्ते मुनिसङ्घाः समागताः।
अभ्यगच्छन्त काकुत्स्थं रामं ज्वलिततेजसम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Śarabhaṅga having risen to heaven, the hosts of sages assembled there approached Kākutstha Rāma of burning lustre. (1)

verses.text:
वैखानसा वालखिल्याः सम्प्रक्षाला मरीचिपाः।
अश्मकुट्टाश्च बहवः पत्राहाराश्च तापसाः॥ २॥
दन्तोलूखलिनश्चैव तथैवोन्मज्जकाः परे।
गात्रशय्या अशय्याश्च तथैवानवकाशिकाः॥ ३॥
मुनयः सलिलाहारा वायुभक्षास्तथापरे।
आकाशनिलयाश्चैव तथा स्थण्डिलशायिनः॥ ४॥
तथोर्ध्ववासिनो दान्तास्तथाऽऽर्द्रपटवाससः।
सजपाश्च तपोनिष्ठास्तथा पञ्चतपोऽन्विताः॥ ५॥
सर्वे ब्राह्म्या श्रिया युक्ता दृढयोगसमाहिताः।
शरभङ्गाश्रमे राममभिजग्मुश्च तापसाः॥ ६॥
verses.m: The Vaikhānasas (a class of ascetics born of the nails of Brahmā), the Vālakhilyas (another class of sages born of Brahmā’s hair), sages who washed the utensils after their meals (keeping nothing for another time), those who lived on the sun’s or moon’s rays, those who powdered grains by stones, many ascetics living on leaves, those using teeth as the mortar and pestle, others doing penance in neck-deep water, those using limbs of the body alone for bed, those without bed, those enjoying no respite from their religious observances, sages living on water alone, others on air alone, those having sky as the only roof, those sleeping on the alter, those dwelling on high altitudes, those who controlled their senses, those who used to wear wet clothes, those doing Japa, those devoted to penance, those doing the penance of sitting in the middle of four fires, with the sun (the fifth) overhead, all possessed of Brahmic lustre, and with their mind concentrated through steadfast practice of yoga—these ascetics approached Rāma in the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga. (2—6)

verses.text:
अभिगम्य च धर्मज्ञा रामं धर्मभृतां वरम्।
ऊचुः परमधर्मज्ञमृषिसङ्घाः समागताः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Having approached him, the assembled hosts of sages—the knowers of Dharma—said to Rāma, the best amongst the upholders of Dharma and the supreme knower of Dharma : (7)

verses.text:
त्वमिक्ष्वाकुकुलस्यास्य पृथिव्याश्च महारथः।
प्रधानश्चापि नाथश्च देवानां मघवानिव॥ ८॥
verses.m: “You are a great car-warrior and the principal personality and master of this Ikṣwāku dynasty as well as of the earth, as Indra is of gods. (8)

verses.text:
विश्रुतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु यशसा विक्रमेण च।
पितृव्रतत्वं सत्यं च त्वयि धर्मश्च पुष्कलः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “You are well-known in the three worlds by virtue of your fame and valour. In you abide filial devotion, truth and abundant virtue. (9)

verses.text:
त्वामासाद्य महात्मानं धर्मज्ञं धर्मवत्सलम्।
अर्थित्वान्नाथ वक्ष्यामस्तच्च नः क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Having met you, the magnanimous knower of Dharma and lover of righteousness, we shall speak like a petitioner. You may please forgive us for this encroachment, O lord ! (10)

verses.text:
अधर्मः सुमहान् नाथ भवेत् तस्य तु भूपतेः।
यो हरेद् बलिषड्भागं न च रक्षति पुत्रवत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “It would be a great Adharma (failure in duty), O master, on the part of that king who would just take away the sixth part by way of land revenue and not protect his subjects like his own children. (11)

verses.text:
युञ्जानः स्वानिव प्राणान् प्राणैरिष्टान् सुतानिव।
नित्ययुक्तः सदा रक्षन् सर्वान् विषयवासिनः॥ १२॥
प्राप्नोति शाश्वतीं राम कीर्तिं स बहुवार्षिकीम्।
ब्रह्मणः स्थानमासाद्य तत्र चापि महीयते॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Always attentively protecting all the people dwelling within the kingdom like his own life or like the sons who are dearer than life, keeping himself engaged, he attains, O Rāma, continuous fame lasting for many years and, having reached the realm of Brahmā, is honoured even there. (12-13)

verses.text:
यत् करोति परं धर्मं मुनिर्मूलफलाशनः।
तत्र राज्ञश्चतुर्भागः प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षतः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Whatever great Dharma a sage living on roots and fruits does, the fourth part of it goes to the king, who protects the people with Dharma. (14)

verses.text:
सोऽयं ब्राह्मणभूयिष्ठो वानप्रस्थगणो महान्।
त्वन्नाथोऽनाथवद् राम राक्षसैर्हन्यते भृशम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “This great multitude of forest-dwellers, mainly consisting of Brāhmaṇas and having you as their master, O Rāma, is being killed like the forlorn in large numbers by the ogres. (15)

verses.text:
एहि पश्य शरीराणि मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्।
हतानां राक्षसैर्घोरैर्बहूनां बहुधा वने॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Come, see the bodies of many pure minded sages killed by the terrible ogres in several ways in the forest. (16)

verses.text:
पम्पानदीनिवासानामनुमन्दाकिनीमपि।
चित्रकूटालयानां च क्रियते कदनं महत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “A great destruction is being wrought of the sages living along the Pampā river, and by the side of Mandākinī and also of those having their residence on Citrakūṭa. (17)

verses.text:
एवं वयं न मृष्यामो विप्रकारं तपस्विनाम्।
क्रियमाणं वने घोरं रक्षोभिर्भीमकर्मभिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Thus we cannot brook the awful persecution to which ascetics in the forest are being subjected by the ogres of fierce activities. (18)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वां शरणार्थं च शरण्यं समुपस्थिताः।
परिपालय नो राम वध्यमानान् निशाचरैः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Hence we have come to you, who are a fit resort, for protection. Rāma, protect us; we are being killed by the ogres, the night-stalkers. (19)

verses.text:
परा त्वत्तो गतिर्वीर पृथिव्यां नोपपद्यते।
परिपालय नः सर्वान् राक्षसेभ्यो नृपात्मज॥ २०॥
verses.m: “O brave prince, there can be no better help on earth than you. Protect us all from the ogres.” (20)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु काकुत्स्थस्तापसानां तपस्विनाम्।
इदं प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा सर्वानेव तपस्विनः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Hearing this from the ascetic sages, the righteous Kākutstha for his part addressed all the ascetics as follows: (21)

verses.text:
नैवमर्हथ मां वक्तुमाज्ञाप्योऽहं तपस्विनाम्।
केवलेन स्वकार्येण प्रवेष्टव्यं वनं मया॥ २२॥
विप्रकारमपाक्रष्टुं राक्षसैर्भवतामिमम्।
पितुस्तु निर्देशकरः प्रविष्टोऽहमिदं वनम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “You should not pray to me thus. I am at the service of the ascetics. I have to enter the forest not only for my own business, it is to stop this persecution of yours by the ogres that I have entered this forest in obedience to the command of my father. (22-23)

verses.text:
भवतामर्थसिद्ध्यर्थमागतोऽहं यदृच्छया।
तस्य मेऽयं वने वासो भविष्यति महाफलः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “By chance, I have come here to achieve your purpose. Thus getting the opportunity, this stay of mine in the forest is going to yield great results. (24)

verses.text:
तपस्विनां रणे शत्रून् हन्तुमिच्छामि राक्षसान्।
पश्यन्तु वीर्यमृषयः सभ्रातुर्मे तपोधनाः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “I desire to kill ogres, the enemies of ascetics, on the battlefield. Let the ascetic sages see my valour together with my brother’s.” (25)

verses.text:
दत्त्वा वरं चापि तपोधनानां
धर्मे धृतात्मा सह लक्ष्मणेन।
तपोधनैश्चापि सहार्यदत्तः
सुतीक्ष्णमेवाभिजगाम वीरः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Giving an assurance to the ascetics, the righteous-minded hero, Śrī Rāma, the bestower of noble gifts, proceeded towards Sutīkṣṇa alone, together with Lakṣmaṇa (and Sītā) as well as with all the ascetics. (26)

verses.text:
रामस्तु सहितो भ्रात्रा सीतया च परंतपः।
सुतीक्ष्णस्याश्रमपदं जगाम सह तैर्द्विजैः॥ १॥
verses.m: Rāma, the tormentor of foes, together with his brother and Sītā and also with the Brāhmaṇas, went to the site of Sutīkṣṇa’s hermitage. (1)

verses.text:
स गत्वा दूरमध्वानं नदीस्तीर्त्वा बहूदकाः।
ददर्श विमलं शैलं महामेरुमिवोन्नतम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Going a long distance and crossing the rivers of deep waters he saw a bright mountain, high like the great Meru. (2)

verses.text:
ततस्तदिक्ष्वाकुवरौ सततं विविधैर्द्रुमैः।
काननं तौ विविशतुः सीतया सह राघवौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then those two Rāghavas, the best amongst the Ikṣwākus, together with Sītā, entered that forest full of a variety of trees.(3)

verses.text:
प्रविष्टस्तु वनं घोरं बहुपुष्पफलद्रुमम्।
ददर्शाश्रममेकान्ते चीरमालापरिष्कृतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having entered the fearful forest having trees laden with flowers and fruits, he saw in one corner a hermitage decorated with bark-garments and garlands. (4)

verses.text:
तत्र तापसमासीनं मलपङ्कजधारिणम्।
रामः सुतीक्ष्णं विधिवत् तपोधनमभाषत॥ ५॥
verses.m: Rāma spoke with due decorum to the ascetic, Sage Sutīkṣṇa, sitting there in the posture of Padmāsana for purification : (5)

verses.text:
रामोऽहमस्मि भगवन् भवन्तं द्रष्टुमागतः।
तन्माभिवद धर्मज्ञ महर्षे सत्यविक्रम॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Sir, I am Rāma, come to see you. Hence, O knower of Dharma, great sage of true spiritual might, please speak to me.” (6)

verses.text:
स निरीक्ष्य ततो धीरो रामं धर्मभृतां वरम्।
समाश्लिष्य च बाहुभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: That wise seer then saw Rāma, the best amongst the upholders of Dharma, folded him in his arms and addressed to him the following words : (7)

verses.text:
स्वागतं ते रघुश्रेष्ठ राम सत्यभृतां वर।
आश्रमोऽयं त्वयाऽऽक्रान्तः सनाथ इव साम्प्रतम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Welcome to you, O Rāma, the foremost amongst the Raghus, the best amongst the upholders of truth. With your arrival this hermitage has now found its master, as it were. (8)

verses.text:
प्रतीक्षमाणस्त्वामेव नारोहेऽहं महायशः।
देवलोकमितो वीर देहं त्यक्त्वा महीतले॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Awaiting you only, I am not ascending to the realm of gods from here, abandoning the body on the surface of the earth, O highly illustrious hero ! (9)

verses.text:
चित्रकूटमुपादाय राज्यभ्रष्टोऽसि मे श्रुतः।
इहोपयातः काकुत्स्थ देवराजः शतक्रतुः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “O Kākutstha, Indra, the king of gods, had come here. I have heard that abandoning the kingdom you have come over to Citrakūṭa. (10)

verses.text:
उपागम्य च मे देवो महादेवः सुरेश्वरः।
सर्वाल्ँलोकाञ्जितानाह मम पुण्येन कर्मणा॥ ११॥
तेषु देवर्षिजुष्टेषु जितेषु तपसा मया।
मत्प्रसादात् सभार्यस्त्वं विहरस्व सलक्ष्मणः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Coming to me, Indra, the great god, the king of gods, told me that I have won all the higher worlds through meritorious action. I urge you that, you may please rejoice in those worlds inhabited by divine sages, won by me, together with your wife and Lakṣmaṇa.” (11-12)

verses.text:
तमुग्रतपसं दीप्तं महर्षिं सत्यवादिनम्।
प्रत्युवाचात्मवान् रामो ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः॥ १३॥
verses.m: The self-restrained Rāma replied to that great resplendent sage of austere penance, who had taken a vow to speak the truth, as Indra does to Brahmā : (13)

verses.text:
अहमेवाहरिष्यामि स्वयं लोकान् महामुने।
आवासं त्वहमिच्छामि प्रदिष्टमिह कानने॥ १४॥
verses.m: “O great sage, I shall myself bring all the worlds within your reach. However, at this moment, I desire that a place for my abode in this forest be pointed out to me.(14)

verses.text:
भवान् सर्वत्र कुशलः सर्वभूतहिते रतः।
आख्यातं शरभङ्गेन गौतमेन महात्मना॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The high-souled Śarabhaṅga of Gautama family told me that you are well-versed in all sciences and devoted to the good of all creatures.” (15)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण महर्षिर्लोकविश्रुतः।
अब्रवीन्मधुरं वाक्यं हर्षेण महता युतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Thus addressed by Rāma, the great sage, well-known in the world, uttered the following sweet words with great delight : (16)

verses.text:
अयमेवाश्रमो राम गुणवान् रम्यतामिति।
ऋषिसंघानुचरितः सदा मूलफलैर्युतः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Rāma, this very hermitage, frequented by multitudes of sages and always abounding in roots and fruits, is comfortable; you may please stay happily here. (17)

verses.text:
इममाश्रममागम्य मृगसंघा महीयसः।
अहत्वा प्रतिगच्छन्ति लोभयित्वाकुतोभयाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Coming to this hermitage, large herds of deer roam everywhere; they return without harming anyone and having lured everyone with their beauty. (18)

verses.text:
नान्यो दोषो भवेदत्र मृगेभ्योऽन्यत्र विद्धि वै।
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य महर्षेर्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः॥ १९॥
उवाच वचनं धीरो विगृह्य सशरं धनुः।
तानहं सुमहाभाग मृगसंघान् समागतान्॥ २०॥
हन्यां निशितधारेण शरेणानतपर्वणा।
भवांस्तत्राभिषज्येत किं स्यात् कृच्छ्रतरं ततः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Rest assured that there will be no disturbance here except that from the frolicking deer.” Hearing that speech of the great sage, the valiant elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa uttered the following words picking up the bow with arrow: “O highly fortunate sage, if perchance I happen to kill those herds of deer collected here with an arrow of sharp edge, bent at the joint, you will be insulted thereby; what could be more painful than that? (19—21)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नाश्रमे वासं चिरं तु न समर्थये।
तमेवमुक्त्वोपरमं रामः संध्यामुपागमत्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Hence I don’t favour a long stay in this hermitage.” Saying thus to him, Rāma stopped short and left for the evening worship. (22)

verses.text:
अन्वास्य पश्चिमां संध्यां तत्र वासमकल्पयत्।
सुतीक्ष्णस्याश्रमे रम्ये सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च॥ २३॥
verses.m: Having performed the evening worship, he took up his abode there in the charming hermitage of Sutīkṣṇa, together with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa. (23)

verses.text:
ततः शुभं तापसयोग्यमन्नं
स्वयं सुतीक्ष्णः पुरुषर्षभाभ्याम्।
ताभ्यां सुसत्कृत्य ददौ महात्मा
संध्यानिवृत्तौ रजनीं समीक्ष्य॥ २४॥
verses.m: Then at the close of evening, seeing the nightfall, the high-souled Sutīkṣṇa himself honoured those jewels among men and offered them pious food fit for ascetics. (24)

verses.text:
रामस्तु सहसौमित्रिः सुतीक्ष्णेनाभिपूजितः।
परिणाम्य निशां तत्र प्रभाते प्रत्यबुध्यत॥ १॥
verses.m: Honoured by Sutīkṣṇa, Rāma for his part together with Lakṣmaṇa passed the night there and got up in the morning. (1)

verses.text:
उत्थाय च यथाकालं राघवः सह सीतया।
उपस्पृश्य सुशीतेन तोयेनोत्पलगन्धिना॥ २॥
verses.m: Getting up at the proper time, Rāma together with Sītā bathed in pleasantly cold water fragrant with the scent of lotuses. (2)

verses.text:
अथ तेऽग्निं सुरांश्चैव वैदेही रामलक्ष्मणौ।
काल्यं विधिवदभ्यर्च्य तपस्विशरणे वने॥ ३॥
उदयन्तं दिनकरं दृष्ट्वा विगतकल्मषाः।
सुतीक्ष्णमभिगम्येदं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रुवन्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Then they—Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā—who were free from sins, worshipped in time the fire and other gods according to the rites, in the forest resorted to by ascetics and, having seen the rising sun and going to Sutīkṣṇa, uttered the following sweet words: (3-4)

verses.text:
सुखोषिताः स्म भगवंस्त्वया पूज्येन पूजिताः।
आपृच्छामः प्रयास्यामो मुनयस्त्वरयन्ति नः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Sir, happily have we stayed, honoured by Your Holiness. We now take leave of you and shall depart. The sages are hastening us. (5)

verses.text:
त्वरामहे वयं द्रष्टुं कृत्स्नमाश्रममण्डलम्।
ऋषीणां पुण्यशीलानां दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “We shall hasten to see the whole circle of hermitages of the sages of meritorious deeds, staying in the Daṇḍaka forest. (6)

verses.text:
अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामः सहैभिर्मुनिपुंगवैः।
धर्मनित्यैस्तपोदान्तैर्विशिखैरिव पावकैः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “We desire to take leave of you together with these jewels among foremost sages, always persistent in virtue and self-restraint through penance, looking like a fire without smoke. (7)

verses.text:
अविषह्यातपो यावत् सूर्यो नातिविराजते।
अमार्गेणागतां लक्ष्मीं प्राप्येवान्वयवर्जितः॥ ८॥
तावदिच्छामहे गन्तुमित्युक्त्वा चरणौ मुनेः।
ववन्दे सहसौमित्रिः सीतया सह राघवः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Before the sun starts shining brightly with unbearable heat, just as a man from a low family becomes unbearable after getting wealth earned through unfair means, we desire to go.” Saying this, Rāghava bowed down at the feet of the sage, together with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā. (8-9)

verses.text:
तौ संस्पृशन्तौ चरणावुत्थाप्य मुनिपुंगवः।
गाढमाश्लिष्य सस्नेहमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: The great sage lifted the two princes touching his feet and, closely embracing them, uttered these affectionate words : (10)

verses.text:
अरिष्टं गच्छ पन्थानं राम सौमित्रिणा सह।
सीतया चानया सार्धं छाययेवानुवृत्तया॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Rāma, proceed on your journey devoid of any danger together with the son of Sumitrā and with Sītā, who is following you like a shadow. (11)

verses.text:
पश्याश्रमपदं रम्यं दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्।
एषां तपस्विनां वीर तपसा भावितात्मनाम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “O hero, see the charming site of the hermitages of these ascetics, dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, their soul purified with penance. (12)

verses.text:
सुप्राज्यफलमूलानि पुष्पितानि वनानि च।
प्रशस्तमृगयूथानि शान्तपक्षिगणानि च॥ १३॥
फुल्लपङ्कजखण्डानि प्रसन्नसलिलानि च।
कारण्डवविकीर्णानि तटाकानि सरांसि च॥ १४॥
द्रक्ष्यसे दृष्टिरम्याणि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च।
रमणीयान्यरण्यानि मयूराभिरुतानि च॥ १५॥
verses.m: “You will see beautiful forests abounding in fruits and roots and full of flowers with excellent herds of deer and peaceful flocks of birds, lakes and ponds containing cluster of blossoming lotuses with crystal waters and thronged with water-fowls, springs on mountains, charming to the eye, and beautiful forests resounding with the noise of peacocks. (13—15)

verses.text:
गम्यतां वत्स सौमित्रे भवानपि च गच्छतु।
आगन्तव्यं च ते दृष्ट्वा पुनरेवाश्रमं प्रति॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Go, dear Rāma; you too may go, O son of Sumitrā ! You should come back to this very hermitage after seeing these things.” (16)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा काकुत्स्थः सहलक्ष्मणः।
प्रदक्षिणं मुनिं कृत्वा प्रस्थातुमुपचक्रमे॥ १७॥
verses.m: Thus addressed, Kākutstha, together with Lakṣmaṇa, said, “So be it !” and going round the sage keeping him to the right, started on his journey. (17)

verses.text:
ततः शुभतरे तूणी धनुषी चायतेक्षणा।
ददौ सीता तयोर्भ्रात्रोः खड्गौ च विमलौ ततः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Then Sītā, possessed of large eyes, handed to those two brothers highly superb quivers, bows and polished swords. (18)

verses.text:
आबध्य च शुभे तूणी चापे चादाय सस्वने।
निष्क्रान्तावाश्रमाद् गन्तुमुभौ तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: Both of them, Rāma as well as Lakṣmaṇa, fastened the beautiful quivers, took with a twang the bows and left the hermitage for proceeding on their journey. (19)

verses.text:
शीघ्रं तौ रूपसम्पन्नावनुज्ञातौ महर्षिणा।
प्रस्थितौ धृतचापासी सीतया सह राघवौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: Permitted by the great sage and holding the bows and the swords, the two handsome Rāghavas started with Sītā. (20)

verses.text:
सुतीक्ष्णेनाभ्यनुज्ञातं प्रस्थितं रघुनन्दनम्।
हृद्यया स्निग्धया वाचा भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Sītā spoke thus to her husband, the delight of Raghu, who had left with the permission of Sutīkṣṇa, in the following charming and loving words : (1)

verses.text:
अधर्मं तु सुसूक्ष्मेण विधिना प्राप्यते महान्।
निवृत्तेन च शक्योऽयं व्यसनात् कामजादिह॥ २॥
त्रीण्येव व्यसनान्यत्र कामजानि भवन्त्युत।
मिथ्यावाक्यं तु परमं तस्माद् गुरुतरावुभौ॥ ३॥
परदाराभिगमनं विना वैरं च रौद्रता।
मिथ्यावाक्यं न ते भूतं न भविष्यति राघव॥ ४॥
verses.m: “In a very subtle way, a great man is led to ‘Adharma’. If one keeps away from addictions born of desire, it can be avoided in this world. Indeed, the addiction born of desire in this world are only three in number: False speech is extremely bad; the other two are even worse than that—copulation with the wife of another and cruelty without enmity. A false statement you have never made nor will you ever make, O Rāghava ! (2—4)

verses.text:
कुतोऽभिलषणं स्त्रीणां परेषां धर्मनाशनम्।
तव नास्ति मनुष्येन्द्र न चाभूत् ते कदाचन॥ ५॥
verses.m: “O ruler of men, how can there spring up in you the desire for others’ wives, that destroys Dharma? You have not got it, nor was it ever with you. (5)

verses.text:
मनस्यपि तथा राम न चैतद् विद्यते क्वचित्।
स्वदारनिरतश्चैव नित्यमेव नृपात्मज॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Rāma, nowhere is it even in your mind. And you are always devoted to your own wife, O prince ! (6)

verses.text:
धर्मिष्ठः सत्यसंधश्च पितुर्निर्देशकारकः।
त्वयि धर्मश्च सत्यं च त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Dharma and Truth—everything is well-established in you. You are the best observer of Dharma and true to your promise and obedient to your father. (7)

verses.text:
तच्च सर्वं महाबाहो शक्यं वोढुं जितेन्द्रियैः।
तव वश्येन्द्रियत्वं च जानामि शुभदर्शन॥ ८॥
verses.m: “All these, O mighty-armed one, can be cherished by those who have conquered the senses; I know your control over the senses, O handsome prince ! (8)

verses.text:
तृतीयं यदिदं रौद्रं परप्राणाभिहिंसनम्।
निर्वैरं क्रियते मोहात् तच्च ते समुपस्थितम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “But the third terrible evil, viz., the taking of others’ lives, which is done without enmity due to ignorance, is facing you. (9)

verses.text:
प्रतिज्ञातस्त्वया वीर दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्।
ऋषीणां रक्षणार्थाय वधः संयति रक्षसाम्॥ १०॥
एतन्निमित्तं च वनं दण्डका इति विश्रुतम्।
प्रस्थितस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा धृतबाणशरासनः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “O hero, you have undertaken a vow to kill the ogres on the battlefield for the protection of sages living in the Daṇḍaka forest; and for this very purpose you have set out with arrows and a bow towards the forest well-known as Daṇḍaka, with your brother. (10-11)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वां प्रस्थितं दृष्ट्वा मम चिन्ताकुलं मनः।
त्वद्वृत्तं चिन्तयन्त्या वै भवेन्निःश्रेयसं हितम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Hence, seeing you on your way to the Daṇḍaka, my mind is perturbed with anxiety, thinking of your imminent doings and of your highest well-being and worldly interests. (12)

verses.text:
नहि मे रोचते वीर गमनं दण्डकान् प्रति।
कारणं तत्र वक्ष्यामि वदन्त्याः श्रूयतां मम॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I do not like, O hero, your going towards the Daṇḍaka. I shall tell you the reason for that; while I speak of it, please listen. (13)

verses.text:
त्वं हि बाणधनुष्पाणिर्भ्रात्रा सह वनं गतः।
दृष्ट्वा वनचरान् सर्वान् कच्चित् कुर्याः शरव्ययम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “When you go to the forest with arrows and bow in hand together with your brother and see all kinds of animals in the forest, you may perhaps shoot an arrow somewhere. (14)

verses.text:
क्षत्रियाणामिह धनुर्हुताशस्येन्धनानि च।
समीपतः स्थितं तेजोबलमुच्छ्रयते भृशम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The bow and the fuel when placed near the warriors and a fire, respectively, greatly enhance their strength in this world. (15)

verses.text:
पुरा किल महाबाहो तपस्वी सत्यवान् शुचिः।
कस्मिंश्चिदभवत् पुण्ये वने रतमृगद्विजे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “They say, formerly, O mighty-armed prince, there was a truthful and pious ascetic in some holy forest, where animals and birds lived in joy. (16)

verses.text:
तस्यैव तपसो विघ्नं कर्तुमिन्द्रः शचीपतिः।
खड्गपाणिरथागच्छदाश्रमं भटरूपधृक्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Then, only to create obstruction in his austerities, Indra, the lord of Śacī, in the guise of a soldier, came to the hermitage, sword in hand. (17)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तदाश्रमपदे निहितः खड्ग उत्तमः।
स न्यासविधिना दत्तः पुण्ये तपसि तिष्ठतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “He kept the excellent sword in the precincts of his hermitage. It was given as a deposit to the sage, who was keeping himself busy with holy austerities. (18)

verses.text:
स तच्छस्त्रमनुप्राप्य न्यासरक्षणतत्परः।
वने तु विचरत्येव रक्षन् प्रत्ययमात्मनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Getting that weapon and being constantly mindful of guarding the deposit, he wandered even in the forest keeping the trust with him. (19)

verses.text:
यत्र गच्छत्युपादातुं मूलानि च फलानि च।
न विना याति तं खड्गं न्यासरक्षणतत्परः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Wherever he went even to bring roots and fruits, he would not go without that sword, being ever mindful of guarding the trust. (20)

verses.text:
नित्यं शस्त्रं परिवहन् क्रमेण स तपोधनः।
चकार रौद्रीं स्वां बुद्धिं त्यक्त्वा तपसि निश्चयम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Constantly carrying the weapon as he did, that ascetic’s mind turned cruel in course of time, giving up his determination to carry on his austerities. (21)

verses.text:
ततः स रौद्राभिरतः प्रमत्तोऽधर्मकर्षितः।
तस्य शस्त्रस्य संवासाज्जगाम नरकं मुनिः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Then, while taking pleasure in cruelty due to the company of that weapon, the said sage became negligent, was led astray by ‘Adharma’ and descended into hell. (22)

verses.text:
एवमेतत् पुरावृत्तं शस्त्रसंयोगकारणम्।
अग्निसंयोगवद्धेतुः शस्त्रसंयोग उच्यते॥ २३॥
verses.m: “This is what happened in the past as a result of association with that weapon. Association with a weapon is said to be of the same consequence as is the association with fire. (23)

verses.text:
स्नेहाच्च बहुमानाच्च स्मारये त्वां तु शिक्षये।
न कथंचन सा कार्या गृहीतधनुषा त्वया॥ २४॥
बुद्धिर्वैरं विना हन्तुं राक्षसान् दण्डकाश्रितान्।
अपराधं विना हन्तुं लोको वीर न मंस्यते॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Due to love and great respect I am making you acquainted with this and advising you that while taking the bow you should never take into your head to kill the ogres residing in Daṇḍaka without enmity. People do not commend killing without fault, O hero ! (24-25)

verses.text:
क्षत्रियाणां तु वीराणां वनेषु नियतात्मनाम्।
धनुषा कार्यमेतावदार्तानामभिरक्षणम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “The function of the bow for self-restrained heroic Kṣatriyas is only this much, viz., protection of those who are suffering. (26)

verses.text:
क्व च शस्त्रं क्व च वनं क्व च क्षात्रं तपः क्व च।
व्याविद्धमिदमस्माभिर्देशधर्मस्तु पूज्यताम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “What connection is there between a weapon and forest-life? What affinity is there between the duty of a Kṣatriya and asceticism? The two are contradictory. Let us respect the laws of the place. (27)

verses.text:
कदर्यकलुषा बुद्धिर्जायते शस्त्रसेवनात्।
पुनर्गत्वा त्वयोध्यायां क्षत्रधर्मं चरिष्यसि॥ २८॥
verses.m: “By use of arms the mind becomes contaminated with sin as in the case of unworthy men. After returning to Ayodhyā you can again follow the duty of a warrior.(28)

verses.text:
अक्षया तु भवेत् प्रीतिः श्वश्रूश्वशुरयोर्मम।
यदि राज्यं हि संन्यस्य भवेस्त्वं निरतो मुनिः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “It will bring endless joy to my mother-in-law and father-in-law if indeed after renouncing the kingdom you become a devoted sage. (29)

verses.text:
धर्मादर्थः प्रभवति धर्मात् प्रभवते सुखम्।
धर्मेण लभते सर्वं धर्मसारमिदं जगत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “From Dharma follows wealth, from Dharma comes happiness, by recourse to Dharma one gets everything. This world has Dharma as its essence. (30)

verses.text:
आत्मानं नियमैस्तैस्तैः कर्षयित्वा प्रयत्नतः।
प्राप्यते निपुणैर्धर्मो न सुखाल्लभते सुखम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The wise emaciate themselves with effort by imposing several restrictions on themselves and achieve Dharma. Dharma does not follow from merriment. (31)

verses.text:
नित्यं शुचिमतिः सौम्य चर धर्मं तपोवने।
सर्वं तु विदितं तुभ्यं त्रैलोक्यामपि तत्त्वतः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “With a pious mind, O gentle Rāma, always practise righteousness in the forest, suited for austerities. In fact, everything comprised in the three worlds is truly known to you. (32)

verses.text:
स्त्रीचापलादेतदुपाहृतं मे
धर्मं च वक्तुं तव कः समर्थः।
विचार्य बुद्ध्या तु सहानुजेन
यद् रोचते तत् कुरु माचिरेण॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “I have said this just in consonance with the frivolity of a woman. Who is really capable of teaching Dharma to you? However, thinking over it by recourse to reason together with your younger brother, you may do whatever appeals to you. Let there be no delay.” (33)

verses.text:
वाक्यमेतत् तु वैदेह्या व्याहृतं भर्तृभक्तया।
श्रुत्वा धर्मे स्थितो रामः प्रत्युवाचाथ जानकीम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having heard these words uttered by Vaidehī, devoted to her husband, Rāma, firmly adhering to Dharma, then, replied to Jānakī: (1)

verses.text:
हितमुक्तं त्वया देवि स्निग्धया सदृशं वचः।
कुलं व्यपदिशन्त्या च धर्मज्ञे जनकात्मजे॥ २॥
verses.m: “O daughter of Janaka, knower of Dharma, O queen, you being affectionate, have given a wholesome advice, which is becoming of you, referring as it does to the duty of my race. (2)

verses.text:
किं नु वक्ष्याम्यहं देवि त्वयैवोक्तमिदं वचः।
क्षत्रियैर्धार्यते चापो नार्तशब्दो भवेदिति॥ ३॥
verses.m: “O queen, what shall I say? You yourself have stated that a bow is wielded by Kṣatriyas so that there should be no cry of the sufferers. (3)

verses.text:
ते चार्ता दण्डकारण्ये मुनयः संशितव्रताः।
मां सीते स्वयमागम्य शरण्यं शरणं गताः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “In the Daṇḍaka forest those suffering sages, with austere vows, themselves came to me, O Sītā, and resorted to me, knowing me capable to protect them. (4)

verses.text:
वसन्तः कालकालेषु वने मूलफलाशनाः।
न लभन्ते सुखं भीरु राक्षसैः क्रूरकर्मभिः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Always dwelling in the forest, eating roots and fruits, they are not getting happiness, O timid one, due to ogres of cruel activities. (5)

verses.text:
भक्ष्यन्ते राक्षसैर्भीमैर्नरमांसोपजीविभिः।
ते भक्ष्यमाणा मुनयो दण्डकारण्यवासिनः॥ ६॥
अस्मानभ्यवपद्येति मामूचुर्द्विजसत्तमाः।
मया तु वचनं श्रुत्वा तेषामेवं मुखाच्च्युतम्॥ ७॥
कृत्वा वचनशुश्रूषां वाक्यमेतदुदाहृतम्।
प्रसीदन्तु भवन्तो मे ह्रीरेषा तु ममातुला॥ ८॥
यदीदृशैरहं विप्रैरुपस्थेयैरुपस्थितः।
किं करोमीति च मया व्याहृतं द्विजसंनिधौ॥ ९॥
verses.m: “They are being eaten up by the terrible ogres living on human flesh. Being devoured by these, the sages dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, the best among the Brāhmaṇas, asked me to show favour to them. I, for my part, having heard the words that had escaped from their mouth and having shown the desire to listen to their speech, made the following statement: ‘Be you gracious to me. Indeed it is a great shame for me that I have been approached by such Brāhmaṇas as are worthy of being approached.’ I then asked the Brāhmaṇas as to what I should do. (6—9)

verses.text:
सर्वैरेव समागम्य वागियं समुदाहृता।
राक्षसैर्दण्डकारण्ये बहुभिः कामरूपिभिः॥ १०॥
अर्दिताः स्म भृशं राम भवान् नस्तत्र रक्षतु।
होमकाले तु सम्प्राप्ते पर्वकालेषु चानघ॥ ११॥
धर्षयन्ति सुदुर्धर्षा राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः।
राक्षसैर्धर्षितानां च तापसानां तपस्विनाम्॥ १२॥
गतिं मृगयमाणानां भवान् नः परमा गतिः।
कामं तपःप्रभावेण शक्ता हन्तुं निशाचरान्॥ १३॥
चिरार्जितं न चेच्छामस्तपः खण्डयितुं वयम्।
बहुविघ्नं तपो नित्यं दुश्चरं चैव राघव॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Coming together, all of them made the following submission : ‘We have been greatly tormented in the Daṇḍaka forest by many ogres assuming different forms according to their will. Rāma, you protect us from them. When the time comes for pouring oblations into the sacred fire and also on holy occasions, the flesh-eating, unassailable ogres attack us, O sinless one ! You are the greatest asylum for us poor ascetics, who are seeking an asylum, assailed as we are by the ogres. Although we are able to kill the night-wanderers by virtue of our austerities, we do not desire to waste the power accumulated by us for a long time. O Rāghava, austerities are beset with many obstacles and are always difficult to be performed. (10—14)

verses.text:
तेन शापं न मुञ्चामो भक्ष्यमाणाश्च राक्षसैः।
तदर्द्यमानान् रक्षोभिर्दण्डकारण्यवासिभिः॥ १५॥
रक्ष नस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा त्वन्नाथा हि वयं वने।
मया चैतद्वचः श्रुत्वा कार्त्स्न्येन परिपालनम्॥ १६॥
ऋषीणां दण्डकारण्ये संश्रुतं जनकात्मजे।
संश्रुत्य च न शक्ष्यामि जीवमानः प्रतिश्रवम्॥ १७॥
मुनीनामन्यथा कर्तुं सत्यमिष्टं हि मे सदा।
अप्यहं जीवितं जह्यां त्वां वा सीते सलक्ष्मणाम्॥ १८॥
न तु प्रतिज्ञां संश्रुत्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विशेषतः।
तदवश्यं मया कार्यमृषीणां परिपालनम्॥ १९॥
अनुक्तेनापि वैदेहि प्रतिज्ञाय कथं पुनः।
मम स्नेहाच्च सौहार्दादिदमुक्तं त्वया वचः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Therefore, though being eaten up by the ogres, we do not pronounce a curse. Hence, alongwith your brother, you protect us, oppressed as we are by ogres dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest. For, you alone are our master in the forest.’ And having heard this speech, I promised complete protection to the sages living in the Daṇḍaka forest, O daughter of Janaka ! And having made a promise, I dare not, as long as I am alive, falsify the word given to the sages. For, truth is always dear to me. I can even give up my life for you, together with Lakṣmaṇa, but not my plighted word, given especially to the Brāhmaṇas. Therefore, O Vaidehī, I am compelled to protect the sages, even if I had not given the word, much more so when a vow has been taken. You have uttered these words due to your love and goodwill for me. (15—20)

verses.text:
परितुष्टोऽस्म्यहं सीते न ह्यनिष्टोऽनुशास्यते।
सदृशं चानुरूपं च कुलस्य तव शोभने।
सधर्मचारिणी मे त्वं प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी॥ २१॥
verses.m: “O Sītā, I am fully pleased. For, a person is never advised unless he is dear. And, it is becoming and proper not only for you but for your family too, O beautiful lady ! You are dearer to me even than life, being my companion in Dharma.” (21)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा
सीतां प्रियां मैथिलराजपुत्रीम्।
रामो धनुष्मान् सह लक्ष्मणेन
जगाम रम्याणि तपोवनानि॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having addressed these words to his beloved Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, the high-souled Rāma, the wielder of a bow, together with Lakṣmaṇa, proceeded to the charming groves inhabited by ascetics. (22)

verses.text:
अग्रतः प्रययौ रामः सीता मध्ये सुशोभना।
पृष्ठतस्तु धनुष्पाणिर्लक्ष्मणोऽनुजगाम ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Rāma walked in the van, the most beautiful Sītā in the middle, and in the rear followed Lakṣmaṇa, bow in hand. (1)

verses.text:
तौ पश्यमानौ विविधान् शैलप्रस्थान् वनानि च।
नदीश्च विविधा रम्या जग्मतुः सह सीतया॥ २॥
verses.m: They two, together with Sītā, went on seeing several mountain-peaks and forests, and several charming rivers. (2)

verses.text:
सारसांश्चक्रवाकांश्च नदीपुलिनचारिणः।
सरांसि च सपद्मानि युतानि जलजैः खगैः॥ ३॥
यूथबद्धांश्च पृषतान् मदोन्मत्तान् विषाणिनः।
महिषांश्च वराहांश्च गजांश्च द्रुमवैरिणः॥ ४॥
verses.m: They further saw cranes and Cakravāka birds moving on river banks, lakes with lotuses and aquatic birds, spotted deer moving in herds, horned buffaloes in rut, boars and elephants, the destroyers of trees. (3-4)

verses.text:
ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं लम्बमाने दिवाकरे।
ददृशुः सहिता रम्यं तटाकं योजनायुतम्॥ ५॥
पद्मपुष्करसम्बाधं गजयूथैरलंकृतम्।
सारसैर्हंसकादम्बैः संकुलं जलजातिभिः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Covering a long distance, they sighted together, while the sun was going down, a beautiful lake with an area of a square Yojana, full of red and white lotuses, adorned with herds of elephants and crowded with cranes, flocks of swans and other aquatic creatures. (5-6)

verses.text:
प्रसन्नसलिले रम्ये तस्मिन् सरसि शुश्रुवे।
गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषो न तु कश्चन दृश्यते॥ ७॥
verses.m: In that beautiful lake of clear water the sound of singing and musical instruments was heard, but nobody was to be seen. (7)

verses.text:
ततः कौतूहलाद् रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महारथः।
मुनिं धर्मभृतं नाम प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे॥ ८॥
verses.m: Then, out of curiosity Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the great car-warrior, proceeded to ask the sage named Dharmabhṛt, who accompanied them : (8)

verses.text:
इदमत्यद्भुतं श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां नो महामुने।
कौतूहलं महज्जातं किमिदं साधु कथ्यताम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “O great sage, hearing this most wonderful sound we are all seized with great curiosity. What is this? Pray, tell us in detail about it.” (9)

verses.text:
तेनैवमुक्तो धर्मात्मा राघवेण मुनिस्तदा।
प्रभावं सरसः क्षिप्रमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे॥ १०॥
verses.m: Thus addressed by Rāghava, the righteous sage forthwith started speaking about the greatness of the lake : (10)

verses.text:
इदं पञ्चाप्सरो नाम तटाकं सार्वकालिकम्।
निर्मितं तपसा राम मुनिना माण्डकर्णिना॥ ११॥
verses.m: “This is a lake named Pañcāpsara, ever full of water and created by Sage Māṇḍakarṇi by dint of his ascetic power, O Rāma ! (11)

verses.text:
स हि तेपे तपस्तीव्रं माण्डकर्णिर्महामुनिः।
दशवर्षसहस्राणि वायुभक्षो जलाशये॥ १२॥
verses.m: “That great Sage Māṇḍakarṇi performed severe austerities in the lake living on air alone for ten thousand years. (12)

verses.text:
ततः प्रव्यथिताः सर्वे देवाः साग्निपुरोगमाः।
अब्रुवन् वचनं सर्वे परस्परसमागताः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Thereupon getting disquieted, all the gods, with the god of fire at the head, gathered together and all of them spoke as follows : (13)

verses.text:
अस्माकं कस्यचित् स्थानमेष प्रार्थयते मुनिः।
इति संविग्नमनसः सर्वे तत्र दिवौकसः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘This sage is seeking the state of some one among us.’ Thus all the denizens of heaven felt disturbed in mind. (14)

verses.text:
ततः कर्तुं तपोविघ्नं सर्वदेवैर्नियोजिताः।
प्रधानाप्सरसः पञ्च विद्युच्चलितवर्चसः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Then, for causing interruption in his austerities, all the gods appointed five principal nymphs with bodies flashing like lightning. (15)

verses.text:
अप्सरोभिस्ततस्ताभिर्मुनिर्दृष्टपरावरः।
नीतो मदनवश्यत्वं देवानां कार्यसिद्धये॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Now that sage, who had seen what is wholesome or otherwise in this world as well as in the other, was captured with love by those nymphs for accomplishing the work of gods. (16)

verses.text:
ताश्चैवाप्सरसः पञ्च मुनेः पत्नीत्वमागताः।
तटाके निर्मितं तासां तस्मिन्नन्तर्हितं गृहम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “The same five nymphs have become the wives of the sage. In the lake has been built a secret house for them. (17)

verses.text:
तत्रैवाप्सरसः पञ्च निवसन्त्यो यथासुखम्।
रमयन्ति तपोयोगान्मुनिं यौवनमास्थितम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Dwelling happily in that very house, the five nymphs delight the sage, who has regained his youth, by virtue of his austerities. (18)

verses.text:
तासां संक्रीडमानानामेष वादित्रनिःस्वनः।
श्रूयते भूषणोन्मिश्रो गीतशब्दो मनोहरः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “This is the sound of the musical instruments and the charming song of the nymphs sung while they are playing, mixed with the tinkling of ornaments, that is the sound being heard.” (19)

verses.text:
आश्चर्यमिति तस्यैतद् वचनं भावितात्मनः।
राघवः प्रतिजग्राह सह भ्रात्रा महायशाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Rāghava of great renown together with his brother accepted the report of the pure-minded sage as a piece of wonder. (20)

verses.text:
एवं कथयमानः स ददर्शाश्रममण्डलम्।
कुशचीरपरिक्षिप्तं ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समावृतम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: While speaking thus, he saw a group of hermitages enveloped in Brahmic grandeur with Kuśa grass and bark garments spread round about. (21)

verses.text:
प्रविश्य सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च राघवः।
तदा तस्मिन् स काकुत्स्थः श्रीमत्याश्रममण्डले॥ २२॥
उषित्वा स सुखं तत्र पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः।
जगाम चाश्रमांस्तेषां पर्यायेण तपस्विनाम्॥ २३॥
येषामुषितवान् पूर्वं सकाशे स महास्त्रवित्।
क्वचित् परिदशान् मासानेकसंवत्सरं क्वचित्॥ २४॥
क्वचिच्च चतुरो मासान् पञ्च षट् च परान् क्वचित्।
अपरत्राधिकान् मासानध्यर्धमधिकं क्वचित्॥ २५॥
त्रीन् मासानष्टमासांश्च राघवो न्यवसत् सुखम्।
तत्र संवसतस्तस्य मुनीनामाश्रमेषु वै॥ २६॥
रमतश्चानुकूल्येन ययुः संवत्सरा दश।
परिसृत्य च धर्मज्ञो राघवः सह सीतया॥ २७॥
सुतीक्ष्णस्याश्रमपदं पुनरेवाजगाम ह।
स तमाश्रममागम्य मुनिभिः परिपूजितः॥ २८॥
तत्रापि न्यवसद् रामः किंचित् कालमरिंदमः।
अथाश्रमस्थो विनयात् कदाचित् तं महामुनिम्॥ २९॥
उपासीनः स काकुत्स्थः सुतीक्ष्णमिदमब्रवीत्।
अस्मिन्नरण्ये भगवन्नगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Rāghava together with Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa then entered that beautiful group of hermitages and staying there happily, being honoured by great sages, that descendant of Kakutstha visited one by one the hermitages of those sages with whom that knower of great weapons had previously stayed. Rāghava happily stayed somewhere for ten months, somewhere for a year, somewhere for four months, somewhere five, six and (even) more, elsewhere for more months, somewhere half a month more and in other hermitages for eight and three months. While he was thus staying in the hermitages of the sages and passing time happily and comfortably, ten years passed. Having thus wandered, Rāghava, the knower of Dharma, together with Sītā came again, they say, to the site of Sutīkṣṇa’s hermitage. Coming to that hermitage, and honoured by the sages, the said Rāma, the vanquisher of foes, stayed there also for some time. Then, while sitting in the hermitage modestly beside the great sage, the said Kākutstha on one occasion spoke as follows to Sutīkṣṇa: “Sir, I have heard from those talking among themselves that Agastya, the foremost of sages, permanently dwells in this forest. However, due to the vastness of this forest, I do not know that place. (22—30)

verses.text:
वसतीति मया नित्यं कथाः कथयतां श्रुतम्।
न तु जानामि तं देशं वनस्यास्य महत्तया॥ ३१॥
कुत्राश्रमपदं रम्यं महर्षेस्तस्य धीमतः।
प्रसादार्थं भगवतः सानुजः सह सीतया॥ ३२॥
अगस्त्यमधिगच्छेयमभिवादयितुं मुनिम्।
मनोरथो महानेष हृदि सम्परिवर्तते॥ ३३॥
यदहं तं मुनिवरं शुश्रूषेयमपि स्वयम्।
इति रामस्य स मुनिः श्रुत्वा धर्मात्मनो वचः॥ ३४॥
सुतीक्ष्णः प्रत्युवाचेदं प्रीतो दशरथात्मजम्।
अहमप्येतदेव त्वां वक्तुकामः सलक्ष्मणम्॥ ३५॥
अगस्त्यमभिगच्छेति सीतया सह राघव।
दिष्ट्या त्विदानीमर्थेऽस्मिन् स्वयमेव ब्रवीषि माम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Where is the lovely site of the hermitage of that wise and eminent sage? There exists a great desire in my heart that I should get an opportunity to pay my obeisance to Sage Agastya alongwith my younger brother and Sītā for obtaining his grace, so that I may personally do some service also to that great sage.” Pleased to hear this submission of the righteous Rāma, the aforesaid Sage Sutīkṣṇa replied as follows to the son of Daśaratha: “I too wanted to tell you as well as Lakṣmaṇa the same thing, viz., that you should go to Agastya with Sītā, O Rāghava! It is good that you are speaking to me about it yourself. (31—36)

verses.text:
अयमाख्यामि ते राम यत्रागस्त्यो महामुनिः।
योजनान्याश्रमात् तात याहि चत्वारि वै ततः।
दक्षिणेन महान् श्रीमानगस्त्यभ्रातुराश्रमः॥ ३७॥
स्थलीप्रायवनोद्देशे पिप्पलीवनशोभिते।
बहुपुष्पफले रम्ये नानाविहगनादिते॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “I am just telling you, O Rāma, where the great Sage Agastya lives. Proceed, O dear son, southward to a distance of four Yojanas from this hermitage; there lies in a well-nigh flat portion of the forest the great and grand hermitage of Agastya’s brother, adorned with a grove of Pippalī (long pepper) trees, nay, having many flowers and fruits, and charming and resonant with the chirping of various birds. (37-38)

verses.text:
पद्मिन्यो विविधास्तत्र प्रसन्नसलिलाशयाः।
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः ॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “There are several lotus-ponds and lakes with limpid water, crowded with swans and Kāraṇḍavas and adorned with Cakravāka birds. (39)

verses.text:
तत्रैकां रजनीं व्युष्य प्रभाते राम गम्यताम्।
दक्षिणां दिशमास्थाय वनखण्डस्य पार्श्वतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Staying there for a night, Rāma, you may proceed in the morning in a southerly direction along side the grove. (40)

verses.text:
तत्रागस्त्याश्रमपदं गत्वा योजनमन्तरम्।
रमणीये वनोद्देशे बहुपादपशोभिते॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Covering a distance of eight miles you will reach the site of Agastya’s hermitage in a delightful part of the forest, adorned with many trees. (41)

verses.text:
रंस्यते तत्र वैदेही लक्ष्मणश्च त्वया सह।
स हि रम्यो वनोद्देशो बहुपादपसंयुतः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “There Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa will dwell happily with you. For, that is a charming part of the forest with many trees. (42)

verses.text:
यदि बुद्धिः कृता द्रष्टुमगस्त्यं तं महामुनिम्।
अद्यैव गमने बुद्धिं रोचयस्व महामते॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “If you have made up your mind to see that great sage, Agastya, O highly intelligent prince, decide to proceed this very day.” (43)

verses.text:
इति रामो मुनेः श्रुत्वा सह भ्रात्राभिवाद्य च।
प्रतस्थेऽगस्त्यमुद्दिश्य सानुगः सह सीतया॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Hearing thus the sage’s words and saluting him with his brother, Rāma set out with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā to meet Agastya. (44)

verses.text:
पश्यन् वनानि चित्राणि पर्वतांश्चाभ्रसंनिभान्।
सरांसि सरितश्चैव पथि मार्गवशानुगान्॥ ४५॥
सुतीक्ष्णेनोपदिष्टेन गत्वा तेन पथा सुखम्।
इदं परमसंहृष्टो वाक्यं लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Seeing varied forests and cloud-like mountains, lakes and rivers on the way, he proceeded happily along the path directed by Sutīkṣṇa and, being supremely delighted, he spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa : (45-46)

verses.text:
एतदेवाश्रमपदं नूनं तस्य महात्मनः।
अगस्त्यस्य मुनेर्भ्रातुर्दृश्यते पुण्यकर्मणः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Indeed this very place appears to be the site of the hermitage of that high-souled brother of Sage Agastya of holy deeds. (47)

verses.text:
यथा हीमे वनस्यास्य ज्ञाताः पथि सहस्रशः।
संनताः फलभारेण पुष्पभारेण च द्रुमाः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “As was pointed out by Sutīkṣṇa, these thousands of trees of this forest are seen in the way bent down with their load of fruits and the mass of flowers. (48)

verses.text:
पिप्पलीनां च पक्वानां वनादस्मादुपागतः।
गन्धोऽयं पवनोत्क्षिप्तः सहसा कटुकोदयः॥ ४९॥
