verses.m: “This scent of the ripe Pippalī fruits wafted by the breeze and coming from this forest is suddenly giving rise to a pungent taste. (49)

verses.text:
तत्र तत्र च दृश्यन्ते संक्षिप्ताः काष्ठसंचयाः।
लूनाश्च परिदृश्यन्ते दर्भा वैदूर्यवर्चसः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Here and there are seen collected heaps of wood and blades of Darbha grass, having the lustre of Vaidūrya (a cat’s-eye gem) are seen cut. (50)

verses.text:
एतच्च वनमध्यस्थं कृष्णाभ्रशिखरोपमम्।
पावकस्याश्रमस्थस्य धूमाग्रं सम्प्रदृश्यते॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “And here in the middle of the forest is vividly seen a column of smoke from the fire in the hermitage, looking like the top of a dark cloud. (51)

verses.text:
विविक्तेषु च तीर्थेषु कृतस्नाना द्विजातयः।
पुष्पोपहारं कुर्वन्ति कुसुमैः स्वयमर्जितैः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Having had their bath in the holy waters, the Brāhmaṇas are giving offerings (to the gods) with the flowers collected by themselves. (52)

verses.text:
ततः सुतीक्ष्णवचनं यथा सौम्य मया श्रुतम्।
अगस्त्यस्याश्रमो भ्रातुर्नूनमेष भविष्यति॥ ५३॥
निगृह्य तरसा मृत्युं लोकानां हितकाम्यया।
यस्य भ्रात्रा कृतेयं दिक्शरण्या पुण्यकर्मणा॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Hence, O gentle Lakṣmaṇa, according to the description of Sutīkṣṇa heard by me, surely this must be the hermitage of the brother of Agastya, by whose brother Agastya of holy deeds, with intent to do good to the people and controlling by his spiritual might death (in the form of the ogres Vātāpi and Ilvala), this (southern) quarter has been made habitable. (53-54)

verses.text:
इहैकदा किल क्रूरो वातापिरपि चेल्वलः।
भ्रातरौ सहितावास्तां ब्राह्मणघ्नौ महासुरौ॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “Once, they say, here dwelt together two brothers—great ogres and killers of Brāhmaṇas—Vātāpi and also Ilvala. (55)

verses.text:
धारयन् ब्राह्मणं रूपमिल्वलः संस्कृतं वदन्।
आमन्त्रयति विप्रान् स श्राद्धमुद्दिश्य निर्घृणः॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Assuming the form of a Brāhmaṇa and speaking Sanskrit, that merciless Ilvala used to invite Brāhmaṇas for the sake of Śrāddha. (56)

verses.text:
भ्रातरं संस्कृतं कृत्वा ततस्तं मेषरूपिणम्।
तान् द्विजान् भोजयामास श्राद्धदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “Thereupon, cooking that brother of his, who used to take the form of a ram, he used to feed those Brāhmaṇas according to the injunctions laid down for Śrāddha. (57)

verses.text:
ततो भुक्तवतां तेषां विप्राणामिल्वलोऽब्रवीत्।
वातापे निष्क्रमस्वेति स्वरेण महता वदन्॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “Then, after those Brāhmaṇas had finished the dinner, llvala used to call out in a loud voice, “O Vātāpi, come out !” (58)

verses.text:
ततो भ्रातुर्वचः श्रुत्वा वातापिर्मेषवन्नदन्।
भित्त्वा भित्त्वा शरीराणि ब्राह्मणानां विनिष्पतत्॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “Now, hearing the voice of his brother, Vātāpi used to come out tearing the bodies of the Brāhmaṇas and bleating like a ram. (59)

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणानां सहस्राणि तैरेवं कामरूपिभिः।
विनाशितानि संहत्य नित्यशः पिशिताशनैः॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “Thus thousands of Brāhmaṇas were killed by those flesh-eaters always coming together and assuming forms at will. (60)

verses.text:
अगस्त्येन तदा देवैः प्रार्थितेन महर्षिणा।
अनुभूय किल श्राद्धे भक्षितः स महासुरः॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “That time, they say, that great ogre was eaten up with taste by the great sage Agastya as requested by gods. (61)

verses.text:
ततः सम्पन्नमित्युक्त्वा दत्त्वा हस्तेऽवनेजनम्।
भ्रातरं निष्क्रमस्वेति चेल्वलः समभाषत॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “Thereupon, saying ‘It is finished’ and offering water for washing the hands, Ilvala cried out to the brother : ‘Come out !’ (62)

verses.text:
स तदा भाषमाणं तु भ्रातरं विप्रघातिनम्।
अब्रवीत् प्रहसन् धीमानगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “Then, while he was addressing these words to his brother, the killer of Brāhmaṇas, that jewel among sages, the intelligent Agastya said laughingly : (63)

verses.text:
कुतो निष्क्रमितुं शक्तिर्मया जीर्णस्य रक्षसः।
भ्रातुस्तु मेषरूपस्य गतस्य यमसादनम्॥ ६४॥
verses.m: ‘Where is the power to come out left in the ogre, your brother in the form of a ram, who stands digested by me and is gone to the abode of Yama?’ (64)

verses.text:
अथ तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भ्रातुर्निधनसंश्रितम्।
प्रधर्षयितुमारेभे मुनिं क्रोधान्निशाचरः॥ ६५॥
verses.m: “Thereupon, hearing his words declaring the death of his brother; the night-wanderer started assailing the sage in anger. (65)

verses.text:
सोऽभ्यद्रवद् द्विजेन्द्रं तं मुनिना दीप्ततेजसा।
चक्षुषानलकल्पेन निर्दग्धो निधनं गतः॥ ६६॥
verses.m: “He attacked the Indra amongst the Brāhmaṇas and, being burnt with his fire-like glance by that sage of blazing lustre, he died. (66)

verses.text:
तस्यायमाश्रमो भ्रातुस्तटाकवनशोभितः।
विप्रानुकम्पया येन कर्मेदं दुष्करं कृतम्॥ ६७॥
verses.m: “This is the hermitage—beautified by lakes and forest—of the brother of that sage who did this difficult deed out of pity for the Brāhmaṇas.” (67)

verses.text:
एवं कथयमानस्य तस्य सौमित्रिणा सह।
रामस्यास्तं गतः सूर्यः संध्याकालोऽभ्यवर्तत॥ ६८॥
verses.m: While the celebrated Rāma was thus talking to the son of Sumitrā, the sun set and the time of evening devotions arrived. (68)

verses.text:
उपास्य पश्चिमां संध्यां सह भ्रात्रा यथाविधि।
प्रविवेशाश्रमपदं तमृषिं चाभ्यवादयत्॥ ६९॥
verses.m: Having performed his evening devotions according to scriptural ordinance together with his younger brother, he entered the site of the hermitage and greeted that sage. (69)

verses.text:
सम्यक्प्रतिगृहीतस्तु मुनिना तेन राघवः।
न्यवसत् तां निशामेकां प्राश्य मूलफलानि च॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Warmly received by the said sage, Rāghava stayed there that one night taking roots and fruits alone. (70)

verses.text:
तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामुदिते रविमण्डले।
भ्रातरं तमगस्त्यस्य आमन्त्रयत राघवः॥ ७१॥
verses.m: When the night had passed, Rāghava at sunrise took leave of that brother of Agastya with the following words : (71)

verses.text:
अभिवादये त्वां भगवन् सुखमस्म्युषितो निशाम्।
आमन्त्रये त्वां गच्छामि गुरुं ते द्रष्टुमग्रजम्॥ ७२॥
verses.m: “I pay obeisance to you, sir; I have stayed happily for the night. I take leave of you. I am going to see your revered elder brother.” (72)

verses.text:
गम्यतामिति तेनोक्तो जगाम रघुनन्दनः।
यथोद्दिष्टेन मार्गेण वनं तच्चावलोकयन्॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Spoken to by him in the words ‘You may go’, the delight of Raghu left along the path pointed out to him, seeing that forest. (73)

verses.text:
नीवारान् पनसान् सालान् वञ्जुलांस्तिनिशांस्तथा।
चिरिबिल्वान् मधूकांश्च बिल्वानथ च तिन्दुकान्॥ ७४॥
पुष्पितान् पुष्पिताग्राभिर्लताभिरुपशोभितान्।
ददर्श रामः शतशस्तत्र कान्तारपादपान्॥ ७५॥
हस्तिहस्तैर्विमृदितान् वानरैरुपशोभितान्।
मत्तैः शकुनिसङ्घैश्च शतशः प्रतिनादितान्॥ ७६॥
verses.m: Rāma saw there hundreds of forest trees—Nīvāra, Panasa, sāl and Vañjula, Tiniśa, Ciribilva, and Madhūka, Bilva and Tinduka too in flower and beautified by blossoming climbers, damaged by the trunks of elephants, adorned by monkeys and made resonant by the noise of flocks of birds in heat. (74—76)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीत् समीपस्थं रामो राजीवलोचनः।
पृष्ठतोऽनुगतं वीरं लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्॥ ७७॥
verses.m: Then the lotus-eyed Rāma said to the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, who was closely following behind him and added to his glory : (77)

verses.text:
स्निग्धपत्रा यथा वृक्षा यथा क्षान्ता मृगद्विजाः।
आश्रमो नातिदूरस्थो महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः॥ ७८॥
verses.m: “As (can be seen from the fact that) the trees are clothed with glossy leaves and the animals and birds are docile, the hermitage of that pure-souled great sage is not far. (78)

verses.text:
अगस्त्य इति विख्यातो लोके स्वेनैव कर्मणा।
आश्रमो दृश्यते तस्य परिश्रान्तश्रमापहः॥ ७९॥
प्राज्यधूमाकुलवनश्चीरमालापरिष्कृतः।
प्रशान्तमृगयूथश्च नानाशकुनिनादितः॥ ८०॥
verses.m: “The hermitage, relieving the fatigue of the tired, of him who has become famous in the world as Agastya by his own deed, is seen filling the forest with the smoke rising from oblations thrown into the sacred fire, adorned with bark-garments and garlands, containing very peaceful herds of deer and resounding with the cries of various birds. (79-80)

verses.text:
निगृह्य तरसा मृत्युं लोकानां हितकाम्यया।
दक्षिणा दिक् कृता येन शरण्या पुण्यकर्मणा॥ ८१॥
तस्येदमाश्रमपदं प्रभावाद् यस्य राक्षसैः।
दिगियं दक्षिणा त्रासाद् दृश्यते नोपभुज्यते॥ ८२॥
verses.m: “This is the site of the hermitage of him who, having by his might controlled death and performing holy deeds, made the southern quarter habitable with intent to do good to the people, and through whose spiritual force this southern quarter is looked on with alarm by the ogres, and not enjoyed. (81-82)

verses.text:
यदाप्रभृति चाक्रान्ता दिगियं पुण्यकर्मणा।
तदाप्रभृति निर्वैराः प्रशान्ता रजनीचराः॥ ८३॥
verses.m: “No sooner had this quarter been set foot on by this sage of holy deeds than the night-wanderers became extremely quiet and free from enmity. (83)

verses.text:
नाम्ना चेयं भगवतो दक्षिणा दिक्प्रदक्षिणा।
प्रथिता त्रिषु लोकेषु दुर्धर्षा क्रूरकर्मभिः॥ ८४॥
verses.m: “This southern quarter has become well-known by the name of the revered sage as most safe and unassailable by people of cruel deeds. (84)

verses.text:
मार्गं निरोद्धुं सततं भास्करस्याचलोत्तमः।
संदेशं पालयंस्तस्य विन्ध्यशैलो न वर्धते॥ ८५॥
verses.m: “Constantly obeying his command, the Vindhya mountain, the foremost of mountains, is not growing up to obstruct the path of the sun. (85)

verses.text:
अयं दीर्घायुषस्तस्य लोके विश्रुतकर्मणः।
अगस्त्यस्याश्रमः श्रीमान् विनीतमृगसेवितः॥ ८६॥
verses.m: “This is the beautiful hermitage, the resort of tame animals, of that long-lived Agastya whose deeds are well-known in the world. (86)

verses.text:
एष लोकार्चितः साधुर्हिते नित्यं रतः सताम्।
अस्मानधिगतानेष श्रेयसा योजयिष्यति॥ ८७॥
verses.m: “He is a saint adored by the people and always devoted to the good of the virtuous. He will endow us, who have come to him, with blessings. (87)

verses.text:
आराधयिष्याम्यत्राहमगस्त्यं तं महामुनिम्।
शेषं च वनवासस्य सौम्य वत्स्याम्यहं प्रभो॥ ८८॥
verses.m: “Here I shall adore that great sage, Agastya, and stay for the rest of my period of exile in the forest, O gentle and powerful prince ! (88)

verses.text:
अत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः।
अगस्त्यं नियताहाराः सततं पर्युपासते॥ ८९॥
verses.m: “Here gods and Gandharvas, Siddhas and the greatest sages always wait upon Agastya, living on a restricted diet. (89)

verses.text:
नात्र जीवेन्मृषावादी क्रूरो वा यदि वा शठः।
नृशंसः पापवृत्तो वा मुनिरेष तथाविधः॥ ९०॥
verses.m: “This sage is such that a liar, or a cruel man, a knave, a wicked person or a sinner cannot live here. (90)

verses.text:
अत्र देवाश्च यक्षाश्च नागाश्च पतगैः सह।
वसन्ति नियताहारा धर्ममाराधयिष्णवः॥ ९१॥
verses.m: “Seeking to observe piety, gods as well as Yakṣas and Nāgas together with birds abide here with their diet controlled.(91)

verses.text:
अत्र सिद्धा महात्मानो विमानैः सूर्यसंनिभैः।
त्यक्त्वा देहान् नवैर्देहैः स्वर्याताः परमर्षयः॥ ९२॥
verses.m: “Here exalted and realized souls and greatest sages endowed with new bodies have ascended to heaven in aerial cars bright as the sun, giving up their (worn-out) bodies. (92)

verses.text:
यक्षत्वममरत्वं च राज्यानि विविधानि च।
अत्र देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति भूतैराराधिताः शुभैः॥ ९३॥
verses.m: “Adored by good people, gods confer Yakṣahood, divinity and different kingdoms on their worshippers here. (93)

verses.text:
आगताः स्माश्रमपदं सौमित्रे प्रविशाग्रतः।
निवेदयेह मां प्राप्तमृषये सह सीतया॥ ९४॥
verses.m: “O son of Sumitrā we have reached the site of the hermitage. Go ahead and tell the sage that I have come here with Sītā.” (94)

verses.text:
स प्रविश्याश्रमपदं लक्ष्मणो राघवानुजः।
अगस्त्यशिष्यमासाद्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Entering the site of the hermitage and approaching a disciple of Agastya, that younger brother of Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa, spoke as follows : (1)

verses.text:
राजा दशरथो नाम ज्येष्ठस्तस्य सुतो बली।
रामः प्राप्तो मुनिं द्रष्टुं भार्यया सह सीतया॥ २॥
verses.m: “There was a king named Daśaratha. His mighty, eldest son, Rāma, has come with Sītā, his wife, to call on the sage. (2)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणो नाम तस्याहं भ्राता त्ववरजो हितः।
अनुकूलश्च भक्तश्च यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “It is possible You may have heard the name. I am his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, rendering service to him, favourably disposed and devoted to him. (3)

verses.text:
ते वयं वनमत्युग्रं प्रविष्टाः पितृशासनात्।
द्रष्टुमिच्छामहे सर्वे भगवन्तं निवेद्यताम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “We have entered a very frightful forest at the command of our father and all of us desire to see the revered sage. May this please be reported to him.” (4)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य तपोधनः।
तथेत्युक्त्वाग्निशरणं प्रविवेश निवेदितुम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid words of the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, the ascetic said, ‘Well’, and entered the fire-sanctuary to make a report. (5)

verses.text:
स प्रविश्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं तपसा दुष्प्रधर्षणम्।
कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदं रामागमनमञ्जसा॥ ६॥
यथोक्तं लक्ष्मणेनैव शिष्योऽगस्त्यस्य सम्मतः।
पुत्रौ दशरथस्येमौ रामो लक्ष्मण एव च॥ ७॥
प्रविष्टावाश्रमपदं सीतया सह भार्यया।
द्रष्टुं भवन्तमायातौ शुश्रूषार्थमरिंदमौ॥ ८॥
verses.m: Entering the sanctuary and joining his palms, that favourite disciple of Agastya reported at once the arrival of Rāma, exactly as requested by Lakṣmaṇa, to the foremost sage, unassailable through askesis : “The yonder two sons of Daśaratha, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, have entered the site of our hermitage with Sītā, the former’s wife. Those vanquishers of foes have come to see you in order to be of some service to you. (6—8)

verses.text:
यदत्रानन्तरं तत् त्वमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि।
ततः शिष्यादुपश्रुत्य प्राप्तं रामं सलक्ष्मणम्॥ ९॥
वैदेहीं च महाभागामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
दिष्ट्या रामश्चिरस्याद्य द्रष्टुं मां समुपागतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “You may be pleased to order what to do next.” Then, hearing from his pupil that Rāma and Vaidehī of great fortune had arrived with Lakṣmaṇa, he spoke as follows : “It is good that after a long time today Śrī Rāma has come to see me. (9-10)

verses.text:
मनसा कांक्षितं ह्यस्य मयाप्यागमनं प्रति।
गम्यतां सत्कृतो रामः सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः॥ ११॥
प्रवेश्यतां समीपं मे किमसौ न प्रवेशितः।
एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना॥ १२॥
अभिवाद्याब्रवीच्छिष्यस्तथेति नियताञ्जलिः।
तदा निष्क्रम्य सम्भ्रान्तः शिष्यो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
कोऽसौ रामो मुनिं द्रष्टुमेतु प्रविशतु स्वयम्।
ततो गत्वाऽऽश्रमपदं शिष्येण सह लक्ष्मणः॥ १४॥
दर्शयामास काकुत्स्थं सीतां च जनकात्मजाम्।
तं शिष्यः प्रश्रितं वाक्यमगस्त्यवचनं ब्रुवन्॥ १५॥
प्रावेशयद् यथान्यायं सत्कारार्हं सुसत्कृतम्।
प्रविवेश ततो रामः सीतया सह लक्ष्मणः॥ १६॥
प्रशान्तहरिणाकीर्णमाश्रमं ह्यवलोकयन्।
स तत्र ब्रह्मणः स्थानमग्नेः स्थानं तथैव च॥ १७॥
विष्णोः स्थानं महेन्द्रस्य स्थानं चैव विवस्वतः।
सोमस्थानं भगस्थानं स्थानं कौबेरमेव च॥ १८॥
धातुर्विधातुः स्थानं च वायोः स्थानं तथैव च।
स्थानं च पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः॥ १९॥
स्थानं तथैव गायत्र्या वसूनां स्थानमेव च।
स्थानं च नागराजस्य गरुडस्थानमेव च॥ २०॥
कार्तिकेयस्य च स्थानं धर्मस्थानं च पश्यति।
ततः शिष्यैः परिवृतो मुनिरप्यभिनिष्पतत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I too had longed in my mind for his arrival. You may go and escort Rāma respectfully together with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa in my presence. Wherefore was he not allowed to enter?” Thus told by the high-souled sage, the knower of Dharma, the pupil prostrated to him and said ‘Amen’ with joined palms. Then, hurriedly coming out, the pupil said to Lakṣmaṇa, “Who is that Rāma? Let him enter the Āśrama and go to see the sage. Let him enter the sanctuary.” Moving to the entrance of the hermitage with the pupil, Lakṣmaṇa showed to him Kākutstha and Sītā, the daughter of Janaka. Repeating the words of Agastya, the pupil modestly ushered him into the sanctuary with due respect and ceremony such as he deserved. Then Rāma with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa actually entered the sanctuary, seeing the hermitage crowded with peaceful deer. He saw there the place assigned to Brahmā (the creator) and also the place of Śiva, the place of Viṣṇu, the place of the great Indra as also of Vivaswān (the sun-god), the place of Soma (the moon-god), the place of Bhaga and the place of Kubera (the deity presiding over the northern quarter), the place of Dhātā and Vidhātā and also the place of Vāyu (the wind-god) and the place of the high-souled Varuṇa distinguished by a noose in his hand, as also the place of Gāyatrī (one of the consorts of Brahmā) and the place of the Vasus as well and the place of Vāsuki (the king of the Nāgas) and the place of Garuḍa (the king of birds), the place of Kārtikeya (the younger son of Lord Śiva) and the place of Dharma (the god of piety). Then, surrounded by his pupils, the sage also came forward. (11—21)

verses.text:
तं ददर्शाग्रतो रामो मुनीनां दीप्ततेजसाम्।
अब्रवीद् वचनं वीरो लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma saw him at the head of the sages of bright lustre. The hero addressed the following words to Lakṣmaṇa of increasing grandeur : (22)

verses.text:
बहिर्लक्ष्मण निष्क्रामत्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः।
औदार्येणावगच्छामि निधानं तपसामिमम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Lakṣmaṇa, the revered sage Agastya is coming out. From his magnanimity I am able to recognize this abode of askesis.” (23)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुरगस्त्यं सूर्यवर्चसम्।
जग्राहापततस्तस्य पादौ च रघुनन्दनः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Thus saying, the mighty-armed scion of Raghu met Agastya of sun-like lustre and touched his feet as he came. (24)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्य तु धर्मात्मा तस्थौ रामः कृताञ्जलिः।
सीतया सह वैदेह्या तदा रामः सलक्ष्मणः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Having saluted him, the righteous Rāma stood with joined palms together with Sītā, the princess of Videha, and Lakṣmaṇa. (25)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य च काकुत्स्थमर्चयित्वाऽऽसनोदकैः।
कुशलप्रश्नमुक्त्वा च आस्यतामिति सोऽब्रवीत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: The sage welcomed Kākutstha, offered him a seat and water (to wash his hands and feet), inquired after his welfare and asked him to sit down. (26)

verses.text:
अग्निं हुत्वा प्रदायार्घ्यमतिथीन् प्रतिपूज्य च।
वानप्रस्थेन धर्मेण स तेषां भोजनं ददौ॥ २७॥
verses.m: He first poured oblations into the sacred fire, then offered water to the guests, honoured them according to the code prescribed for anchorites and offered them meals. (27)

verses.text:
प्रथमं चोपविश्याथ धर्मज्ञो मुनिपुंगवः।
उवाच राममासीनं प्राञ्जलिं धर्मकोविदम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Sitting down himself first, the knower of Dharma, the foremost among sages, said to Śrī Rāma, who now sat with folded hands, well-versed as he was in the code of right conduct : (28)

verses.text:
अग्निं हुत्वा प्रदायार्घ्यमतिथिं प्रतिपूजयेत्।
अन्यथा खलु काकुत्स्थ तपस्वी समुदाचरन्।
दुःसाक्षीव परे लोके स्वानि मांसानि भक्षयेत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “An ascetic should pour oblations into the sacred fire, offer water to a guest (to wash his hands) and honour him (in other ways). An ascetic behaving otherwise, O Kākutstha, will, like a false-witness, have to eat his own flesh in the other world. (29)

verses.text:
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य धर्मचारी महारथः।
पूजनीयश्च मान्यश्च भवान् प्राप्तः प्रियातिथिः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “You, the king of the whole world, a righteous and great car-warrior, an adorable and respectable dear guest, have come.” (30)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा फलैर्मूलैः पुष्पैश्चान्यैश्च राघवम्।
पूजयित्वा यथाकामं ततोऽगस्त्यस्तमब्रवीत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Thus saying and entertaining Rāghava according to the latter’s desire with fruits, roots, flowers and other things, Agastya then said to him : (31)

verses.text:
इदं दिव्यं महच्चापं हेमवज्रविभूषितम्।
वैष्णवं पुरुषव्याघ्र निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Here is a great divine bow of Viṣṇu ornamented with gold and diamonds and manufactured by Viśwakarmā, O tiger among men ! (32)

verses.text:
अमोघः सूर्यसंकाशो ब्रह्मदत्तः शरोत्तमः।
दत्तौ मम महेन्द्रेण तूणी चाक्षय्यसायकौ॥ ३३॥
सम्पूर्णौ निशितैर्बाणैर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः।
महाराजतकोशोऽयमसिर्हेमविभूषितः ॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “This jewel among arrows, never failing and bright as the sun, was given by Brahmā. Mahendra gave me two inexhaustible quivers full of sharp arrows burning like fire. This is a sword ornamented with gold and kept in a gold sheath. (33-34)

verses.text:
अनेन धनुषा राम हत्वा संख्ये महासुरान्।
आजहार श्रियं दीप्तां पुरा विष्णुर्दिवौकसाम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Formerly, O Rāma, Viṣṇu killed on the battlefield great demons with this bow and brought back to the denizens of heaven their bright splendour. (35)

verses.text:
तद्धनुस्तौ च तूणी च शरं खड्गं च मानद।
जयाय प्रतिगृह्णीष्व वज्रं वज्रधरो यथा॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “O bestower of honour, accept for your victory that bow, those two quivers, the arrow and the sword, as Indra accepted the thunderbolt.” (36)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः समस्तं तद्वरायुधम्।
दत्त्वा रामाय भगवानगस्त्यः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Thus speaking and giving all that collection of foremost weapons to Rāma, the revered Agastya of great lustre said again : (37)

verses.text:
राम प्रीतोऽस्मि भद्रं ते परितुष्टोऽस्मि लक्ष्मण।
अभिवादयितुं यन्मां प्राप्तौ स्थः सह सीतया॥ १॥
verses.m: “Rāma, I am pleased with you. Luck be to you ! Lakṣmaṇa, I am fully satisfied that you two have come to greet me together with Sītā. (1)

verses.text:
अध्वश्रमेण वां खेदो बाधते प्रचुरश्रमः।
व्यक्तमुत्कण्ठते वापि मैथिली जनकात्मजा॥ २॥
verses.m: “Fatigue due to exertion entailed by journey and marked by profuse perspiration is troubling you two and it is evident that the Princess of Mithilā, daughter of Janaka, too longs for rest. (2)

verses.text:
एषा च सुकुमारी च खेदैश्च न विमानिता।
प्राज्यदोषं वनं प्राप्ता भर्तृस्नेहप्रचोदिता॥ ३॥
verses.m: “She is tender and has never been tormented by fatigue before; she has come to the forest full of risks due to sheer love for her husband. (3)

verses.text:
यथैषा रमते राम इह सीता तथा कुरु।
दुष्करं कृतवत्येषा वने त्वामभिगच्छती॥ ४॥
verses.m: “O Rāma, do that by which Sītā may this Sītā feels happy and comfortable here. Coming with you to the forest, she has done a difficult thing. (4)

verses.text:
एषा हि प्रकृतिः स्त्रीणामासृष्टे रघुनन्दन।
समस्थमनुरज्यन्ते विषमस्थं त्यजन्ति च॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Ever since the dawn of creation, it has been the nature of women that they love a man only so long as he is in prosperity and give him up when he is in adversity. (5)

verses.text:
शतह्रदानां लोलत्वं शस्त्राणां तीक्ष्णतां तथा।
गरुडानिलयोः शैघ्र्यमनुगच्छन्ति योषितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Women follow the inconstancy of lightning, the sharpness of weapons and the speed of an eagle and wind. (6)

verses.text:
इयं तु भवतो भार्या दोषैरेतैर्विवर्जिता।
श्लाघ्या च व्यपदेश्या च यथा देवीष्वरुन्धती॥ ७॥
verses.m: “This wife of yours, however, is entirely free from these blemishes and praiseworthy; and deserves to be reckoned among the divine ladies like Arundhatī. (7)

verses.text:
अलंकृतोऽयं देशश्च यत्र सौमित्रिणा सह।
वैदेह्या चानया राम वत्स्यसि त्वमरिंदम॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Nay, this region where you are going to stay, O Rāma, vanquisher of foes, together with the son of Sumitrā and this Sītā, stands graced today.” (8)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना राघवः संयताञ्जलिः।
उवाच प्रश्रितं वाक्यमृषिं दीप्तमिवानलम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by the sage, Rāghava, with folded hands, addressed the following polite words to the sage, who looked like a blazing fire : (9)

verses.text:
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे मुनिपुंगवः।
गुणैः सभ्रातृभार्यस्य गुरुर्नः परितुष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Blessed and favoured am I, with whose virtues as well as with those of my brother and wife, you, the foremost of sages and our object of veneration, are fully pleased. (10)

verses.text:
किं तु व्यादिश मे देशं सोदकं बहुकाननम्।
यत्राश्रमपदं कृत्वा वसेयं निरतः सुखम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “But please tell me the region, abounding in water and forests, where I can happily and joyously stay, setting up a hermitage.” (11)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीन्मुनिश्रेष्ठः श्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम्।
ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं धर्मात्मा ततोवाच वचः शुभम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Hearing the submission of Śrī Rāma, the righteous Agastya, the foremost of sages, meditated a while and then spoke the following auspicious words : (12)

verses.text:
इतो द्वियोजने तात बहुमूलफलोदकः।
देशो बहुमृगः श्रीमान् पञ्चवट्यभिविश्रुतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Two Yojanas (sixteen miles) from here, O dear one, is a splendid region abounding in roots, fruits and water, having many deer, and is known all round as Pañcavaṭī. (13)

verses.text:
तत्र गत्वाऽऽश्रमपदं कृत्वा सौमित्रिणा सह।
रमस्व त्वं पितुर्वाक्यं यथोक्तमनुपालयन्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Going there with Lakṣmaṇa and setting up a hermitage, live you all happily fully obeying to the letter the command of your father. (14)

verses.text:
विदितो ह्येष वृत्तान्तो मम सर्वस्तवानघ।
तपसश्च प्रभावेण स्नेहाद् दशरथस्य च॥ १५॥
verses.m: “O sinless one, all this story of yours’ as well as that of Daśaratha (your father) is known to me through the power of my austerities and by virtue of my affection to you all. (15)

verses.text:
हृदयस्थं च ते च्छन्दो विज्ञातं तपसा मया।
इह वासं प्रतिज्ञाय मया सह तपोवने॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I have also come to know the purpose in your mind in inquiring of me a place suitable for your abode after having agreed to stay in this penance-grove with me.(16)

verses.text:
अतश्च त्वामहं ब्रूमि गच्छ पञ्चवटीमिति।
स हि रम्यो वनोद्देशो मैथिली तत्र रंस्यते॥ १७॥
verses.m: “It is, therefore, that I say to you : ‘Go to Pañcavaṭī’. For, that part of the forest is charming. The princess of Mithilā will rejoice there. (17)

verses.text:
स देशः श्लाघनीयश्च नातिदूरे च राघव।
गोदावर्याः समीपे च मैथिली तत्र रंस्यते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “That region is commendable and also not very far off from this place, O Rāghava, and stands near the Godāvarī. The princess of Mithilā will feel delighted there. (18)

verses.text:
प्राज्यमूलफलैश्चैव नानाद्विजगणैर्युतः।
विविक्तश्च महाबाहो पुण्यो रम्यस्तथैव च॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Having abundant roots and fruits and full of diverse flocks of birds. O mighty-armed one, it is solitary, holy and charming as well. (19)

verses.text:
भवानपि सदाचारः शक्तश्च परिरक्षणे।
अपि चात्र वसन् राम तापसान् पालयिष्यसि॥ २०॥
verses.m: “You too are of good conduct and capable of protecting the weak. Nay, staying there, O Rāma, you will protect the ascetics. (20)

verses.text:
एतदालक्ष्यते वीर मधूकानां महावनम्।
उत्तरेणास्य गन्तव्यं न्यग्रोधमपि गच्छता॥ २१॥
verses.m: “O hero, here is seen the great forest of Madhūka trees; from there you have to proceed along the northern route leading to a banyan tree. (21)

verses.text:
ततः स्थलमुपारुह्य पर्वतस्याविदूरतः।
ख्यातः पञ्चवटीत्येव नित्यपुष्पितकाननः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Then, moving up a plateau, will be reached by you not far away from a mountain, a region full of woodlands, ever laden with blossoms and known by the name of Pañcavaṭī.” (22)

verses.text:
अगस्त्येनैवमुक्तस्तु रामः सौमित्रिणा सह।
सत्कृत्यामन्त्रयामास तमृषिं सत्यवादिनम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by Agastya, Rāma together with the son of Sumitrā honoured and took leave of that sage, who always spoke the truth. (23)

verses.text:
तौ तु तेनाभ्यनुज्ञातौ कृतपादाभिवन्दनौ।
तमाश्रमं पञ्चवटीं जग्मतुः सह सीतया॥ २४॥
verses.m: Permitted by him and having bowed down at his feet in reverence, the two brothers moved with Sītā towards the Pañcavaṭī hermitage. (24)

verses.text:
गृहीतचापौ तु नराधिपात्मजौ
विषक्ततूणी समरेष्वकातरौ।
यथोपदिष्टेन पथा महर्षिणा
प्रजग्मतुः पञ्चवटीं समाहितौ॥ २५॥
verses.m: With their quivers fastened at the back and wielding their bows, the two princes, who were of concentrated mind and fearless in battle, proceeded to Pañcavaṭī along the path as directed by the great sage. (25)

verses.text:
अथ पञ्चवटीं गच्छन्नन्तरा रघुनन्दनः।
आससाद महाकायं गृध्रं भीमपराक्रमम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Now, while going to Pañcavaṭī, the scion of Raghu met on the way a vulture with a gigantic body and possessed of terrific prowess. (1)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा तौ महाभागौ वनस्थं रामलक्ष्मणौ।
मेनाते राक्षसं पक्षिं ब्रुवाणौ को भवानिति॥ २॥
verses.m: Seeing him in the forest, those two highly blessed princes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, thought the bird to be an ogre and said to him, “Who are you?” (2)

verses.text:
ततो मधुरया वाचा सौम्यया प्रीणयन्निव।
उवाच वत्स मां विद्धि वयस्यं पितुरात्मनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then, as though delighting them with a gentle and sweet speech, he said, “O dear son, know me to be a friend of your father.” (3)

verses.text:
स तं पितृसखं मत्वा पूजयामास राघवः।
स तस्य कुलमव्यग्रमथ पप्रच्छ नाम च॥ ४॥
verses.m: Believing him to be a friend of his father, the scion of Raghu honoured him and gently enquired his name and race. (4)

verses.text:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा कुलमात्मानमेव च।
आचचक्षे द्विजस्तस्मै सर्वभूतसमुद्भवम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Rāma, the bird told him about himself and his descent and the origin of all beings. (5)

verses.text:
पूर्वकाले महाबाहो ये प्रजापतयोऽभवन्।
तान् मे निगदतः सर्वानादितः शृणु राघव॥ ६॥
verses.m: “O mighty-armed scion of Raghu, listen to me, while I am speaking from the beginning about all the lords of creation who existed in the past. (6)

verses.text:
कर्दमः प्रथमस्तेषां विकृतस्तदनन्तरम्।
शेषश्च संश्रयश्चैव बहुपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्॥ ७॥
स्थाणुर्मरीचिरत्रिश्च क्रतुश्चैव महाबलः।
पुलस्त्यश्चाङ्गिराश्चैव प्रचेताः पुलहस्तथा॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Kardama was the first of them; after him came Vikṛta, Śeṣa, Saṁśraya and the powerful Bahuputra and Sthāṇu, Marīci, Atri, the mighty Kratu, Pulastya, Aṅgirā, Pracetā and also Pulaha. (7-8)

verses.text:
दक्षो विवस्वानपरोऽरिष्टनेमिश्च राघव।
कश्यपश्च महातेजास्तेषामासीच्च पश्चिमः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Then came Dakṣa, Vivaswān and Ariṣṭanemi, O Rāghava, and the last one of great lustre amongst them was Kaśyapa. (9)

verses.text:
प्रजापतेस्तु दक्षस्य बभूवुरिति विश्रुताः।
षष्टिर्दुहितरो राम यशस्विन्यो महायशः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Prajāpati Dakṣa had sixty well-known and illustrious daughters, O Rāma of great fame ! (10)

verses.text:
कश्यपः प्रतिजग्राह तासामष्टौ सुमध्यमाः।
अदितिं च दितिं चैव दनूमपि च कालकाम्॥ ११॥
ताम्रां क्रोधवशां चैव मनुं चाप्यनलामपि।
तास्तु कन्यास्ततः प्रीतः कश्यपः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Kaśyapa married eight beautiful girls of them—Aditi and Diti, Danu and also Kālakā, Tāmrā and Krodhavaśā, Manu and also Analā. Then, pleased with them, Kaśyapa again said to those girls : (11-12)

verses.text:
पुत्रांस्त्रैलोक्यभर्तॄन् वै जनयिष्यथ मत्समान्।
अदितिस्तन्मना राम दितिश्च दनुरेव च॥ १३॥
कालका च महाबाहो शेषास्त्वमनसोऽभवन्।
अदित्यां जज्ञिरे देवास्त्रयस्तिं्रशदरिंदम॥ १४॥
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा अश्विनौ च परंतप।
दितिस्त्वजनयत् पुत्रान् दैत्यांस्तात यशस्विनः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “ ‘You will give birth to sons like me, masters of the three worlds.’ O Rāma of mighty arms, Aditi, Diti, Danu and Kālakā were attentive, the rest were indifferent. “Of Aditi thirty-three gods were born, O vanquisher of foes—the twelve Ādityas, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras and the two Aświns, O tormentor of foes ! Diti for her part gave birth to the famous Daityas (demons), O dear one ! (13—15)

verses.text:
तेषामियं वसुमती पुराऽऽसीत् सवनार्णवा।
दनुस्त्वजनयत् पुत्रमश्वग्रीवमरिंदम॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Formerly they owned all this earth with forests and oceans. Danu for her part bore a son, Aśwagrīva, O vanquisher of foes ! (16)

verses.text:
नरकं कालकं चैव कालकापि व्यजायत।
क्रौञ्चीं भासीं तथा श्येनीं धृतराष्ट्रीं तथा शुकीम्॥ १७॥
ताम्रा तु सुषुवे कन्याः पञ्चैता लोकविश्रुताः।
उलूकाञ्जनयत् क्रौञ्ची भासी भासान् व्यजायत॥ १८॥
श्येनी श्येनांश्च गृध्रांश्च व्यजायत सुतेजसः।
धृतराष्ट्री तु हंसांश्च कलहंसाश्च सर्वशः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Kālakā too gave birth to Naraka and also Kālaka. Tāmrā for her part bore the following five daughters well-known in the world—Krauñcī, Bhāsī as also Śyenī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrī and Śukī. Krauñcī gave birth to Ulūkas (owls), Bhāsī bore Bhāsas (a species of birds of prey), Śyenī gave birth to Śyenas (hawks) and vultures of bright lustre. Dhṛtarāṣṭrī for her part bore swans and Kalahaṁsas of all types. (17—19)

verses.text:
चक्रवाकांश्च भद्रं ते विजज्ञे सापि भामिनी।
शुकी नतां विजज्ञे तु नतायां विनता सुता॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Luck be to you ! That lady also gave birth to Cakravāka birds. Śukī bore a daughter, Natā by name, and of Natā was born a daughter, Vinatā. (20)

verses.text:
दश क्रोधवशा राम विजज्ञेऽप्यात्मसंभवाः।
मृगीं च मृगमन्दां च हरीं भद्रमदामपि॥ २१॥
मातङ्गीमथ शार्दूलीं श्वेतां च सुरभीं तथा।
सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नां सुरसां कद्रुकामपि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “O Rāma, Krodhavaśā also bore ten daughters—Mṛgī and Mṛgamandā, Harī as also Bhadramadā, Mātaṅgī and then Śārdūlī, Śwetā as also Surabhī, Surasā endowed with all auspicious characteristics and also Kadrū. (21-22)

verses.text:
अपत्यं तु मृगाः सर्वे मृग्या नरवरोत्तम।
ऋक्षाश्च मृगमन्दायाः सृमराश्चमरास्तथा॥ २३॥
verses.m: “O jewel among the foremost of men, all the deer are the progeny of Mṛgī; Ṛkṣas (bears), Sṛmaras (a species of antelopes) and camaras (another species of antelopes), of Mṛgamandā. (23)

verses.text:
ततस्त्विरावतीं नाम जज्ञे भद्रमदा सुताम्।
तस्यास्त्वैरावतः पुत्रो लोकनाथो महागजः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Then Bhadramadā bore a daughter named Irāvatī. The great elephant, Airāvata, coveted by the world, is her son. (24)

verses.text:
हर्याश्च हरयोऽपत्यं वानराश्च तपस्विनः।
गोलाङ्गूलाश्च शार्दूली व्याघ्रांश्चाजनयत् सुतान्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Lions and the poor monkeys and baboons are the progeny of Harī. Śārdūlī bore tigers as her sons. (25)

verses.text:
मातङ्ग्यास्त्वथ मातङ्गा अपत्यं मनुजर्षभ।
दिशागजं तु काकुत्स्थ श्वेता व्यजनयत् सुतम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “O jewel among men, the elephants are the progeny of Mātaṅgī; O Kākutstha ! Śwetā bore a son, Diśāgaja (the elephant guarding the quarters). (26)

verses.text:
ततो दुहितरौ राम सुरभिर्द्वे व्यजायत।
रोहिणीं नाम भद्रं ते गन्धर्वीं च यशस्विनीम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Then, O Rāma, Surabhi bore two daughters named Rohiṇī and the famous Gandharvī. Luck be to you ! (27)

verses.text:
रोहिण्यजनयद् गावो गन्धर्वी वाजिनः सुतान्।
सुरसाजनयन्नागान् राम कद्रूश्च पन्नगान्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Rohiṇī gave birth to the bovine race and Gandharvī to the horses as her sons. Surasā bore the Nāgas and Kadrū the serpents, O Rāma ! (28)

verses.text:
मनुर्मनुष्याञ्जनयत् कश्यपस्य महात्मनः।
ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियान् वैश्यान् शूद्रांश्च मनुजर्षभ॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Manu, wife of the high-souled Kaśyapa, gave birth to men—viz., Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras, O jewel among men ! (29)

verses.text:
मुखतो ब्राह्मणा जाता उरसः क्षत्रियास्तथा।
ऊरुभ्यां जज्ञिरे वैश्याः पद्भ्यां शूद्रा इति श्रुतिः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Brāhmaṇas appeared from the mouth, the Kṣatriyas from the breast, the Vaiśyas from the thighs and the Śūdras from the feet—so says the Śruti text. (30)

verses.text:
सर्वान् पुण्यफलान् वृक्षाननलापि व्यजायत।
विनता च शुकीपौत्री कद्रूश्च सुरसास्वसा॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Analā also gave birth to all the trees of holy fruits; Vinatā was the grand-daughter of Śukī (the daughter of Tāmrā) and Kadrū was the sister of Surasā. (31)

verses.text:
कद्रूर्नागसहस्रं तु विजज्ञे धरणीधरान्।
द्वौ पुत्रौ विनतायास्तु गरुडोऽरुण एव च॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Kadrū bore a thousand Nāgas, the supporters of the earth. Garuḍa and Aruṇa are the two sons of Vinatā. (32)

verses.text:
तस्माज्जातोऽहमरुणात् सम्पातिश्च ममाग्रजः।
जटायुरिति मां विद्धि श्येनीपुत्रमरिंदम॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “I came into being from the said Aruṇa, and also my elder brother, Sampāti. Know me to be Jaṭāyu, the son of Śyenī, O vanquisher of foes ! (33)

verses.text:
सोऽहं वाससहायस्ते भविष्यामि यदीच्छसि।
इदं दुर्गं हि कान्तारं मृगराक्षससेवितम्।
सीतां च तात रक्षिष्ये त्वयि याते सलक्ष्मणे॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “If you so desire, I shall be your assistant at your dwelling. For, this inaccessible forest is frequented by beasts and ogres; and, O dear one, when you go out with Lakṣmaṇa, I shall guard Sītā.” (34)

verses.text:
जटायुषं तु प्रतिपूज्य राघवो
मुदा परिष्वज्य च संनतोऽभवत्।
पितुर्हि शुश्राव सखित्वमात्मवा-
ञ्जटायुषा संकथितं पुनः पुनः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Rāghava honoured Jaṭāyu, embraced him with joy and bowed low to him; for, the self-restrained Rāma had heard about the vulture’s friendship with his father, Daśaratha, spoken of by Jaṭāyu again and again. (35)

verses.text:
स तत्र सीतां परिदाय मैथिलीं
सहैव तेनातिबलेन पक्षिणा।
जगाम तां पञ्चवटीं सलक्ष्मणो
रिपून् दिधक्षञ्शलभानिवानलः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Entrusting Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, to the care of Jaṭāyu, he proceeded to the well-known Pañcavaṭī, together with the selfsame mighty bird and Lakṣmaṇa, seeking, as it were, to burn the enemy as fire would burn moths. (36)

verses.text:
ततः पञ्चवटीं गत्वा नानाव्यालमृगायुताम्।
उवाच लक्ष्मणं रामो भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Then going to Pañcavaṭī full of various beasts of prey and deer, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa, his brother of bright lustre : (1)

verses.text:
आगताः स्म यथोद्दिष्टं यं देशं मुनिरब्रवीत्।
अयं पञ्चवटीदेशः सौम्य पुष्पितकाननः॥ २॥
verses.m: “According to our plan we have come to the region of which the sage spoke to us. O gentle brother, this is the region of Pañcavaṭī with woodlands in blossom. (2)

verses.text:
सर्वतश्चार्यतां दृष्टिः कानने निपुणो ह्यसि।
आश्रमः कतरस्मिन् नो देशे भवति सम्मतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Since you are a man of insight, cast a look all around in the forest: At which place will a hermitage be suitable for us? (3)

verses.text:
रमते यत्र वैदेही त्वमहं चैव लक्ष्मण।
तादृशो दृश्यतां देशः संनिकृष्टजलाशयः॥ ४॥
वनरामण्यकं यत्र जलरामण्यकं तथा।
संनिकृष्टं च यस्मिंस्तु समित्पुष्पकुशोदकम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Look about for a site with a pool nearby, in which the princess of Videha, yourself and I will feel delighted, where there is beauty of forest and beauty of water, and also in the vicinity of which there are firewood, flowers, the holy Kuśa grass and water.” (4-5)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः संयताञ्जलिः।
सीतासमक्षं काकुत्स्थमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa with folded hands spoke as follows to Kākutstha in the presence of Sītā : (6)

verses.text:
परवानस्मि काकुत्स्थ त्वयि वर्षशतं स्थिते।
स्वयं तु रुचिरे देशे क्रियतामिति मां वद॥ ७॥
verses.m: “O Kākutstha, so long as you are present, say, a hundred years, I am a dependent only. Therefore, tell me of your own accord to erect a hut at a place which is agreeable to you.” (7)

verses.text:
सुप्रीतस्तेन वाक्येन लक्ष्मणस्य महाद्युतिः।
विमृशन् रोचयामास देशं सर्वगुणान्वितम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Very much pleased by this reply of Lakṣmaṇa and thinking for a while, Śrī Rāma of surpassing lustre, selected a spot, possessed of all good qualities. (8)

verses.text:
स तं रुचिरमाक्रम्य देशमाश्रमकर्मणि।
हस्ते गृहीत्वा हस्तेन रामः सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: He went to that spot selected for setting up a hermitage and clasping Lakṣmaṇa by the hand, Śrī Rāma said to the son of Sumitrā : (9)

verses.text:
अयं देशः समः श्रीमान् पुष्पितैस्तरुभिर्वृतः।
इहाश्रमपदं रम्यं यथावत् कर्तुमर्हसि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “This plot is even, grand and surrounded by trees in blossom. Here you ought duly to set up a beautiful hermitage. (10)

verses.text:
इयमादित्यसंकाशैः पद्मैः सुरभिगन्धिभिः।
अदूरे दृश्यते रम्या पद्मिनी पद्मशोभिता॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Here is seen nearby a lake looking delightful with fragrant sun-like lotuses and further beautified by blue lotuses. (11)

verses.text:
यथाख्यातमगस्त्येन मुनिना भावितात्मना।
इयं गोदावरी रम्या पुष्पितैस्तरुभिर्वृता॥ १२॥
verses.m: “As pointed out by sage Agastya, the pure-minded sage, this is the site of charming Godāvarī, hemmed with trees in blossom. (12)

verses.text:
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा चक्रवाकोपशोभिता।
नातिदूरे न चासन्ने मृगयूथनिपीडिता॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Crowded with swans and Kāraṇḍava birds, beautified by Caravāka birds and stirred by herds of deer, it is neither very far nor very near. (13)

verses.text:
मयूरनादिता रम्याः प्रांशवो बहुकन्दराः।
दृश्यन्ते गिरयः सौम्य फुल्लैस्तरुभिरावृताः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Here are seen lofty and charming mountains made noisy by peacocks, having many caves and covered with trees, in blossom, O gentle Lakṣmaṇa ! (14)

verses.text:
सौवर्णै राजतैस्ताम्रैर्देशे देशे तथा शुभैः।
गवाक्षिता इवाभान्ति गजाः परमभक्तिभिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Speckled here and there with shining golden, silvery and coppery minerals, they look like elephants decorated with exquisite coloured diagrams resembling latticed windows. (15)

verses.text:
सालैस्तालैस्तमालैश्च खर्जूरैः पनसैर्द्रुमैः।
नीवारैस्तिनिशैश्चैव पुन्नागैश्चोपशोभिताः॥ १६॥
चूतैरशोकैस्तिलकैः केतकैरपि चम्पकैः।
पुष्पगुल्मलतोपेतैस्तैस्तैस्तरुभिरावृताः ॥ १७॥
स्यन्दनैश्चन्दनैर्नीपैः पर्णासैर्लकुचैरपि।
धवाश्वकर्णखदिरैः शमीकिंशुकपाटलैः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “The mountains are graced with Sāl, palmyra, Tamāla, date, jack-fruit, Nīvāra (watery Kadamba), Tiniśa and Punnāga trees and covered by mango, Aśoka, Tilaka, Ketaka, Campaka, Syandana, sandalwood, Nīpa, Parṇāsa, Lakuca, Dhava, Aśwakarṇa, Khadira, Śamī, Kiṁśuka and Pāṭala trees laden with blossoms and surrounded with shrubs and climbers. (16—18)

verses.text:
इदं पुण्यमिदं रम्यमिदं बहुमृगद्विजम्।
इह वत्स्याम सौमित्रे सार्धमेतेन पक्षिणा॥ १९॥
verses.m: “This spot is holy, this is charming, this abounds in deer and birds, O son of Sumitrā ! We will stay here with this bird (Jaṭāyu).” (19)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।
अचिरेणाश्रमं भ्रातुश्चकार सुमहाबलः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of hostile warriors, possessed as he was of extraordinary might, set up a hermitage for his brother without delay. (20)

verses.text:
पर्णशालां सुविपुलां तत्र संघातमृत्तिकाम्।
सुस्तम्भां मस्करैर्दीर्घैः कृतवंशां सुशोभनाम्॥ २१॥
शमीशाखाभिरास्तीर्य दृढपाशावपाशिताम्।
कुशकाशशरैः पर्णैः सुपरिच्छादितां तथा॥ २२॥
समीकृततलां रम्यां चकार सुमहाबलः।
निवासं राघवस्यार्थे प्रेक्षणीयमनुत्तमम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa, who was possessed of extraordinary might, erected a lovely and excellent abode for Śrī Rāma in the shape of a very extensive hut with a wall of mud supported on good pillars and roofed with long bamboo sticks, and looking very attractive and charming, thatching it with boughs of a Śamī tree, fastened with strong cords and also well covered with blades of Kuśa and flowers of Kāśa grass and reeds and levelling the floor. (21—23)

verses.text:
स गत्वा लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान् नदीं गोदावरीं तदा।
स्नात्वा पद्मानि चादाय सफलः पुनरागतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: The glorious Lakṣmaṇa forthwith went to the river Godāvarī, bathed in it and taking lotuses and fruits returned. (24)

verses.text:
ततः पुष्पबलिं कृत्वा शान्तिं च स यथाविधि।
दर्शयामास रामाय तदाश्रमपदं कृतम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Then, making a flower-offering and performing a propitiatory rite with due ceremony, he showed the hermitage, which he had duly set up, to Śrī Rāma. (25)

verses.text:
स तं दृष्ट्वा कृतं सौम्यमाश्रमं सह सीतया।
राघवः पर्णशालायां हर्षमाहारयत् परम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Seeing that delightful hermitage set up for him, the said Śrī Rāma with Sītā derived supreme joy in that cottage. (26)

verses.text:
सुसंहृष्टः परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां लक्ष्मणं तदा।
अतिस्निग्धं च गाढं च वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Being supremely delighted and tightly clasping Lakṣmaṇa with his arms most affectionately, Śrī Rāma then sopke to him as follows : (27)

verses.text:
प्रीतोऽस्मि ते महत् कर्म त्वया कृतमिदं प्रभो।
प्रदेयो यन्निमित्तं ते परिष्वङ्गो मया कृतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “I am pleased with you. O powerful brother, you have accomplished this great work, as a reward for which I have given you a well-deserved embrace. (28)

verses.text:
भावज्ञेन कृतज्ञेन धर्मज्ञेन च लक्ष्मण।
त्वया पुत्रेण धर्मात्मा न संवृत्तः पिता मम॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Lakṣmaṇa, with you as his son, knowing my feelings, grateful and a knower of what is right, my pious-minded father is not dead.” (29)

verses.text:
एवं लक्ष्मणमुक्त्वा तु राघवो लक्ष्मिवर्धनः।
तस्मिन् देशे बहुफले न्यवसत् स सुखं सुखी॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having thus spoken to Lakṣmaṇa, the happy Rāghava, the promoter of others’ grandeur, stayed in that region of abundant fruits happily. (30)

verses.text:
कञ्चित् कालं स धर्मात्मा सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च।
अन्वास्यमानो न्यवसत् स्वर्गलोके यथामरः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Attended upon by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, that righteous prince stayed for some period like a god in heaven. (31)

verses.text:
वसतस्तस्य तु सुखं राघवस्य महात्मनः।
शरद्व्यपाये हेमन्त ऋतुरिष्टः प्रवर्तत॥ १॥
verses.m: While the magnanimous Rāghava was staying happily, the desired winter set in at the expiry of autumn. (1)

verses.text:
स कदाचित् प्रभातायां शर्वर्यां रघुनन्दनः।
प्रययावभिषेकार्थं रम्यां गोदावरीं नदीम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Once that delight of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, at the break of day went to the beautiful Godāvarī river for a bath. (2)

verses.text:
प्रह्वः कलशहस्तस्तु सीतया सह वीर्यवान्।
पृष्ठतोऽनुव्रजन् भ्राता सौमित्रिरिदमब्रवीत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Following at the heels of Śrī Rāma, his brave brother, the son of Sumitrā, alongwith Sītā, and with a vessel for water in his hand, spoke as follows : (3)

verses.text:
अयं स कालः सम्प्राप्तः प्रियो यस्ते प्रियंवद।
अलंकृत इवाभाति येन संवत्सरः शुभः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Now has arrived that season which is dear to you, O polite brother, with which the blessed year appears as though ornamented. (4)

verses.text:
नीहारपरुषो लोकः पृथिवी सस्यमालिनी।
जलान्यनुपभोग्यानि सुभगो हव्यवाहनः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The people feel dry with cold, the earth is rich with crops; the waters are unenjoyable, the fire is agreeable. (5)

verses.text:
नवाग्रयणपूजाभिरभ्यर्च्य पितृदेवताः।
कृताग्रयणकाः काले सन्तो विगतकल्मषाः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Having propitiated the manes and gods with offerings of the first fruits of the preceding harvest and partaken of them themselves, virtuous people have been rid of sin. (6)

verses.text:
प्राज्यकामा जनपदाः सम्पन्नतरगोरसाः।
विचरन्ति महीपाला यात्रार्थं विजिगीषवः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The people of the countryside have their desires for foodgrains abandantly fulfilled and have richer supply of cow’s milk etc. The kings are moving on their expedition with the desire for conquest. (7)

verses.text:
सेवमाने दृढं सूर्ये दिशमन्तकसेविताम्।
विहीनतिलकेव स्त्री नोत्तरा दिक् प्रकाशते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “As the sun firmly adheres to the quarter inhabited by the god of Death (viz., the south), the northern quarter looks no more charming than a lady without Tilaka (an auspicious mark on the forehead). (8)

verses.text:
प्रकृत्या हिमकोशाढ्यो दूरसूर्यश्च साम्प्रतम्।
यथार्थनामा सुव्यक्तं हिमवान् हिमवान् गिरिः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Rich in its treasure of snow by nature, and abounding in snow at present, the sun being away (in the southern hemisphere), the Himālaya mountain more perceptibly justifies its name. (9)

verses.text:
अत्यन्तसुखसंचारा मध्याह्ने स्पर्शतः सुखाः।
दिवसाः सुभगादित्याश्छायासलिलदुर्भगाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “At noontide the days are exceedingly pleasant for a walk, and afford delight by the touch of the sun’s rays; the sun is agreeable, while shade and water are disagreeable. (10)

verses.text:
मृदुसूर्याः सुनीहाराः पटुशीताः समारुताः।
शून्यारण्या हिमध्वस्ता दिवसा भान्ति साम्प्रतम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “With an unoppressive sun, beautiful thick fog, bitter cold and wind and desolate woodlands blighted by frost, the days look calm (devoid of activity and bustle). (11)

verses.text:
निवृत्ताकाशशयनाः पुष्यनीता हिमारुणाः।
शीतवृद्धतरायामास्त्रियामा यान्ति साम्प्रतम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The nights now preclude repose in open air, are marked with the presence of the constellation known by the name of Puṣya, look dusty with frost, and become colder and longer. (12)

verses.text:
रविसंक्रान्तसौभाग्यस्तुषारारुणमण्डलः।
निःश्वासान्ध इवादर्शश्चन्द्रमा न प्रकाशते॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Having transferred her pleasantness to the sun, and with its orb looking reddish due to snow, the moon does not shine any more than a mirror soiled with exhalation. (13)

verses.text:
ज्योत्स्ना तुषारमलिना पौर्णमास्यां न राजते।
सीतेव चातपश्यामा लक्ष्यते न च शोभते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Even on a full-moon day the moonlight does not look bright, obscured as it is with frost even as Sītā appears tanned with the sun and does not look as attractive as earlier. (14)

verses.text:
प्रकृत्या शीतलस्पर्शो हिमविद्धश्च साम्प्रतम्।
प्रवाति पश्चिमो वायुः काले द्विगुणशीतलः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Cool to the touch by its very nature and now saturated with snow the westerly wind blows doubly cold in the morning. (15)

verses.text:
बाष्पच्छन्नान्यरण्यानि यवगोधूमवन्ति च।
शोभन्तेऽभ्युदिते सूर्ये नदद्भिः क्रौञ्चसारसैः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Shrouded in mist and rich with crops of barley and wheat, the woodlands look attractive at sunrise with noisy herons and cranes. (16)

verses.text:
खर्जूरपुष्पाकृतिभिः शिरोभिः पूर्णतण्डुलैः।
शोभन्ते किंचिदालम्बाः शालयः कनकप्रभाः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Wearing a golden lustre and slightly bent with their weight of corn, paddy crops look charming with their ears full of corn and resembling date flowers in appearance. (17)

verses.text:
मयूखैरुपसर्पद्भिर्हिमनीहारसंवृतैः।
दूरमभ्युदितः सूर्यः शशाङ्क इव लक्ष्यते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “With its approaching rays wrapped in frost and fog, the sun, though risen high, looks like the moon. (18)

verses.text:
आग्राह्यवीर्यः पूर्वाह्णे मध्याह्ने स्पर्शतः सुखः।
संरक्तः किंचिदापाण्डुरातपः शोभते क्षितौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: “With its glory faintly perceptible in the forenoon and agreeable to the touch at noon, the sunshine, which is partially bright red and partially pale, is spreading its charm on the earth. (19)

verses.text:
अवश्यायनिपातेन किंचित्प्रक्लिन्नशाद्वला।
वनानां शोभते भूमिर्निविष्टतरुणातपा॥ २०॥
verses.m: “With its grass slightly drenched with dew-drops, the land of the woods penetrated as it is with the morning sunshine, looks charming. (20)

verses.text:
स्पृशन् सुविपुलं शीतमुदकं द्विरदः सुखम्।
अत्यन्ततृषितो वन्यः प्रतिसंहरते करम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Though touching for the sake of gratification the excessively cold water of a pool, the wild elephant, seized as it was with extreme thirst, withdraws its trunk (due to its cold touch). (21)

verses.text:
एते हि समुपासीना विहगा जलचारिणः।
नावगाहन्ति सलिलमप्रगल्भा इवाहवम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Though standing very close to water, the aquatic birds do not actually dive into it even as the pusillanimous do not plunge into a fight though standing very close to the scene of fighting. (22)

verses.text:
अवश्यायतमोनद्धा नीहारतमसावृताः।
प्रसुप्ता इव लक्ष्यन्ते विपुष्पा वनराजयः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Covered with dewdrops and enveloped in darkness at night and shrouded in the dark occasioned by fog, the rows of forest trees bereft of their blossom appear as though buried in slumber. (23)

verses.text:
बाष्पसंछन्नसलिला रुतविज्ञेयसारसाः।
हिमार्द्रवालुकैस्तीरैः सरितो भान्ति साम्प्रतम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “With their water shrouded in mist and the cranes inhabiting them, discernible only by their cries, the streams are perceptible at this time only through their banks with their sands wet with frost. (24)

verses.text:
तुषारपतनाच्चैव मृदुत्वाद् भास्करस्य च।
शैत्यादगाग्रस्थमपि प्रायेण रसवज्जलम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Due to cold occasioned by the fall of frost as also the mildness of the sun, the water even on mountain-tops is generally tasty. (25)

verses.text:
जराजर्जरितैः पत्रैः शीर्णकेसरकर्णिकैः।
नालशेषा हिमध्वस्ता न भान्ति कमलाकराः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “With their lotuses worn out due to decay and their filaments and pericarps withered, the lotus-beds, blasted as they are by snow, are reduced to mere stalks and no longer look charming. (26)

verses.text:
अस्मिंस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्र काले दुःखसमन्वितः।
तपश्चरति धर्मात्मा त्वद्भक्त्या भरतः पुरे॥ २७॥
verses.m: “At this time of the year, O tiger among men, the pious-minded Bharata, full of agony (caused by separation from you) is practising austerities in the city out of devotion to you. (27)

verses.text:
त्यक्त्वा राज्यं च मानं च भोगांश्च विविधान् बहून्।
तपस्वी नियताहारः शेते शीते महीतले॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Giving up the sovereignty and honour as well as the manifold and diverse enjoyments and living on a restricted diet, the ascetic reposes on the cold surface of the earth. (28)

verses.text:
सोऽपि वेलामिमां नूनमभिषेकार्थमुद्यतः।
वृतः प्रकृतिभिर्नित्यं प्रयाति सरयूं नदीम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Ready for a dip in the river, and followed by his ministers, he too without doubt walks to the Sarayū river daily at this hour. (29)

verses.text:
अत्यन्तसुखसंवृद्धः सुकुमारो हिमार्दितः।
कथं त्वपररात्रेषु सरयूमवगाहते॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Tormented by cold, though brought up in the highest luxury and tender as he is, how indeed does he take a dip in the Sarayū during the last watch of the night? (30)

verses.text:
पद्मपत्रेक्षणः श्यामः श्रीमान् निरुदरो महान्।
धर्मज्ञः सत्यवादी च ह्रीनिषेवी जितेन्द्रियः॥ ३१॥
प्रियाभिभाषी मधुरो दीर्घबाहुररिंदमः।
संत्यज्य विविधान् सौख्यानार्यं सर्वात्मनाश्रितः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “With his eyes resembling the petals of a lotus, dark-brown of complexion, majestic, almost without a belly, a great knower of Dharma, truthful, bashful, master of his senses, polite of expression, amiable, long-armed, the subduer of enemies, he has given up the various pleasures and is devoted to you (his elder brother) with all his being. (31-32)

verses.text:
जितः स्वर्गस्तव भ्रात्रा भरतेन महात्मना।
वनस्थमपि तापस्ये यस्त्वामनुविधीयते॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Paradise has been conquered by your high-souled brother, Bharata, who is following you in your ascetic life, even though you are staying in the forest (away from him). (33)

verses.text:
न पित्र्यमनुवर्तन्ते मातृकं द्विपदा इति।
ख्यातो लोकप्रवादोऽयं भरतेनान्यथा कृतः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “The well-known popular saying that men follow the nature of their mother and not of their father has been belied by Bharata. (34)

verses.text:
भर्ता दशरथो यस्याः साधुश्च भरतः सुतः।
कथं नु साम्बा कैकेयी तादृशी क्रूरदर्शिनी॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “How is it that mother Kaikeyī, whose husband was Daśaratha and whose son is the virtuous Bharata, wears such a cruel aspect?” (35)

verses.text:
इत्येवं लक्ष्मणे वाक्यं स्नेहाद् वदति धार्मिके।
परिवादं जनन्यास्तमसहन् राघवोऽब्रवीत्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Unable to endure such condemnation of his (step-) mother, while the righteous Lakṣmaṇa was speaking as above out of affection (for Śrī Rāma), Rāghava said : (36)

verses.text:
न तेऽम्बा मध्यमा तात गर्हितव्या कदाचन।
तामेवेक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य भरतस्य कथां कुरु॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Dear brother, Kaikeyī, our second mother, should never be condemned by you. Speak exclusively about that Bharata, the king of the Ikṣvākus. (37)

verses.text:
निश्चितैव हि मे बुद्धिर्वनवासे दृढव्रता।
भरतस्नेहसंतप्ता बालिशीक्रियते पुनः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “To be sure, my mind is intent on my vow of residing in the forest alone, and is of firm resolve; yet, being agonized by Bharata’s affection, it gets infatuated once more. (38)

verses.text:
संस्मराम्यस्य वाक्यानि प्रियाणि मधुराणि च।
हृद्यान्यमृतकल्पानि मनःप्रह्लादनानि च॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “I fully recollect his agreeable, sweet, affectionate, nectar-like and soul-ravishing words. (39)

verses.text:
कदा ह्यहं समेष्यामि भरतेन महात्मना।
शत्रुघ्नेन च वीरेण त्वया च रघुनन्दन॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “When shall I actually be united with the high-souled Bharata, the heroic Śatrughna, together with you, O scion of Raghu?” (40)

verses.text:
इत्येवं विलपंस्तत्र प्राप्य गोदावरीं नदीम्।
चक्रेऽभिषेकं काकुत्स्थः सानुजः सह सीतया॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Discoursing thus on the aforesaid topic and reaching the river Godāvarī, Śrī Rāma with his younger brother and Sītā bathed in it. (41)

verses.text:
तर्पयित्वाथ सलिलैस्तैः पितॄन् दैवतानपि।
स्तुवन्ति स्मोदितं सूर्यं देवताश्च तथानघाः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Having propitiated with those waters the manes as well as the gods, the sinless trio then glorified the shining sun and the other gods as well. (42)

verses.text:
कृताभिषेकः स रराज रामः
सीताद्वितीयः सह लक्ष्मणेन।
कृताभिषेकस्त्वगराजपुत्र्या
रुद्रः सनन्दिर्भगवानिवेशः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Having finished his bath, Śrī Rāma shone with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa even as Lord Śiva (the Destroyer of the universe) with Nandī (His beloved associate) and Pārvatī (the Daughter of the lord of mountains) on having concluded His bath in the Gaṅgā. (43)

verses.text:
कृताभिषेको रामस्तु सीता सौमित्रिरेव च।
तस्माद् गोदावरीतीरात् ततो जग्मुः स्वमाश्रमम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having taken their bath, Rāma, Sītā and also Lakṣmaṇa then returned to their hermitage from the aforesaid bank of the Godāvarī. (1)

verses.text:
आश्रमं तमुपागम्य राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः।
कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकं कर्म पर्णशालामुपागमत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Having reached that hermitage on performing the morning devotions, Rāghava with Lakṣmaṇa entered his hut thatched with leaves. (2)

verses.text:
उवास सुखितस्तत्र पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः।
स रामः पर्णशालायामासीनः सह सीतया॥ ३॥
विरराज महाबाहुश्चित्रया चन्द्रमा इव।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा चकार विविधाः कथाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Being honoured by great sages, he stayed happily there. Seated with Sītā in that hut thatched with leaves, the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma shone brightly like the moon accompanied with the constellation Citrā, and discussed various topics with his brother, Lakṣmaṇa. (3-4)

verses.text:
तदासीनस्य रामस्य कथासंसक्तचेतसः।
तं देशं राक्षसी काचिदाजगाम यदृच्छया॥ ५॥
verses.m: While Śrī Rāma was seated there, his mind engrossed in talk, a certain ogress visited that region by chance. (5)

verses.text:
सा तु शूर्पणखा नाम दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः।
भगिनी राममासाद्य ददर्श त्रिदशोपमम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Having arrived there, the aforesaid sister of the ogre Rāvaṇa, (who was endowed with ten heads), Śūrpaṇakhā (whose nails resembled a winnowing basket) beheld Śrī Rāma, who looked like a god. (6)

verses.text:
दीप्तास्यं च महाबाहुं पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणम्।
गजविक्रान्तगमनं जटामण्डलधारिणम्॥ ७॥
सुकुमारं महासत्त्वं पार्थिवव्यञ्जनान्वितम्।
राममिन्दीवरश्यामं कंदर्पसदृशप्रभम्॥ ८॥
बभूवेन्द्रोपमं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसी काममोहिता।
सुमुखं दुर्मुखी रामं वृत्तमध्यं महोदरी॥ ९॥
विशालाक्षं विरूपाक्षी सुकेशं ताम्रमूर्धजा।
प्रियरूपं विरूपा सा सुस्वरं भैरवस्वना॥ १०॥
तरुणं दारुणा वृद्धा दक्षिणं वामभाषिणी।
न्यायवृत्तं सुदुर्वृत्ता प्रियमप्रियदर्शना॥ ११॥
शरीरजसमाविष्टा राक्षसी राममब्रवीत्।
जटी तापसवेषेण सभार्यः शरचापधृक्॥ १२॥
आगतस्त्वमिमं देशं कथं राक्षससेवितम्।
किमागमनकृत्यं ते तत्त्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: Seeing Śrī Rāma with a radiant countenance, mighty arms, eyes large like the petals of a lotus, and a majestic gait like that of an elephant, wearing a rounded mass of matted hair, tender, yet possessed of extraordinary strength, endowed with the bodily marks of a monarch, cerulean like a blue lotus, having a splendour similar to that of Cupid and looking like Indra (the ruler of gods), the ogress got infatuated with love. Overcome with passion, the ogress, who had an ugly face, large belly, deformed eyes, coppery hair, was misshapen, had a frightful voice, was hard-hearted and aged, spoke adversely, was extremely vile of conduct and had a repelling aspect, spoke as follows to Śrī Rāma, who had a charming face, a slender waist, large eyes, beautiful locks, a pleasing aspect and a sweet voice, was youthful and candid, of right conduct and amiable : “Wearing matted locks and dressed in an ascetic garb, wielding a bow and arrows and accompanied with your wife, how have you come to this region frequented by ogres? What is the object of your visit? Be pleased to relate that.” (7—13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु राक्षस्या शूर्पणख्या परंतपः।
ऋजुबुद्धितया सर्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे॥ १४॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by the ogress Śūrpaṇakhā, Śrī Rāma (the tormentor of foes) proceeded to narrate everything, possessed as he was of a guileless mind : (14)

verses.text:
आसीद् दशरथो नाम राजा त्रिदशविक्रमः।
तस्याहमग्रजः पुत्रो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “There was a king named Daśaratha, possessing the prowess of gods. I am his eldest son, known among the people by the name of Rāma. (15)

verses.text:
भ्रातायं लक्ष्मणो नाम यवीयान् मामनुव्रतः।
इयं भार्या च वैदेही मम सीतेति विश्रुता॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Here is my younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa by name, devoted to me, and here is my wife, the princess of Videha, known by the name of Sītā. (16)

verses.text:
नियोगात् तु नरेन्द्रस्य पितुर्मातुश्च यन्त्रितः।
धर्मार्थं धर्मकांक्षी च वनं वस्तुमिहागतः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Fettered by the command of my father, the king, and my mother (Kaikeyī), and seeking to discharge my sacred obligation to them and in order to practise virtue in the form of austerities, I have come to stay in this forest. (17)

verses.text:
त्वां तु वेदितुमिच्छामि कस्य त्वं कासि कस्य वा।
त्वं हि तावन्मनोज्ञाङ्गी राक्षसी प्रतिभासि मे॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I, for my part, desire to know you. Whose daughter are you? What is your name and whose wife are you? Possessed as you are of charming limbs, you appear to me to be an ogress (capable of assuming any form at will) on the face of it. (18)

verses.text:
इह वा किंनिमित्तं त्वमागता ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः।
साब्रवीद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसी मदनार्दिता॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Tell me truly what for you have come here.” Stricken with love to hear this, the ogress in question replied as follows : (19)

verses.text:
श्रूयतां राम तत्त्वार्थं वक्ष्यामि वचनं मम।
अहं शूर्पणखा नाम राक्षसी कामरूपिणी॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Hear my word, O Rāma ! I shall give out to you the real truth. I am an ogress, Śūrpaṇakhā by name, and capable of assuming any form at will. (20)

verses.text:
अरण्यं विचरामीदमेका सर्वभयंकरा।
रावणो नाम मे भ्राता यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Causing fear to all, I haunt this forest alone. I have a brother, Rāvaṇa by name; I wonder if his name has ever reached your ears. (21)

verses.text:
वीरो विश्रवसः पुत्रो यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः।
प्रवृद्धनिद्रश्च सदा कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “He is a valiant son of Viśravā, if you have ever heard of him. The very mighty Kumbhakarṇa too, who is given to excessive sleep, is my brother. (22)

verses.text:
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा न तु राक्षसचेष्टितः।
प्रख्यातवीर्यौ च रणे भ्रातरौ खरदूषणौ॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Vibhīṣaṇa, my third brother, for his part, is pious-minded; he has none of the activities of an ogre. Again, my other two brothers, Khara and Dūṣaṇa, are well-known for their valour on the battlefield. (23)

verses.text:
तानहं समतिक्रान्तां राम त्वापूर्वदर्शनात्।
समुपेतास्मि भावेन भर्तारं पुरुषोत्तमम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “I definitely surpass them all in point of valour, O Rāma ! Ever since I saw you for the first time, I have sought you, the foremost among men, as my husband in my mind. (24)

verses.text:
अहं प्रभावसम्पन्ना स्वच्छन्दबलगामिनी।
चिराय भव भर्ता मे सीतया किं करिष्यसि॥ २५॥
verses.m: “I am richly endowed with power. I am able to range at will by dint of my strength. Therefore, be my husband for long. What can you hope to accomplish with Sītā as your partner? (25)

verses.text:
विकृता च विरूपा च न सेयं सदृशी तव।
अहमेवानुरूपा ते भार्यारूपेण पश्य माम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Being deformed and ugly too, she is not worthy of you. I alone stand as a match for you. Look upon me as your wife. (26)

verses.text:
इमां विरूपामसतीं करालां निर्णतोदरीम्।
अनेन सह ते भ्रात्रा भक्षयिष्यामि मानुषीम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Alongwith this brother of yours I shall devour this ugly, vile, hideous human lady with a sunken belly. (27)

verses.text:
ततः पर्वतशृङ्गाणि वनानि विविधानि च।
पश्यन् सह मया कामी दण्डकान् विचरिष्यसि॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Then, beholding the peaks of mountains and forests of every description, you full of concupiscence will wander with me through the Daṇḍaka forest.” (28)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्तः काकुत्स्थः प्रहस्य मदिरेक्षणाम्।
इदं वचनमारेभे वक्तुं वाक्यविशारदः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words and laughing heartily, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), who was an adept in expression, proceeded to reply as follows to that woman with love-intoxicated eyes : (29)

verses.text:
तां तु शूर्पणखां रामः कामपाशावपाशिताम्।
स्वेच्छया श्लक्ष्णया वाचा स्मितपूर्वमथाब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: To the aforesaid Śūrpaṇakhā, bound by the cords of love, Śrī Rāma then spoke with a smile in sweet words as follows according to his own liking : (1)

verses.text:
कृतदारोऽस्मि भवति भार्येयं दयिता मम।
त्वद्विधानां तु नारीणां सुदुःखा ससपत्नता॥ २॥
verses.m: “O lady, I am already married. Here is my beloved wife. For ladies like you the presence of a co-wife is most painful. (2)

verses.text:
अनुजस्त्वेष मे भ्राता शीलवान् प्रियदर्शनः।
श्रीमानकृतदारश्च लक्ष्मणो नाम वीर्यवान्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Of course, here is my younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa by name, of good conduct, lovely to look at, glorious and brave and has not got a wife with him. (3)

verses.text:
अपूर्वी भार्यया चार्थी तरुणः प्रियदर्शनः।
अनुरूपश्च ते भर्ता रूपस्यास्य भविष्यति॥ ४॥
verses.m: “He is possessed of unique qualities, young and pleasing of aspect, and will prove to be a husband worthy of this comely form of yours if he seeks to obtain a wife. (4)

verses.text:
एनं भज विशालाक्षि भर्तारं भ्रातरं मम।
असपत्ना वरारोहे मेरुमर्कप्रभा यथा॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Accept this brother of mine as your husband, O large eyed and charming lady, without a rival even as sunlight woos Mount Meru.” (5)

verses.text:
इति रामेण सा प्रोक्ता राक्षसी काममोहिता।
विसृज्य रामं सहसा ततो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Leaving Rāma, when spoken to in these words by Śrī Rāma, the aforesaid ogress, infatuated as she was through love, suddenly spoke to Lakṣmaṇa as follows : (6)

verses.text:
अस्य रूपस्य ते युक्ता भार्याहं वरवर्णिनी।
मया सह सुखं सर्वान् दण्डकान् विचरिष्यसि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Possessing as I do an excellent complexion, I shall be a wife worthy of this comely form of yours. You will happily wander through the entire range of the Daṇḍaka forest with me.” (7)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्री राक्षस्या वाक्यकोविदः।
ततः शूर्पनखीं स्मित्वा लक्ष्मणो युक्तमब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words by the ogress, Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, who was an adept in expression, smilingly made the following just reply to Śūrpaṇakhā : (8)

verses.text:
कथं दासस्य मे दासी भार्या भवितुमिच्छसि।
सोऽहमार्येण परवान् भ्रात्रा कमलवर्णिनि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “How do you seek to turn a maid-servant by becoming a wife to me, a slave, possessing as you do the hue of a red lotus? I am only dependent on my worthy brother. (9)

verses.text:
समृद्धार्थस्य सिद्धार्था मुदितामलवर्णिनी।
आर्यस्य त्वं विशालाक्षि भार्या भव यवीयसी॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Become you, O large-eyed lady, a happy younger wife of spotless complexion of my elder brother, who is fully endowed with all riches, and be accomplished of purpose thereby. (10)

verses.text:
एतां विरूपामसतीं करालां निर्णतोदरीम्।
भार्यां वृद्धां परित्यज्य त्वामेवैष भजिष्यति॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Giving up for good this deformed, vile, hideous and aged wife with a sunken belly, he will accept you alone. (11)

verses.text:
को हि रूपमिदं श्रेष्ठं संत्यज्य वरवर्णिनि।
मानुषीषु वरारोहे कुर्याद् भावं विचक्षणः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Abandoning this excellent form of yours, what wise man indeed would fasten his love on human ladies, O charming lady with an excellent complexion?” (12)

verses.text:
इति सा लक्ष्मणेनोक्ता कराला निर्णतोदरी।
मन्यते तद्वचः सत्यं परिहासाविचक्षणा॥ १३॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words by Lakṣmaṇa, that hideous woman with a prominent belly, who was too naive to catch the jest, took his words to be true. (13)

verses.text:
सा रामं पर्णशालायामुपविष्टं परंतपम्।
सीतया सह दुर्धर्षमब्रवीत् काममोहिता॥ १४॥
verses.m: Infatuated through love, she spoke once more to Rāma, the tormentor of his foes, who was hard to overpower, and was sitting in the hut thatched with leaves in the company of Sītā: (14)

verses.text:
इमां विरूपामसतीं करालां निर्णतोदरीम्।
वृद्धां भार्यामवष्टभ्य न मां त्वं बहु मन्यसे॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Clinging to this old, deformed, vile, hideous and aged wife with a sunken belly, you do not make much of me. (15)

verses.text:
अद्येमां भक्षयिष्यामि पश्यतस्तव मानुषीम्।
त्वया सह चरिष्यामि निःसपत्ना यथासुखम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Today I shall devour this human lady even while you are looking on. Having been rid of a rival, I shall roam with you at ease.” (16)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा मृगशावाक्षीमलातसदृशेक्षणा।
अभ्यगच्छत् सुसंक्रुद्धा महोल्का रोहिणीमिव॥ १७॥
verses.m: Saying so, the woman, whose eyes shone like live embers, highly enraged as she was, rushed upon the fawn-eyed Sītā, even as a large meteor would descend on the constellation known by the name of Rohiṇī. (17)

verses.text:
तां मृत्युपाशप्रतिमामापतन्तीं महाबलः।
विगृह्य रामः कुपितस्ततो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Checking by his very menacing sound the woman, who was rushing towards Sītā like the noose of Death, Śrī Rāma, who was possessed of extraordinary might, now angrily said to Lakṣmaṇa : (18)

verses.text:
क्रूरैरनार्यैः सौमित्रे परिहासः कथंचन।
न कार्यः पश्य वैदेहीं कथंचित् सौम्य जीवतीम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “You should in no case jest, O son of Sumitrā, with cruel and unworthy people. See the princess of Videha surviving with great difficulty (having narrowly escaped being devoured by the ogress), O gentle brother ! (19)

verses.text:
इमां विरूपामसतीमतिमत्तां महोदरीम्।
राक्षसीं पुरुषव्याघ्र विरूपयितुमर्हसि॥ २०॥
verses.m: “You ought to mutilate, O tiger among men, this ugly, vile, highly wanton and big-bellied woman.” (20)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तो लक्ष्मणस्तस्याः क्रुद्धो रामस्य पश्यतः।
उद्धृत्य खड्गं चिच्छेद कर्णनासे महाबलः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Drawing his sword, when spoken to in these words, the angry Lakṣmaṇa, who was possessed of great might, lopped off her ears and nose while Śrī Rāma looked on. (21)

verses.text:
निकृत्तकर्णनासा तु विस्वरं सा विनद्य च।
यथागतं प्रदुद्राव घोरा शूर्पणखा वनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: With her ears and nose severed, that fierce Śūrpaṇakhā for her part ran away into the forest, as she had come, yelling dissonantly. (22)

verses.text:
सा विरूपा महाघोरा राक्षसी शोणितोक्षिता।
ननाद विविधान् नादान् यथा प्रावृषि तोयदः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Bathed in blood, that ugly and extraordinarily fierce ogress roared in various ways like a cloud in the monsoon. (23)

verses.text:
सा विक्षरन्ती रुधिरं बहुधा घोरदर्शना।
प्रगृह्य बाहू गर्जन्ती प्रविवेश महावनम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Dropping profusely blood on the way, raising her arms and roaring in various ways, that woman of fierce looks entered the heart of the great forest. (24)

verses.text:
ततस्तु सा राक्षससङ्घसंवृतं
खरं जनस्थानगतं विरूपिता।
उपेत्य तं भ्रातरमुग्रतेजसं
पपात भूमौ गगनाद् यथाशनिः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Then, approaching her notorious brother, Khara of terrific energy, who lived in Janasthāna, surrounded by a multitude of ogres, that mutilated woman then dropped down on the ground like a bolt from the blue. (25)

verses.text:
ततः सभार्यं भयमोहमूर्च्छिता
सलक्ष्मणं राघवमागतं वनम्।
विरूपणं चात्मनि शोणितोक्षिता
शशंस सर्वं भगिनी खरस्य सा॥ २६॥
verses.m: Overcome with a swoon through fear and drenched in blood, that sister of Khara then told him everything about Rāghava having arrived in the forest with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa and of her own mutilation. (26)

verses.text:
तां तथा पतितां दृष्ट्वा विरूपां शोणितोक्षिताम्।
भगिनीं क्रोधसंतप्तः खरः पप्रच्छ राक्षसः॥ १॥
verses.m: Inflamed with anger to see his aforesaid sister fallen as she had done, mutilated and drenched in blood, the ogre Khara said : (1)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठ तावदाख्याहि प्रमोहं जहि सम्भ्रमम्।
व्यक्तमाख्याहि केन त्वमेवंरूपा विरूपिता॥ २॥
verses.m: “Get up, shake off your unconsciousness and fear and point out explicitly by whom you have been mutilated in this way. (2)

verses.text:
कः कृष्णसर्पमासीनमाशीविषमनागसम्।
तुदत्यभिसमापन्नमङ्गुल्यग्रेण लीलया॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Who has hit in sport with the tip of his finger a poisonous black serpent arrived in front and sitting harmlessly: (3)

verses.text:
कालपाशं समासज्य कण्ठे मोहान्न बुध्यते।
यस्त्वामद्य समासाद्य पीतवान् विषमुत्तमम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “He who having assailed you has drunk up a most effective poison (in the form of mutilating you) is not conscious of his having fastened the noose of Death round his neck. (4)

verses.text:
बलविक्रमसम्पन्ना कामगा कामरूपिणी।
इमामवस्थां नीता त्वं केनान्तकसमागता॥ ५॥
verses.m: “By whom were you approached and reduced to this state—you, who are richly endowed with strength and prowess, nay, moving at will, are capable of assuming any form you like and are a compeer of Death? (5)

verses.text:
देवगन्धर्वभूतानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्।
कोऽयमेवं महावीर्यस्त्वां विरूपां चकार ह॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Possessed of extraordinary prowess among gods, Gandharvas (celestial musicians) and high-souled seers of Vedic Mantras, who is it that has actually mutilated you thus? (6)

verses.text:
नहि पश्याम्यहं लोके यः कुर्यान्मम विप्रियम्।
अमरेषु सहस्राक्षं महेन्द्रं पाकशासनम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Really I do not perceive in the world anyone who dare give offence to me—not even the mighty Indra, the thousand-eyed tamer of the demon Pāka. (7)

verses.text:
अद्याहं मार्गणैः प्राणानादास्ये जीवितान्तगैः।
सलिले क्षीरमासक्तं निष्पिबन्निव सारसः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Today I shall take the offender’s life with my deadly arrows, even as a swan drains off the milk mixed up in water, while heartily drinking it. (8)

verses.text:
निहतस्य मया संख्ये शरसंकृत्तमर्मणः।
सफेनं रुधिरं कस्य मेदिनी पातुमिच्छति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Whose foaming blood does the earth seek to suck when he has been slain by me on the battlefield, his vital parts having been cut through with my arrows? (9)

verses.text:
कस्य पत्ररथाः कायान्मांसमुत्कृत्य संगताः।
प्रहृष्टा भक्षयिष्यन्ति निहतस्य मया रणे॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Whose flesh will the birds, come together, most delightedly swallow tearing it off from his body when he has been killed by me on the battlefield? (10)

verses.text:
तं न देवा न गन्धर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः।
मयापकृष्टं कृपणं शक्तास्त्रातुं महाहवे॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Neither gods nor Gandharvas, nor fiends nor ogres shall be able to save the wretch dragged by me on the battlefield. (11)

verses.text:
उपलभ्य शनैः संज्ञां तं मे शंसितुमर्हसि।
येन त्वं दुर्विनीतेन वने विक्रम्य निर्जिता॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Gradually recovering consciousness, please tell me the name of the unruly fellow by whom you were assailed and subdued in the forest.” (12)

verses.text:
इति भ्रातुर्वचः श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धस्य च विशेषतः।
ततः शूर्पणखा वाक्यं सबाष्पमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of her brother, Khara, especially when he was seized with fury, Śūrpaṇakhā now made the following reply with tears in her eyes : (13)

verses.text:
तरुणौ रूपसम्पन्नौ सुकुमारौ महाबलौ।
पुण्डरीकविशालाक्षौ चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरौ॥ १४॥
फलमूलाशनौ दान्तौ तापसौ ब्रह्मचारिणौ।
पुत्रौ दशरथस्यास्तां भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Young and richly endowed with comeliness, tender yet possessed of extraordinary might, having large lotus-like eyes and clad in the bark of trees and black antelope skin, living on fruits and roots, self-controlled, practising austerities and continence, there are two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, sons of Daśaratha. (14-15)

verses.text:
गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमौ पार्थिवव्यञ्जनान्वितौ।
देवौ वा दानवावेतौ न तर्कयितुमुत्सहे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “They look like the king of Gandharvas and are endowed with the bodily marks of kings. I am unable to guess whether they are gods or demons. (16)

verses.text:
तरुणी रूपसम्पन्ना सर्वाभरणभूषिता।
दृष्टा तत्र मया नारी तयोर्मध्ये सुमध्यमा॥ १७॥
verses.m: “In their midst was seen by me there a young lady with a slender waist, richly endowed with bodily charm and adorned with all kinds of ornaments. (17)

verses.text:
ताभ्यामुभाभ्यां सम्भूय प्रमदामधिकृत्य ताम्।
इमामवस्थां नीताहं यथानाथासती तथा॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I was reduced to this plight by both the aforesaid brothers together on account of that young lady, in the same way as an unprotected and vile woman would be. (18)

verses.text:
तस्याश्चानृजुवृत्तायास्तयोश्च हतयोरहम्।
सफेनं पातुमिच्छामि रुधिरं रणमूर्धनि॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I long to drink the foaming blood of that woman of crooked ways as well as of those two brothers, killed in the van of a combat. (19)

verses.text:
एष मे प्रथमः कामः कृतस्तत्र त्वया भवेत्।
तस्यास्तयोश्च रुधिरं पिबेयमहमाहवे॥ २०॥
verses.m: “This foremost desire of mine may be accomplished by you there, viz., that I may drink on the battlefield the blood of that lady as well as of those two brothers.” (20)

verses.text:
इति तस्यां ब्रुवाणायां चतुर्दश महाबलान्।
व्यादिदेश खरः क्रुद्धो राक्षसानन्तकोपमान्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Even while she was speaking thus, the infuriated Khara commanded (as follows) fourteen ogres, who were possessed of extraordinary might and resembled Death : (21)

verses.text:
मानुषौ शस्त्रसम्पन्नौ चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरौ।
प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यं घोरं प्रमदया सह॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Two human beings, fully equipped with arms, clad in bark and black antelope skin, and accompanied by a young woman, have entered the frightful Daṇḍaka forest. (22)

verses.text:
तौ हत्वा तां च दुर्वृत्तामुपावर्तितुमर्हथ।
इयं च भगिनी तेषां रुधिरं मम पास्यति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Having made short work of the two brothers, you should also kill that vile woman. This sister of mine will drink their blood. (23)

verses.text:
मनोरथोऽयमिष्टोऽस्या भगिन्या मम राक्षसाः।
शीघ्रं सम्पाद्यतां गत्वा तौ प्रमथ्य स्वतेजसा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Proceeding quickly and killing those two brothers with your own might, accomplish this cherished longing of this sister of mine, O ogres ! (24)

verses.text:
युष्माभिर्निहतौ दृष्ट्वा तावुभौ भ्रातरौ रणे।
इयं प्रहृष्टा मुदिता रुधिरं युधि पास्यति॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Highly delighted to see those two brothers killed on the battlefield by you, this lady will drink their blood on the battlefield with joy.” (25)

verses.text:
इति प्रतिसमादिष्टा राक्षसास्ते चतुर्दश।
तत्र जग्मुस्तया सार्धं घना वातेरिता इव॥ २६॥
verses.m: Commanded in these words by Khara, those fourteen ogres went there with her like clouds driven by a blast. (26)

verses.text:
ततः शूर्पणखा घोरा राघवाश्रममागता।
राक्षसानाचचक्षे तौ भ्रातरौ सह सीतया॥ १॥
verses.m: Having reached the hermitage of Rāghava, the dreadful Śūrpaṇakhā then pointed out to the ogres the two brothers with Sītā. (1)

verses.text:
ते रामं पर्णशालायामुपविष्टं महाबलम्।
ददृशुः सीतया सार्धं लक्ष्मणेनापि सेवितम्॥ २॥
verses.m: They saw the exceptionally mighty Śrī Rāma seated with Sītā in his hut thatched with leaves and waited upon by Lakṣmaṇa. (2)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमानागतांस्तांश्च राक्षसान्।
अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं रामो लक्ष्मणं दीप्ततेजसम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Seeing her as well as those ogres come, the glorious Rāma, a scion of Raghu, said to his brother, Lakṣmaṇa of resplendent lustre: (3)

verses.text:
मुहूर्तं भव सौमित्रे सीतायाः प्रत्यनन्तरः।
इमानस्या वधिष्यामि पदवीमागतानिह॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Remain, O son of Sumitrā, by the side of Sītā for a while. I shall make short work of these ogres, who have come here to back the ogress”. (4)

verses.text:
वाक्यमेतत् ततः श्रुत्वा रामस्य विदितात्मनः।
तथेति लक्ष्मणो वाक्यं राघवस्य प्रपूजयन्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Rāma, the knower of his own Self, and bowing his head to the utterance of Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa said ‘Amen !’ (5)

verses.text:
राघवोऽपि महच्चापं चामीकरविभूषितम्।
चकार सज्यं धर्मात्मा तानि रक्षांसि चाब्रवीत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: The pious-minded Rāghava too strung his mighty bow ornamented with gold and said to those ogres : (6)

verses.text:
पुत्रौ दशरथस्यावां भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
प्रविष्टौ सीतया सार्धं दुश्चरं दण्डकावनम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “We two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, sons of Daśaratha, have entered with Sītā the forest of Daṇḍaka, which is difficult to pass through. (7)

verses.text:
फलमूलाशनौ दान्तौ तापसौ ब्रह्मचारिणौ।
वसन्तौ दण्डकारण्ये किमर्थमुपहिंसथ॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Why do you seek to injure us, who subsist on fruits and roots, are self-disciplined, practise austerities and continence and are living in the Daṇḍaka forest? (8)

verses.text:
युष्मान् पापात्मकान् हन्तुं विप्रकारान् महाहवे।
ऋषीणां तु नियोगेन सम्प्राप्तः सशरासनः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Armed with a bow, I for my part have duly come here at the behest of sages to kill in a major conflict you, whose mind is given to sin and who have offended against the sages. (9)

verses.text:
तिष्ठतैवात्र संतुष्टा नोपवर्तितुमर्हथ।
यदि प्राणैरिहार्थो वो निवर्तध्वं निशाचराः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Halt where you stand, if you love war and you should not run away. If, however, you love your life, go back, O night-stalkers !” (10)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसास्ते चतुर्दश।
ऊचुर्वाचं सुसंक्रुद्धा ब्रह्मघ्नाः शूलपाणयः॥ ११॥
संरक्तनयना घोरा रामं संरक्तलोचनम्।
परुषा मधुराभाषं हृष्टा दृष्टपराक्रमम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Highly enraged and delighted (at the same time) to hear the aforesaid challenge of Śrī Rāma, those fourteen dreadful ogres, the slayers of Brāhmaṇas, who were armed with lances and had bloodshot eyes, spoke harshly as follows to Rāma, who had naturally deep red eyes, who always spoke sweet words and whose prowess had been seen by them : (11-12)

verses.text:
क्रोधमुत्पाद्य नो भर्तुः खरस्य सुमहात्मनः।
त्वमेव हास्यसे प्राणान् सद्योऽस्माभिर्हतो युधि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Having provoked the anger of our extremely high-souled master, Khara, you will surely give up your ghost in no time, when struck by us on the battlefield. (13)

verses.text:
का हि ते शक्तिरेकस्य बहूनां रणमूर्धनि।
अस्माकमग्रतः स्थातुं किं पुनर्योद्धुमाहवे॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Indeed what power have you to stand single-handed in front of us, who are so many, in the van of a fight, much less to give fight in a battle? (14)

verses.text:
एभिर्बाहुप्रयुक्तैश्च परिघैः शूलपट्टिशैः।
प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यसि वीर्यं च धनुश्च करपीडितम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Under the pressure of these iron clubs, darts and Paṭṭiśas (a kind of sharp-edged sword) hurled by our arms, you will give up the ghost, your valour too as well as the bow pressed in your hands.” (15)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा संरब्धा राक्षसास्ते चतुर्दश।
उद्यतायुधनिस्तिं्रशा राममेवाभिदुद्रुवुः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Saying so, those fourteen ogres ran in their zeal towards Rāma alone, their weapons, including swords, uplifted. (16)

verses.text:
