Nay, you desire to tread on the heads of iron-tipped pikes—you who seek to lay your hands on the worthy consort of Śrī Rāma ! (42—44)

verses.text:
यदन्तरं सिंहसृगालयोर्वने
यदन्तरं स्यन्दनिकासमुद्रयोः।
सुराग्र्यसौवीरकयोर्यदन्तरं
तदन्तरं दाशरथेस्तवैव च॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “The same disparity exists between Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha) and yourself as does between a lion and a jackal in a forest, between a sea and a brook, between nectar (the foremost of beverages) and Sauvīraka (a sour and savoury drink prepared by dissolving powdered rye-seeds into water and preserving it for a day or two). (45)

verses.text:
यदन्तरं काञ्चनसीसलोहयो-
र्यदन्तरं चन्दनवारिपङ्कयोः।
यदन्तरं हस्तिबिडालयोर्वने
तदन्तरं दाशरथेस्तवैव च॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Nay, the same disparity exists between Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha) and you as does between gold and a base metal like lead, between sandal-paste and mud and between an elephant and a cat in a jungle. (46)

verses.text:
यदन्तरं वायसवैनतेययो-
र्यदन्तरं मद्गुमयूरयोरपि।
यदन्तरं हंसकगृध्रयोर्वने
तदन्तरं दाशरथेस्तवैव च॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Again, the same disparity exists between you and Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha) as does between Garuḍa (son of Vinatā and the King of birds) and a crow, between a peacock and a diver bird, between a swan (which is believed to feed on pearls) and a vulture (which feeds on the rotten flesh of carcasses). (47)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् सहस्राक्षसमप्रभावे
रामे स्थिते कार्मुकबाणपाणौ।
हृतापि तेऽहं न जरां गमिष्ये
आज्यं यथा मक्षिकयावगीर्णम्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “So long as Śrī Rāma, whose might equals that of Indra (the thousand-eyed god), is alive holding a bow and an arrow in his hand, I shall not be retained by you, even though carried away by you, any more than ghee swallowed by a bee (which ultimately causes its death).” (48)

verses.text:
इतीव तद्वाक्यमदुष्टभावा
सुदुष्टमुक्त्वा रजनीचरं तम्।
गात्रप्रकम्पाद् व्यथिता बभूव
वातोद्धता सा कदलीव तन्वी॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Having thus addressed the foregoing most pungent words to the said ranger of the night, the lean and thin Sītā, who harboured no vile motive towards him, felt afflicted due to a tremor in her body like a plantain tree shaken by a blast. (49)

verses.text:
तां वेपमानामुपलक्ष्य सीतां
स रावणो मृत्युसमप्रभावः।
कुलं बलं नाम च कर्म चात्मनः
समाचचक्षे भयकारणार्थम्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Perceiving Sītā shaking through uncertainty, the said Rāvaṇa, who was mighty as Death, proudly mentioned his own descent, strength, name and exploits in order to intimidate her. (50)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवत्यां सीतायां संरब्धः परुषं वचः।
ललाटे भ्रुकुटिं कृत्वा रावणः प्रत्युवाच ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Knitting his brows on his forehead while Sītā was speaking as aforesaid, Rāvaṇa felt provoked and replied in the following harsh words : so the tradition goes : (1)

verses.text:
भ्राता वैश्रवणस्याहं सापत्नो वरवर्णिनि।
रावणो नाम भद्रं ते दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्॥ २॥
यस्य देवाः सगन्धर्वाः पिशाचपतगोरगाः।
विद्रवन्ति सदा भीता मृत्योरिव सदा प्रजाः॥ ३॥
येन वैश्रवणो भ्राता वैमात्राः कारणान्तरे।
द्वन्द्वमासादितः क्रोधाद् रणे विक्रम्य निर्जितः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Good luck to you, O lady of excellent complexion ! I am the glorious ten-headed half-brother of Kubera (son of Sage Viśravā), Rāvaṇa by name, from whom gods including Gandharvas, nay, fiends, birds and serpents ever flee in terror as created beings are always afraid of death, nay, provoked by whom to a conflict on some excuse, his half-brother, Kubera (son of Sage Viśravā) was assailed and utterly vanquished. (2—4)

verses.text:
मद्भयार्तः परित्यज्य स्वमधिष्ठानमृद्धिमत्।
कैलासं पर्वतश्रेष्ठमध्यास्ते नरवाहनः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Deserting for good his sumptuous abode, Laṅkā, stricken as he was with fear of me, Kubera (who is carried from place to place on a palanquin borne by human beings) dwells on the top of Kailāsa, the foremost of mountains. (5)

verses.text:
यस्य तत् पुष्पकं नाम विमानं कामगं शुभम्।
वीर्यादावर्जितं भद्रे येन यामि विहायसम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “His celebrated and beautiful aerial car, Puṣpaka by name, which can go wherever one likes, and in which I range the skies, was snatched by me by dint of my prowess, O good lady ! (6)

verses.text:
मम संजातरोषस्य मुखं दृष्ट्वैव मैथिलि।
विद्रवन्ति परित्रस्ताः सुराः शक्रपुरोगमाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Alarmed to see my very face when I am provoked to anger, gods headed by Indra take to flight, O princess of Mithilā ! (7)

verses.text:
यत्र तिष्ठाम्यहं तत्र मारुतो वाति शङ्कितः।
तीव्रांशुः शिशिरांशुश्च भयात् सम्पद्यते दिवि॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Wheresoever I halt, the wind blows gently through apprehension and the sun with its fierce rays is transformed into the moon (because of its cool rays) in the heavens. (8)

verses.text:
निष्कम्पपत्रास्तरवो नद्यश्च स्तिमितोदकाः।
भवन्ति यत्र तत्राहं तिष्ठामि च चरामि च॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Nay, wherever I stay and move, the trees find their leaves motionless and the rivers find their waters still. (9)

verses.text:
मम पारे समुद्रस्य लङ्का नाम पुरी शुभा।
सम्पूर्णा राक्षसैर्घोरैर्यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Beyond the sea stands my beautiful capital, Laṅkā by name, vying with Amarāvatī, the capital of Indra, and full of fierce ogres. (10)

verses.text:
प्राकारेण परिक्षिप्ता पाण्डुरेण विराजिता।
हेमकक्ष्या पुरी रम्या वैदूर्यमयतोरणा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Enclosed and beautified by a white enclosure wall, the city looks charming with the inner apartments of its houses built of gold and outer gates made of cat’s-eye jewels. (11)

verses.text:
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधा तूर्यनादविनादिता।
सर्वकामफलैर्वृक्षैः संकुलोद्यानभूषिता॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The city is crowded with elephants, horses and chariots and rendered noisy by the sound of musical instruments of every description; nay, it abounds in trees yielding all kinds of coveted fruits and is beautified by gardens. (12)

verses.text:
तत्र त्वं वस हे सीते राजपुत्रि मया सह।
न स्मरिष्यसि नारीणां मानुषीणां मनस्विनि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Dwell you there with me, O princess Sītā ! There you will no longer remember mortal women, O proud lady ! (13)

verses.text:
भुञ्जाना मानुषान् भोगान् दिव्यांश्च वरवर्णिनि।
न स्मरिष्यसि रामस्य मानुषस्य गतायुषः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Enjoying human as well as celestial delights, you will no longer think of the mortal Rāma, whose life has now well-nigh departed, O lady of excellent complexion ! (14)

verses.text:
स्थापयित्वा प्रियं पुत्रं राज्ये दशरथो नृपः।
मन्दवीर्यस्ततो ज्येष्ठः सुतः प्रस्थापितो वनम्॥ १५॥
तेन किं भ्रष्टराज्येन रामेण गतचेतसा।
करिष्यसि विशालाक्षि तापसेन तपस्विना॥ १६॥
verses.m: “What use can you have for the aforesaid Rāma, an ascetic practising austerities, who has lost his sovereignty and consequently been deprived of his reasoning faculty, and who, possessed as he was of negligible prowess, though the eldest son of his father, was consequently sent into exile to the forest by King Daśaratha after installing on the throne as Prince Regent his pet son, Bharata, O large-eyed lady? (15-16)

verses.text:
रक्ष राक्षसभर्तारं कामय स्वयमागतम्।
न मन्मथशराविष्टं प्रत्याख्यातुं त्वमर्हसि॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Save the lord of ogres, i.e., myself, who has sought you in person, and love him. You ought not to spurn me, overpowered as I am by shafts of love. (17)

verses.text:
प्रत्याख्याय हि मां भीरु पश्चात्तापं गमिष्यसि।
चरणेनाभिहत्येव पुरूरवसमुर्वशी॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Spurning me, O timid one, you will surely suffer contrition as did Urvaśī on having kicked King Purūravā. (18)

verses.text:
अङ्गुल्या न समो रामो मम युद्धे स मानुषः।
तव भाग्येन सम्प्राप्तं भजस्व वरवर्णिनि॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The mortal Rāma is not equal even to my finger on the field of battle. Therefore, accept me, who have sought you by your good luck, O lady with an excellent complexion !” (19)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही क्रुद्धा संरक्तलोचना।
अब्रवीत् परुषं वाक्यं रहिते राक्षसाधिपम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Enraged when spoken to as aforesaid, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, for her part with blood-red eyes addressed the following harsh words to Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, in that lonely place : (20)

verses.text:
कथं वैश्रवणं देवं सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम्।
भ्रातरं व्यपदिश्य त्वमशुभं कर्तुमिच्छसि॥ २१॥
verses.m: “How after calling god Kubera (son of Viśravā), who is hailed by all gods, your (half-) brother, do you seek to perpetrate a foul deed? (21)

verses.text:
अवश्यं विनशिष्यन्ति सर्वे रावण राक्षसाः।
येषां त्वं कर्कशो राजा दुर्बुद्धिरजितेन्द्रियः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “All ogres, O Rāvaṇa, will inevitably perish inasmuch as you, who are so hard-hearted and evil-minded and have not been able to subdue your senses, are their ruler. (22)

verses.text:
अपहृत्य शचीं भार्यां शक्यमिन्द्रस्य जीवितुम्।
नहि रामस्य भार्यां मामानीय स्वस्तिमान् भवेत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “It may be possible to survive on abducting Śacī, the consort of Indra, the lord of paradise; but none can survive peacefully after carrying away me, the consort of Śrī Rāma. (23)

verses.text:
जीवेच्चिरं वज्रधरस्य पश्चा-
च्छचीं प्रधृष्याप्रतिरूपरूपाम्।
न मादृशीं राक्षस धर्षयित्वा
पीतामृतस्यापि तवास्ति मोक्षः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Having laid one’s hands on Śacī, the consort of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, of peerless beauty, one might survive long, but on treating with indignity a woman like me there is no escape from death for you even though you have quaffed the drink of immortality, O ogre ! (24)

verses.text:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्।
हस्ते हस्तं समाहत्य चकार सुमहद् वपुः॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the rebuke of Sītā, and violently striking his hand against the other hand in anger, the mighty Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, revealed his gigantic form. (1)

verses.text:
स मैथिलीं पुनर्वाक्यं बभाषे वाक्यकोविदः।
नोन्मत्तया श्रुतौ मन्ये मम वीर्यपराक्रमौ॥ २॥
verses.m: A master of expression, he once more addressed the following words to Sītā, the princess of Mithilā : “I believe my valour and prowess have not been heard of by you, insane as you are. (2)

verses.text:
उद्वहेयं भुजाभ्यां तु मेदिनीमम्बरे स्थितः।
आपिबेयं समुद्रं च मृत्युं हन्यां रणे स्थितः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Standing in the air, I can actually lift up the earth with my hands, drink up the ocean on all sides and, stationed on a field of battle, can kill even Death. (3)

verses.text:
अर्कं तुद्यां शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विभिन्द्यां हि महीतलम्।
कामरूपेण उन्मत्ते पश्य मां कामरूपिणम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “With my sharp arrows I can torment the sun and cleave the surface of the earth. Look at me, who can take any form at will, O lady ! intoxicated with passion and pride of beauty !” (4)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तवतस्तस्य रावणस्य शिखिप्रभे।
क्रुद्धस्य हरिपर्यन्ते रक्ते नेत्रे बभूवतुः॥ ५॥
verses.m: By the time he had spoken thus the eyes of the angry Rāvaṇa with dark corners turned red and began to burn as fire. (5)

verses.text:
सद्यः सौम्यं परित्यज्य तीक्ष्णरूपं स रावणः।
स्वं रूपं कालरूपाभं भेजे वैश्रवणानुजः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Abandoning his benign aspect at once, the said Rāvaṇa, a younger (half-) brother of Kubera (son of Sage Viśravā), resumed his own native fierce form, resembling that of Death. (6)

verses.text:
संरक्तनयनः श्रीमांस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणः।
क्रोधेन महताविष्टो नीलजीमूतसंनिभः॥ ७॥
verses.m: With blood-red eyes the glorious ogre, who was decked with ornaments of refined gold and seized with great anger, looked like a dark cloud. (7)

verses.text:
दशास्यो विंशतिभुजो बभूव क्षणदाचरः।
स परिव्राजकच्छद्म महाकायो विहाय तत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Shaking off the aforesaid disguise of a wandering ascetic, the ranger of the night assumed a colossal form with ten heads and twenty arms. (8)

verses.text:
प्रतिपेदे स्वकं रूपं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः।
रक्ताम्बरधरस्तस्थौ स्त्रीरत्नं प्रेक्ष्य मैथिलीम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, resumed his native form and gazing on Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, a veritable jewel among women, stood clad in a red robe. (9)

verses.text:
स तामसितकेशान्तां भास्करस्य प्रभामिव।
वसनाभरणोपेतां मैथिलीं रावणोऽब्रवीत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: The said Rāvaṇa spoke as follows to that princess of Mithilā, who with her dark ends of hair was duly dressed and adorned with jewels and shone like the radiance of the sun : (10)

verses.text:
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं यदि भर्तारमिच्छसि।
मामाश्रय वरारोहे तवाहं सदृशः पतिः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “If you desire a husband well-known throughout the three worlds (heaven, earth and the intermediate region), betake yourself to me, O lady with charming limbs ! I am a husband worthy of you. (11)

verses.text:
मां भजस्व चिराय त्वमहं श्लाघ्यः पतिस्तव।
नैव चाहं क्वचिद् भद्रे करिष्ये तव विप्रियम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Serve me for a long time ! I am a husband worthy of praise for you. I shall certainly never do anything unpalatable to you, O good lady ! (12)

verses.text:
त्यज्यतां मानुषो भावो मयि भावः प्रणीयताम्।
राज्याच्च्युतमसिद्धार्थं रामं परिमितायुषम्॥ १३॥
कैर्गुणैरनुरक्तासि मूढे पण्डितमानिनि।
यः स्त्रियो वचनाद् राज्यं विहाय ससुहृज्जनम्॥ १४॥
अस्मिन् व्यालानुचरिते वने वसति दुर्मतिः।
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं वाक्यं प्रियार्हां प्रियवादिनीम्॥ १५॥
अभिगम्य सुदुष्टात्मा राक्षसः काममोहितः।
जग्राह रावणः सीतां बुधः खे रोहिणीमिव॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Let your affection for a human being be given up and let it be placed on me. Due to what virtues do you feel attached to the silly Rāma, who has been banished from his kingdom, nay, who has failed to achieve his object and whose days are numbered, O deluded woman accounting yourself wise, and who, having given up the throne of Ayodhyā as well as his kith and kin at the instance of a woman, is dwelling in this forest frequented by beasts of prey?” Having spoken as aforesaid to Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, who spoke kindly to all and deserved kind words from all, and approaching her, the ogre, Rāvaṇa, who was extremely vile of disposition and was infatuated with passion, caught hold of Sītā (who was like a mother to him) as Budha (the deity presiding over the planet Mercury and son of the moon-god) would seize Rohiṇī (the principal consort of the moon-god and the deity presiding over a constellation of that name). (13—16)

verses.text:
वामेन सीतां पद्माक्षीं मूर्धजेषु करेण सः।
ऊर्वोस्तु दक्षिणेनैव परिजग्राह पाणिना॥ १७॥
verses.m: With his left hand he caught hold of the lotus-eyed Sītā by her locks, while with his right hand he clasped her by her thighs. (17)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा गिरिशृङ्गाभं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रं महाभुजम्।
प्राद्रवन् मृत्युसंकाशं भयार्ता वनदेवताः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Stricken with fear to see him looking like a mountain-peak in stature and resembling Death himself, endowed as he was with sharp teeth and mighty arms, the sylvan deities ran away. (18)

verses.text:
स च मायामयो दिव्यः खरयुक्तः खरस्वनः।
प्रत्यदृश्यत हेमाङ्गो रावणस्य महारथः॥ १९॥
verses.m: And there appeared close by at that very moment the well-known, enchanted, huge celestial car of Rāvaṇa, which was drawn by mules, made a jarring sound, and was made of gold. (19)

verses.text:
ततस्तां परुषैर्वाक्यैरभितर्ज्य महास्वनः।
अंकेनादाय वैदेहीं रथमारोपयत् तदा॥ २०॥
verses.m: Then, overawing Sītā, the princess of the Videha territory, with harsh words, and taking her in his arms, Rāvaṇa, who uttered a loud roar, forthwith placed her in the car. (20)

verses.text:
सा गृहीतातिचुक्रोश रावणेन यशस्विनी।
रामेति सीता दुःखार्ता रामं दूरं गतं वने॥ २१॥
verses.m: Stricken with agony when seized by Rāvaṇa, the illustrious and well-known Sītā cried at the top of her voice ‘O Rāma’, addressing Śrī Rāma, who had penetrated deep into the forest. (21)

verses.text:
तामकामां स कामार्तः पन्नगेन्द्रवधूमिव।
विचेष्टमानामादाय उत्पपाताथ रावणः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Taking Sītā, who had no desire to meet Rāvaṇa and who was wriggling like a consort of the king of Nāgas, the aforesaid Rāvaṇa, who was stricken with passion, presently rose to the skies in his aerial car. (22)

verses.text:
ततः सा राक्षसेन्द्रेण ह्रियमाणा विहायसा।
भृशं चुक्रोश मत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्ता यथातुरा॥ २३॥
verses.m: While being borne away through the air by Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, she then began to wail loudly as follows like one mad and injured, her mind distracted through grief : (23)

verses.text:
हा लक्ष्मण महाबाहो गुरुचित्तप्रसादक।
ह्रियमाणां न जानीषे रक्षसा कामरूपिणा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “O mighty-armed Lakṣmaṇa, O delighter of the mind of your elder brother, Śrī Rāma, you do not perceive me being carried away by an ogre, who is able to assume any form at will. (24)

verses.text:
जीवितं सुखमर्थं च धर्महेतोः परित्यजन्।
ह्रियमाणामधर्मेण मां राघव न पश्यसि॥ २५॥
verses.m: (Addressing Śrī Rāma) “even though you have fully renounced your happiness and whatever is solicited by all, nay, staked your very life, for the sake of virtue, O scion of Raghu, you are not able to see me being borne away unrighteously. (25)

verses.text:
ननु नामाविनीतानां विनेतासि परंतप।
कथमेवंविधं पापं न त्वं शाधि हि रावणम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Undoubtedly you are the tamer of the unruly, O scorcher of your enemies ! How, then, do you not punish Rāvaṇa, who is so sinful, (26)

verses.text:
न तु सद्योऽविनीतस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्।
कालोऽप्यङ्गीभवत्यत्र सस्यानामिव पक्तये॥ २७॥
verses.m: (Turning to Rāvaṇa, she continued :) “Of course, the fruit of the evil deed of an insolent man is not perceived immediately. Time as well plays a part in the fructification of an act, as it does in the ripening of foodgrains. (27)

verses.text:
त्वं कर्म कृतवानेतत् कालोपहतचेतनः।
जीवितान्तकरं घोरं रामाद् व्यसनमाप्नुहि॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Your understanding having been vitiated by an adverse fate, you have perpetrated this outrageous act. As such suffer terrible misfortune, which is sure to bring your life to an end, at the hands of Śrī Rāma. (28)

verses.text:
हन्तेदानीं सकामा तु कैकेयी बान्धवैः सह।
ह्रियेयं धर्मकामस्य धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Alas, Kaikeyī with her kith and kin has her desire fulfilled in that I, the lawful consort of an illustrious hero, who is covetous of virtue alone, am being borne away by a desperado. (29)

verses.text:
आमन्त्रये जनस्थाने कर्णिकारांश्च पुष्पितान्।
क्षिप्रं रामाय शंसध्वं सीतां हरति रावणः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Nay, I pray to the Karṇikāra trees in blossom in Janasthāna in the following words: ‘Kindly tell Śrī Rāma promptly that Rāvaṇa is taking away Sītā.’ (30)

verses.text:
हंससारससंघुष्टां वन्दे गोदावरीं नदीम्।
क्षिप्रं रामाय शंस त्वं सीतां हरति रावणः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “I salute the river Godāvarī made noisy by swans and cranes and pray to her as follows: ‘Please tell Śrī Rāma (when he comes to you) at once that Rāvaṇa is carrying away Sītā.’ (31)

verses.text:
दैवतानि च यान्यस्मिन् वने विविधपादपे।
नमस्करोम्यहं तेभ्यो भर्तुः शंसत मां हृताम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Nay I offer salutations to all those deities who dwell in this forest full of various trees, and pray to them : ‘(Kindly) speak to my husband of my having been borne away.’ (32)

verses.text:
यानि कानिचिदप्यत्र सत्त्वानि विविधानि च।
सर्वाणि शरणं यामि मृगपक्षिगणानि वै॥ ३३॥
ह्रियमाणां प्रियां भर्तुः प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसीम्।
विवशा ते हृता सीता रावणेनेति शंसत॥ ३४॥
verses.m: I seek the protection of all the animals of different species, the herds of deer and the flocks of birds, which actually dwell in this forest, and pray : “Kindly tell my husband of his beloved spouse, more valuable to him than his very life, being borne away, and add the following : Your Sītā has been carried away by Rāvaṇa, helpless as she was. (33-34)

verses.text:
विदित्वा तु महाबाहुरमुत्रापि महाबलः।
आनेष्यति पराक्रम्य वैवस्वतहृतामपि॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Taking recourse to his prowess on coming to know of my presence even in the other world, the mighty-armed prince, possessed as he is of great strength, will recover me even though carried away by Yama (son of the sun-god).” (35)

verses.text:
सा तदा करुणा वाचो विलपन्ती सुदुःखिता।
वनस्पतिगतं गृध्रं ददर्शायतलोचना॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Uttering loud laments as aforesaid, sore distressed as she was, the large-eyed Sītā presently caught sight of the vulture, Jaṭāyu, perched on a tree. (36)

verses.text:
सा तमुद्वीक्ष्य सुश्रोणी रावणस्य वशंगता।
समाक्रन्दद् भयपरा दुःखोपहतया गिरा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Perceiving him, Sītā of comely limbs, who had given way to fear, fallen as she was into the clutches of Rāvaṇa, cried loudly in a voice choked with agony : (37)

verses.text:
जटायो पश्य मामार्य ह्रियमाणामनाथवत्।
अनेन राक्षसेन्द्रेणाकरुणं पापकर्मणा॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Look at me being ruthlessly borne away, like a woman bereft of her protector, by this Rāvaṇa, king of ogres, of sinful deeds, O noble Jaṭāyu ! (38)

verses.text:
नैष वारयितुं शक्यस्त्वया क्रूरो निशाचरः।
सत्ववाञ्जितकाशी च सायुधश्चैव दुर्मतिः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “This cruel prowler of the night is incapable of being stopped by you, mighty and proud of his victory, armed with weapons and evil-minded too as he is. (39)

verses.text:
रामाय तु यथातत्त्वं जटायो हरणं मम।
लक्ष्मणाय च तत् सर्वमाख्यातव्यमशेषतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “In any case, O Jaṭāyu, my abduction as well as all that is worth relating in that connection must be correctly reported by you to Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa in full.” (40)

verses.text:
तं शब्दमवसुप्तस्तु जटायुरथ शुश्रुवे।
निरैक्षद् रावणं क्षिप्रं वैदेहीं च ददर्श सः॥ १॥
verses.m: Jaṭāyu, for his part, who was lying fast asleep at that time, presently heard that call. He forthwith perceived Rāvaṇa and also saw Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory. (1)

verses.text:
ततः पर्वतशृङ्गाभस्तीक्ष्णतुण्डः खगोत्तमः।
वनस्पतिगतः श्रीमान् व्याजहार शुभां गिरम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Continuing on the tree, the glorious Jaṭāyu, the foremost of birds, who looked like a mountain-peak and had a sharp bill, thereupon addressed the following wholesome words to Rāvaṇa : (2)

verses.text:
दशग्रीव स्थितो धर्मे पुराणे सत्यसंश्रयः।
भ्रातस्त्वं निन्दितं कर्म कर्तुं नार्हसि साम्प्रतम्॥ ३॥
जटायुर्नाम नाम्नाहं गृध्रराजो महाबलः।
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपमः॥ ४॥
लोकानां च हिते युक्तो रामो दशरथात्मजः।
तस्यैषा लोकनाथस्य धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनी॥ ५॥
सीता नाम वरारोहा यां त्वं हर्तुमिहेच्छसि।
कथं राजा स्थितो धर्मे परदारान् परामृशेत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa (who are endowed with ten heads), I am the well-known king of vultures, Jaṭāyu by name, possessed of great might, devoted to the eternal code of virtue and true to my promise. Brother, you ought not to perpetrate a reproachful act at least at this moment in my presence. Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is the ruler of the entire globe, vying with the mighty Indra and Varuṇa (the god presiding over the waters) and devoted to the welfare of all beings. This lady, whom you seek to bear away at this moment, is the illustrious and lawfully wedded wife of excellent limbs of the aforesaid protector of the world, Sītā by name. How dare a king, firm on virtue, lay his finger on another’s consort? (3—6)

verses.text:
रक्षणीया विशेषेण राजदारा महाबल।
निवर्तय गतिं नीचां परदाराभिमर्शनात्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The consorts of kings, O ogre of extraordinary might, are deserving of protection in a special degree. Therefore, avert a vile destiny which is sure to follow from the sin of laying one’s finger on another’s wife. (7)

verses.text:
न तत् समाचरेद् धीरो यत् परोऽस्य विगर्हयेत्।
यथाऽऽत्मनस्तथान्येषां दारा रक्ष्या विमर्शनात्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “A wise man should not deliberately do that on account of which others may revile him. The consorts of others should be protected from another’s touch in the same way as one’s own wife. (8)

verses.text:
अर्थं वा यदि वा कामं शिष्टाः शास्त्रेष्वनागतम्।
व्यवस्यन्त्यनुराजानं धर्मं पौलस्त्यनन्दन॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The cultured pursue wealth or sensuous enjoyment or even virtue not sanctioned in the scriptures following the example of a king, O delight of Pulastya’s race ! (9)

verses.text:
राजा धर्मश्च कामश्च द्रव्याणां चोत्तमो निधिः।
धर्मः शुभं वा पापं वा राजमूलं प्रवर्तते॥ १०॥
verses.m: “A king embodies virtue and sensuous enjoyment and is an excellent repertory of riches in that virtue; right conduct or sin has its root in a king and proceeds from him. (10)

verses.text:
पापस्वभावश्चपलः कथं त्वं रक्षसां वर।
ऐश्वर्यमभिसम्प्राप्तो विमानमिव दुष्कृती॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Though sinful of disposition and fickle, how have you stumbled upon lordship, O jewel among ogres, as a man of sinful deeds would come upon an aerial car (which as a rule is the lot of the virtuous alone)? (11)

verses.text:
कामस्वभावो यः सोऽसौ न शक्यस्तं प्रमार्जितुम्।
नहि दुष्टात्मनामार्यमावसत्यालये चिरम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The man, who is licentious by nature, is not able to get rid of such nature; for eminence does not abide for long in the house of the evil-minded. (12)

verses.text:
विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा रामो महाबलः।
नापराध्यति धर्मात्मा कथं तस्यापराध्यसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “When Śrī Rāma, who is possessed of extraordinary might and whose mind is set on virtue, does not commit any wrong in your territory or capital, why should you (take into your head to) wrong him? (13)

verses.text:
यदि शूर्पणखाहेतोर्जनस्थानगतः खरः।
अतिवृत्तो हतः पूर्वं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ १४॥
अत्र ब्रूहि यथातत्त्वं को रामस्य व्यतिक्रमः।
यस्य त्वं लोकनाथस्य हृत्वा भार्यां गमिष्यसि॥ १५॥
verses.m: “If Khara stationed in Janasthāna, who transgressed his limits in order to wipe the tears of Śūrpaṇakhā, was killed in action in the past by Śrī Rāma of unwearied action, tell me truly what the fault of Śrī Rāma was in this matter, for which you are bearing away the spouse of that ruler of the worlds? (14-15)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं विसृज वैदेहीं मा त्वा घोरेण चक्षुषा।
दहेद् दहनभूतेन वृत्रमिन्द्राशनिर्यथा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Release Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, at once. Let not Śrī Rāma consume you with his fearful eye converted into fire, as the thunderbolt of Indra consumed the demon, Vṛtra. (16)

verses.text:
सर्पमाशीविषं बद्ध्वा वस्त्रान्ते नावबुध्यसे।
ग्रीवायां प्रतिमुक्तं च कालपाशं न पश्यसि॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Though having tied a poisonous snake in the end of your cloth you are unconscious of it, and you do not perceive the noose of Death placed round your neck; (17)

verses.text:
स भारः सौम्य भर्तव्यो यो नरं नावसादयेत्।
तदन्नमपि भोक्तव्यं जीर्यते यदनामयम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “That load alone, O gentle one, should be borne by a man, which may not oppress him. And that food alone should be eaten, which may be digested without giving rise to an ailment. (18)

verses.text:
यत् कृत्वा न भवेद् धर्मो न कीर्तिर्न यशो ध्रुवम्।
शरीरस्य भवेत् खेदः कस्तत् कर्म समाचरेत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Who will knowingly perform an act as a sequel to which follows neither religious merit, nor glory, nor lasting fame, but in whose wake ensues weariness of body? (19)

verses.text:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि जातस्य मम रावण।
पितृपैतामहं राज्यं यथावदनुतिष्ठतः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Sixty thousand years have elapsed, O Rāvaṇa, ever since I was born, during which I have duly carried on the hereditary rulership of birds. (20)

verses.text:
वृद्धोऽहं त्वं युवा धन्वी सरथः कवची शरी।
न चाप्यादाय कुशली वैदेहीं मे गमिष्यसि॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I have grown old, while you are still young, and are armed with a bow and arrows, protected by an armour and mounted on a chariot. Nevertheless you shall not bear away Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, safely before my eyes. (21)

verses.text:
न शक्तस्त्वं बलाद्धर्तुं वैदेहीं मम पश्यतः।
हेतुभिर्न्यायसंयुक्तैर्ध्रुवां वेदश्रुतीमिव॥ २२॥
verses.m: “You will not be able to carry away Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, by force while I stand looking on, any more than one can alter an unalterable Vedic text by force of arguments consistent with logic. (22)

verses.text:
युध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि मुहूर्तं तिष्ठ रावण।
शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ यथा पूर्वं खरस्तथा॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Fight with me if you are a hero; halt awhile, O Rāvaṇa ! Struck dead by me, you will lie on the ground as Khara did in the past. (23)

verses.text:
असकृत्संयुगे येन निहता दैत्यदानवाः।
न चिराच्चीरवासास्त्वां रामो युधि वधिष्यति॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Clad in the bark of trees, Śrī Rāma, by whom Daityas and Dānavas have been slain on the battlefield more than once, will make short work of you before long. (24)

verses.text:
किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं गतौ दूरं नृपात्मजौ।
क्षिप्रं त्वं नश्यसे नीच तयोर्भीतो न संशयः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “What can be done by me when the two princes have gone afar? If I proceed to call them you will flee at once, afraid of them : there is no doubt about it, O vile ogre ! (25)

verses.text:
नहि मे जीवमानस्य नयिष्यसि शुभामिमाम्।
सीतां कमलपत्राक्षीं रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “So long as I breathe, you can on no account carry away this blessed lady, Sītā, the beloved consort of Śrī Rāma, whose eyes resemble the petals of a lotus. (26)

verses.text:
अवश्यं तु मया कार्यं प्रियं तस्य महात्मनः।
जीवितेनापि रामस्य तथा दशरथस्य च॥ २७॥
verses.m: “What is pleasing to him, the high-souled Śrī Rāma, as well as to the late King Daśaratha, needs must be done by me at all events even at the cost of my life. (27)

verses.text:
तिष्ठ तिष्ठ दशग्रीव मुहूर्तं पश्य रावण।
वृन्तादिव फलं त्वां तु पातयेयं रथोत्तमात्।
युद्धातिथ्यं प्रदास्यामि यथाप्राणं निशाचर॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Tarry, tarry awhile, O ten-headed monster! See, O Rāvaṇa, how I knock you down from the foremost of chariots on which you are mounted as one would dash down a fruit from its stalk. I shall offer hospitality to you on the battlefield according to my strength, O prowler of the night !” (28)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तः क्रोधताम्राक्षस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः।
राक्षसेन्द्रोऽभिदुद्राव पतगेन्द्रममर्षणः॥ १॥
verses.m: When challenged in the aforesaid words, Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, who was adorned with ear-rings of refined gold, indignantly rushed towards Jaṭāyu, the king of winged creatures, his eyes red with anger. (1)

verses.text:
स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलस्तयोस्तस्मिन् महामृधे।
बभूव वातोद्धुतयोर्मेघयोर्गगने यथा॥ २॥
verses.m: The sustained exchange of blows which ensued between the two warriors (viz., Jaṭāyu and Rāvaṇa) in that great conflict was tumultuous like a clash between two clouds impelled by a blast in the sky. (2)

verses.text:
तद् बभूवाद्भुतं युद्धं गृध्रराक्षसयोस्तदा।
सपक्षयोर्माल्यवतोर्महापर्वतयोरिव ॥ ३॥
verses.m: The said conflict between a vulture (Jaṭāyu) and an ogre (Rāvaṇa) at that time was astounding like the encounter of the two large mountains known by the name of Mālyavān (one situated in the Daṇḍakāraṇya near Kiṣkindhā and the other near Mount Meru) and endowed with wings. (3)

verses.text:
ततो नालीकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णाग्रैश्च विकर्णिभिः।
अभ्यवर्षन्महाघोरैर्गृध्रराजं महाबलम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Thereupon Rāvaṇa assailed the king of vultures, who was possessed of great might, with most terrible Nālīkas, Nārācas and sharp-pointed Vikarṇis (three particular varieties of arrows). (4)

verses.text:
स तानि शरजालानि गृध्रः पत्ररथेश्वरः।
जटायुः प्रतिजग्राह रावणास्त्राणि संयुगे॥ ५॥
verses.m: In the encounter the celebrated vulture, Jaṭāyu, the king of winged creatures, put up with those volleys of arrows discharged by Rāvaṇa. (5)

verses.text:
तस्य तीक्ष्णनखाभ्यां तु चरणाभ्यां महाबलः।
चकार बहुधा गात्रे व्रणान् पतगसत्तमः॥ ६॥
verses.m: With his feet endowed with sharp talons, Jaṭāyu (the foremost of birds), for his part, who was possessed of great might, inflicted many wounds on the person of Rāvaṇa. (6)

verses.text:
अथ क्रोधाद् दशग्रीवो जग्राह दश मार्गणान्।
मृत्युदण्डनिभान् घोरान् शत्रोर्निधनकांक्षया॥ ७॥
verses.m: With intent to compass the death of his adversary, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) presently seized in anger ten dread arrows resembling the rod of Death. (7)

verses.text:
स तैर्बाणैर्महावीर्यः पूर्णमुक्तैरजिह्मगैः।
बिभेद निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गृध्रं घोरैः शिलीमुखैः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, who was possessed of extraordinary prowess, pierced the vulture with those straight-going, sharp and terrible barbed arrows whetted on a stone and discharged with full force. (8)

verses.text:
स राक्षसरथे पश्यञ्जानकीं बाष्पलोचनाम्।
अचिन्तयित्वा बाणांस्तान् राक्षसं समभिद्रवत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Beholding Sītā (daughter of Janaka) in the ogre’s chariot with tears in her eyes, and not minding those arrows, Jaṭāyu darted towards the ogre. (9)

verses.text:
ततोऽस्य सशरं चापं मुक्तामणिविभूषितम्।
चरणाभ्यां महातेजा बभञ्ज पतगोत्तमः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then Jaṭāyu (the foremost of birds), who was possessed of great energy, broke with his talons the bow, fitted with an arrow, of Rāvaṇa, artistically decked with pearls. (10)

verses.text:
ततोऽन्यद् धनुरादाय रावणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः।
ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thereupon, seizing another bow, Rāvaṇa, who was beside himself with anger, rained showers of arrows in hundreds and thousands. (11)

verses.text:
शरैरावारितस्तस्य संयुगे पतगेश्वरः।
कुलायमभिसम्प्राप्तः पक्षिवच्च बभौ तदा॥ १२॥
verses.m: Enclosed by the arrows of Rāvaṇa on the field of battle at that time, Jaṭāyu (the king of birds) looked like a bird having found shelter in a nest. (12)

verses.text:
स तानि शरजालानि पक्षाभ्यां तु विधूय ह।
चरणाभ्यां महातेजा बभञ्जास्य महद् धनुः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having shaken off that network of arrows with his wings, Jaṭāyu (who was endowed with great energy) for his part snapped the mighty bow of Rāvaṇa with his feet. (13)

verses.text:
तच्चाग्निसदृशं दीप्तं रावणस्य शरावरम्।
पक्षाभ्यां च महातेजा व्यधुनोत् पतगेश्वरः॥ १४॥
verses.m: The king of birds, who was endowed with great energy, also broke his coat of mail, blazing like fire. (14)

verses.text:
काञ्चनोरश्छदान् दिव्यान् पिशाचवदनान् खरान्।
तांश्चास्य जवसम्पन्नाञ्जघान समरे बली॥ १५॥
verses.m: The mighty bird further killed in the course of the encounter the celebrated swift-going heavenly mules of Rāvaṇa, endowed with the heads of fiends and protected by breast-plates of gold. (15)

verses.text:
अथ त्रिवेणुसम्पन्नं कामगं पावकार्चिषम्।
मणिसोपानचित्राङ्गं बभञ्ज च महारथम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Jaṭāyu presently smashed the huge chariot as well (of Rāvaṇa) provided with a pole to which the yoke is fixed and flaming like fire, which could go wherever one liked and whose frame looked charming with its steps of gems. (16)

verses.text:
पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतीकाशं छत्रं च व्यजनैः सह।
पातयामास वेगेन ग्राहिभी राक्षसैः सह॥ १७॥
verses.m: Jaṭāyu also knocked down with vehemence the canopy (over the seat of Rāvaṇa) shining as the full moon, alongwith the whisks as also the ogres holding them. (17)

verses.text:
सारथेश्चास्य वेगेन तुण्डेन च महच्छिरः।
पुनर्व्यपहनच्छ्रीमान् पक्षिराजो महाबलः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Nay, the glorious Jaṭāyu (the king of birds), who was possessed of great might, then vehemently struck off with his bill the big head of the charioteer of Rāvaṇa. (18)

verses.text:
स भग्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः।
अङ्केनादाय वैदेहीं पपात भुवि रावणः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Clasping in his arms Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), Rāvaṇa, whose bow had been broken, nay, who was left without a chariot and whose horses and charioteer had been killed—fell to the ground. (19)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा निपतितं भूमौ रावणं भग्नवाहनम्।
साधु साध्विति भूतानि गृध्रराजमपूजयन्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Seeing Rāvaṇa dashed to the ground, his chariot smashed, all beings applauded the king of vultures in the words “Well done, bravo !” (20)

verses.text:
परिश्रान्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा जरया पक्षियूथपम्।
उत्पपात पुनर्हृष्टो मैथिलीं गृह्य रावणः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Clasping the princess of Mithilā, Rāvaṇa, for his part—who felt rejoiced to see Jaṭāyu, the ruler of the feathered kingdom, exhausted due to age—rose once more to the heavens. (21)

verses.text:
तं प्रहृष्टं निधायाङ्के रावणं जनकात्मजाम्।
गच्छन्तं खड्गशेषं च प्रणष्टहतसाधनम्॥ २२॥
गृध्रराजः समुत्पत्य रावणं समभिद्रवत्।
समावार्य महातेजा जटायुरिदमब्रवीत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Springing up on his wings, the king of vultures rushed towards Rāvaṇa, who was now on his move, highly rejoiced, clasping the daughter of Janaka in his arms, the sword alone being left with him, all his other implements of war destroyed. Intercepting Rāvaṇa, Jaṭāyu (who was—endowed with great energy) spoke as follows to Rāvaṇa : (22-23)

verses.text:
वज्रसंस्पर्शबाणस्य भार्यां रामस्य रावण।
अल्पबुद्धे हरस्येनां वधाय खलु रक्षसाम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Surely it is for the destruction of ogres that you are carrying away this spouse of Śrī Rāma, whose arrows impinge on the body like the thunderbolt, O Rāvaṇa of meagre understanding ! (24)

verses.text:
समित्रबन्धुः सामात्यः सबलः सपरिच्छदः।
विषपानं पिबस्येतत् पिपासित इवोदकम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “With your near and dear ones, ministers, army and retinue you are drinking this beverage mixed with poison (in the shape of princess Sītā) as a thirsty man would drink water. (25)

verses.text:
अनुबन्धमजानन्तः कर्मणामविचक्षणाः।
शीघ्रमेव विनश्यन्ति यथा त्वं विनशिष्यसि॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Not foreseeing the result of their evil acts, unwise men perish very soon as you are going to perish. (26)

verses.text:
बद्धस्त्वं कालपाशेन क्व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे।
वधाय बडिशं गृह्य सामिषं जलजो यथा॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Caught as you are in the noose of Death, where can you hope to be delivered from it, like the fish which has swallowed a hook alongwith the bait? (27)

verses.text:
नहि जातु दुराधर्षौ काकुत्स्थौ तव रावण।
धर्षणं चाश्रमस्यास्य क्षमिष्येते तु राघवौ॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Nay, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Raghu, for their part, who are descended from the stock of Kakutstha, and are hard to overcome, will never on any account brook the violation of the sanctity of their hermitage. (28)

verses.text:
यथा त्वया कृतं कर्म भीरुणा लोकगर्हितम्।
तस्कराचरितो मार्गो नैष वीरनिषेवितः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “The way in which an act denounced by the world has been perpetrated by you, a coward that you are, is the path trodden by thieves; it is not the path followed by heroes. (29)

verses.text:
युद्ध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि मुहूर्तं तिष्ठ रावण।
शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ यथा भ्राता खरस्तथा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Fight with me, if you are a hero and pause awhile, O Rāvaṇa ! Struck dead by me, you will lie on the ground in the same way as did your brother Khara. (30)

verses.text:
परेतकाले पुरुषो यत् कर्म प्रतिपद्यते।
विनाशायात्मनोऽधर्म्यं प्रतिपन्नोऽसि कर्म तत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “For your own destruction you have adopted such an unrighteous conduct as a man does at the hour of death. (31)

verses.text:
पापानुबन्धो वै यस्य कर्मणः को नु तत् पुमान्।
कुर्वीत लोकाधिपतिः स्वयंभूर्भगवानपि॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “What man on earth, be he even Lord Brahmā (the self-born) and the ruler of all the worlds, would undertake an action that results invariably in sin?” (32)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा शुभं वाक्यं जटायुस्तस्य रक्षसः।
निपपात भृशं पृष्ठे दशग्रीवस्य वीर्यवान्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Uttering these wholesome words, the powerful Jaṭāyu swooped on the back of that ten-headed ogre. (33)

verses.text:
तं गृहीत्वा नखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विददार समन्ततः।
अधिरूढो गजारोहो यथा स्याद् दुष्टवारणम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Catching hold of the latter, he tore the ogre all over with his sharp talons as the rider of an elephant, mounted on it, would prick the elephant with his goad. (34)

verses.text:
विददार नखैरस्य तुण्डं पृष्ठे समर्पयन्।
केशांश्चोत्पाटयामास नखपक्षमुखायुधः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Plunging his beak into the ogre’s back, Jaṭāyu (who had claws, wings and a bill for his weapons) tore him and pulled his hair with his talons. (35)

verses.text:
स तथा गृध्रराजेन क्लिश्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः।
अमर्षस्फुरितोष्ठः सन् प्राकम्पत च राक्षसः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Nay, being tormented again and again by the king of vultures as aforesaid, the said ogre trembled with rage, his lips throbbing through indignation. (36)

verses.text:
सम्परिष्वज्य वैदेहीं वामेनाङ्केन रावणः।
तलेनाभिजघानार्तो जटायुं क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Pressing Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) tightly in his left lap, the afflicted Rāvaṇa, who was beside himself with rage, struck Jaṭāyu with the palm of his hand. (37)

verses.text:
जटायुस्तमतिक्रम्य तुण्डेनास्य खगाधिपः।
वामबाहून् दश तदा व्यपाहरदरिंदमः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Dodging that blow, Jaṭāyu, the king of birds, the chastiser of his foes, presently tore off his ten left arms with his beak. (38)

verses.text:
संछिन्नबाहोः सद्यो वै बाहवः सहसाभवन्।
विषज्वालावलीयुक्ता वल्मीकादिव पन्नगाः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Even though his ten arms had been severed, fresh arms sprang up all of a sudden even like serpents issuing from an ant-hill and emitting sprouts of poison. (39)

verses.text:
ततः क्रोधाद् दशग्रीवः सीतामुत्सृज्य वीर्यवान्।
मुष्टिभ्यां चरणाभ्यां च गृध्रराजमपोथयत्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Thereupon, letting alone Sītā, the powerful Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) angrily struck the king of vultures with his fists and feet. (40)

verses.text:
ततो मुहूर्तं संग्रामो बभूवातुलवीर्ययोः।
राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य पक्षिणां प्रवरस्य च॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Then, for an hour or so, a duel ensued between the two warriors of incomparable prowess, Rāvaṇa, the foremost of ogres, and Jaṭāyu, the chief of vultures. (41)

verses.text:
तस्य व्यायच्छमानस्य रामस्यार्थे स रावणः।
पक्षौ पादौ च पार्श्वौ च खड्गमुद्धृत्य सोऽच्छिनत्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Again, unsheathing his sword, the said Rāvaṇa lopped off the wings, the feet and the flanks too of Jaṭāyu, who was contending in the cause of Śrī Rāma. (42)

verses.text:
स च्छिन्नपक्षः सहसा रक्षसा रौद्रकर्मणा।
निपपात महागृध्रो धरण्यामल्पजीवितः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: With his wings sundered all at once by the ogre of fierce deeds, the great vulture, whose life was now of short duration, dropped down on the ground. (43)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा पतितं भूमौ क्षतजार्द्रं जटायुषम्।
अभ्यधावत वैदेही स्वबन्धुमिव दुःखिता॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Distressed to see Jaṭāyu fallen on the ground drenched with blood, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, rushed towards him as towards one of her own kin. (44)

verses.text:
तं नीलजीमूतनिकाशकल्पं
सपाण्डुरोरस्कमुदारवीर्यम्।
ददर्श लङ्काधिपतिः पृथिव्यां
जटायुषं शान्तमिवाग्निदावम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: The said Rāvaṇa (the sovereign ruler of Laṅkā) beheld the celebrated Jaṭāyu of exalted prowess—who approached the splendour of a dark-blue cloud and was marked with a white breast—lying on the ground like an extinguished forest fire. (45)

verses.text:
ततस्तु तं पत्ररथं महीतले
निपातितं रावणवेगमर्दितम्।
पुनश्च संगृह्य शशिप्रभानना
रुरोद सीता जनकात्मजा तदा॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Then, embracing the aforesaid bird, who had been fatally injured by the vehemence of Rāvaṇa and thrown on the ground, Sītā, daughter of Janaka, for her part, whose countenance shone like the moon, cried once more on that occasion. (46)

verses.text:
सा तु ताराधिपमुखी रावणेन निरीक्ष्य तम्।
गृध्रराजं विनिहतं विललाप सुदुःखिता॥ १॥
verses.m: Sore distressed to perceive the aforesaid king of vultures mortally wounded by Rāvaṇa, Sītā, whose countenance resembled the full moon (the king of stars), for her part wailed as follows addressing Śrī Rāma : (1)

verses.text:
निमित्तं लक्षणं स्वप्नं शकुनिस्वरदर्शनम्।
अवश्यं सुखदुःखेषु नराणां परिदृश्यते॥ २॥
verses.m: “Omens, dreams and the sight of the movement of birds and deer etc., to one’s left or right and the hearing of their cries are invariably found to foreshadow joy or sorrow in the case of human beings. (2)

verses.text:
न नूनं राम जानासि महद्व्यसनमात्मनः।
धावन्ति नूनं काकुत्स्थ मदर्थं मृगपक्षिणः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Surely, O Rāma, you do not perceive the great calamity in the shape of my abduction which has befallen you, although deer and birds are moving in a direction foreboding evil in order to indicate my abduction, O scion of Kakutstha ! (3)

verses.text:
अयं हि कृपया राम मां त्रातुमिह संगतः।
शेते विनिहतो भूमौ ममाभाग्याद् विहंगमः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Here lies on the ground, mortally wounded due to my misfortune, the bird, Jaṭāyu, who actually arrived here to rescue me out of compassion, O Rāma ! (4)

verses.text:
त्राहि मामद्य काकुत्स्थ लक्ष्मणेति वराङ्गना।
सुसंत्रस्ता समाक्रन्दच्छृण्वतां तु यथान्तिके॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Deliver me today, O Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, and Lakṣmaṇa !” So did Sītā (a lovely lady), who was greatly alarmed, cry bitterly at such a pitch that those listening at close quarters at least might hear her. (5)

verses.text:
तां क्लिष्टमाल्याभरणां विलपन्तीमनाथवत्।
अभ्यधावत वैदेहीं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, darted towards the aforesaid Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), whose garland and ornaments had been squeezed and who was wailing like a woman without her lord. (6)

verses.text:
तां लतामिव वेष्टन्तीमालिङ्गन्तीं महाद्रुमान्।
मुञ्च मुञ्चेति बहुशः प्राप तां राक्षसाधिपः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of ogres) approached the aforesaid Sītā—who was embracing huge trees like a climber entwining them—saying again and again, “Save, Save me, O trees ! (7)

verses.text:
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति रामेण रहितां वने।
जीवितान्ताय केशेषु जग्राहान्तकसंनिभः॥ ८॥
verses.m: For his destruction the ogre (who resembled Death) seized by the hair Sītā, who was crying “Rāma, O Rāma !” bereft as she was of Śrī Rāma in the forest. (8)

verses.text:
प्रधर्षितायां वैदेह्यां बभूव सचराचरम्।
जगत् सर्वममर्यादं तमसान्धेन संवृतम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: When Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, was assaulted in this way, the whole world including the animate and inanimate creation went out of order and was enveloped in thick darkness. (9)

verses.text:
न वाति मारुतस्तत्र निष्प्रभोऽभूद् दिवाकरः।
दृष्ट्वा सीतां परामृष्टां देवो दिव्येन चक्षुषा॥ १०॥
कृतं कार्यमिति श्रीमान् व्याजहार पितामहः।
प्रहृष्टा व्यथिताश्चासन् सर्वे ते परमर्षयः॥ ११॥
दृष्ट्वा सीतां परामृष्टां दण्डकारण्यवासिनः।
रावणस्य विनाशं च प्राप्तं बुद्ध्वा यदृच्छया॥ १२॥
verses.m: The wind did not blow at that moment and the sun grew lustreless. Perceiving by his divine eye Sītā, laid violent hands on by Rāvaṇa, the glorious Lord Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation) exclaimed: “Our purpose is accomplished!” Seeing Sītā seized by Rāvaṇa, all the great sages dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest and mentioned before, felt agonized. They were also highly rejoiced to foresee the destruction of Rāvaṇa brought about as a matter of course. (10—12)

verses.text:
स तु तां राम रामेति रुदतीं लक्ष्मणेति च।
जगामादाय चाकाशं रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Nay, laying hold of Sītā, who was crying “Rāma, O Rāma, O Lakṣmaṇa !” Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, rose to the skies. (13)

verses.text:
तप्ताभरणवर्णाङ्गी पीतकौशेयवासिनी।
रराज राजपुत्री तु विद्युत्सौदामनी यथा॥ १४॥
verses.m: With her limbs possessing the hue of her ornaments of molten gold and clad in yellow silk, the princess for her part shone like lightning athwart a cloud. (14)

verses.text:
उद्धूतेन च वस्त्रेण तस्याः पीतेन रावणः।
अधिकं परिबभ्राज गिरिर्दीप्त इवाग्निना॥ १५॥
verses.m: Because of her yellow garment being shaken violently by the wind, Rāvaṇa shone all the more brightly like a mountain illumined by a fire. (15)

verses.text:
तस्याः परमकल्याण्यास्ताम्राणि सुरभीणि च।
पद्मपत्राणि वैदेह्या अभ्यकीर्यन्त रावणम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: The coppery and fragrant petals of lotuses dropping from the person of the aforesaid supremely blessed Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, covered Rāvaṇa. (16)

verses.text:
तस्याः कौशेयमुद्धूतमाकाशे कनकप्रभम्।
बभौ चादित्यरागेण ताम्रमभ्रमिवातपे॥ १७॥
verses.m: Nay, shaken violently in the air, her silken garment possessing a golden hue, shone like a cloud rendered coppery by the sun’s rays at dusk. (17)

verses.text:
तस्यास्तद् विमलं वक्त्रमाकाशे रावणाङ्कगम्।
न रराज विना रामं विनालमिव पङ्कजम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Lying in the lap of Rāvaṇa in the air, that fair countenance of Sītā did not shine, bereft as it was of Śrī Rāma, any more than a lotus detached from its stalk. (18)

verses.text:
बभूव जलदं नीलं भित्त्वा चन्द्र इवोदितः।
सुललाटं सुकेशान्तं पद्मगर्भाभमव्रणम्॥ १९॥
शुक्लैः सुविमलैर्दन्तैः प्रभावद्भिरलंकृतम्।
तस्याः सुनयनं वक्त्रमाकाशे रावणाङ्कगम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Marked with a fair brow, lovely locks and charming eyes and resembling the interior of a lotus in hue, nay, devoid of scars and adorned with white, entirely spotless and brilliant teeth, her countenance placed in the lap of Rāvaṇa in the air resembled the moon emerged after splitting a cloud. (19-20)

verses.text:
रुदितं व्यपमृष्टास्रं चन्द्रवत्प्रियदर्शनम्।
सुनासं चारुताम्रोष्ठमाकाशे हाटकप्रभम्॥ २१॥
राक्षसेन्द्रसमाधूतं तस्यास्तद् वदनं शुभम्।
शुशुभे न विना रामं दिवा चन्द्र इवोदितः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Shaken with fear of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), that lovely face of Sītā—which had just burst into tears, although her tears had been wiped off, nay which was pleasing like the moon to look upon, was marked with a shapely nose and beautiful coppery lips and possessed a golden hue—did not look charming in the heavens in the absence of Śrī Rāma any more than the moon risen during the day. (21-22)

verses.text:
सा हेमवर्णा नीलाङ्गं मैथिली राक्षसाधिपम्।
शुशुभे काञ्चनी काञ्ची नीलं गजमिवाश्रिता॥ २३॥
verses.m: Confined in the lap of the dark-bodied Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of ogres), the said princess of Mithilā, who possessed a golden hue, shone brightly like a girth of gold round a dark-blue elephant. (23)

verses.text:
सा पद्मपीता हेमाभा रावणं जनकात्मजा।
विद्युद् घनमिवाविश्य शुशुभे तप्तभूषणा॥ २४॥
verses.m: Nearing Rāvaṇa’s back, the said daughter of Janaka—who possessed a yellowish hue, resembling the filaments of a lotus, and was bright as gold, nay, who was adorned with jewels of refined gold—shone like lightning flashing athwart a cloud. (24)

verses.text:
तस्या भूषणघोषेण वैदेह्या राक्षसेश्वरः।
बभूव विमलो नीलः सघोष इव तोयदः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Due to the jingling of ornaments of the aforesaid Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) the king of ogres appeared like a clear dark-blue rumbling rain-cloud. (25)

verses.text:
उत्तमाङ्गच्युता तस्याः पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः।
सीताया ह्रियमाणायाः पपात धरणीतले॥ २६॥
verses.m: While Sītā was being borne away, a shower of flowers dropped from her head, rained on all sides on the earth’s surface. (26)

verses.text:
सा तु रावणवेगेन पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः।
समाधूता दशग्रीवं पुनरेवाभ्यवर्तत॥ २७॥
verses.m: Raised on all sides by the tempest released by the vehemence of Rāvaṇa, however, the rain of blossoms covered the ten-headed monster once more. (27)

verses.text:
अभ्यवर्तत पुष्पाणां धारा वैश्रवणानुजम्।
नक्षत्रमाला विमला मेरुं नगमिवोन्नतम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: That shower of flowers descended on Rāvaṇa (a younger half-brother of Kubera) as does the immaculate belt of the lunar mansions descend on Mount Meru, the foremost of mountains. (28)

verses.text:
चरणान्नूपुरं भ्रष्टं वैदेह्या रत्नभूषितम्।
विद्युन्मण्डलसंकाशं पपात धरणीतले॥ २९॥
verses.m: A bejewelled anklet of gold, loosed from a foot of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) and resembling a circular flash of lightning, dropped on the earth’s surface.(29)

verses.text:
तरुप्रवालरक्ता सा नीलाङ्गं राक्षसेश्वरम्।
प्रशोभयत वैदेही गजं कक्ष्येव काञ्चनी॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Ruddy like the shoots of certain trees, the aforesaid princess of the Videha kingdom adorned the dark-limbed king of ogres as a girth of gold would adorn an elephant. (30)

verses.text:
तां महोल्कामिवाकाशे दीप्यमानां स्वतेजसा।
जहाराकाशमाविश्य सीतां वैश्रवणानुजः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Betaking himself to the heavens, the younger brother of Kubera, Rāvaṇa (son of Sage Viśravā), bore away the celebrated Sītā, who was blazing with her own effulgence as a big meteor in the heavens. (31)

verses.text:
तस्यास्तान्यग्निवर्णानि भूषणानि महीतले।
सघोषाण्यवशीर्यन्त क्षीणास्तारा इवाम्बरात्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: The aforesaid jewels of Sītā, shining like fire, dropped on the earth’s surface with a jingling sound like worn-away meteors falling from the firmament. (32)

verses.text:
तस्याः स्तनान्तराद् भ्रष्टो हारस्ताराधिपद्युतिः।
वैदेह्या निपतन् भाति गङ्गेव गगनच्युता॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Dissociated from the heart of the aforesaid princess of the Videha territory and dropping down, the necklace of pearls, which shone like the moon (the suzerain lord of stars) looked like the Gaṅgā descending from the heavens. (33)

verses.text:
उत्पातवाताभिरता नानाद्विजगणायुताः।
मा भैरिति विधूताग्रा व्याजह्रुरिव पादपाः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Violently shaken by a portentous blast (released by the flight of Rāvaṇa) and inhabited by birds of every description, the trees with their topmost branches set into motion said (to Sītā) as it were : “Don’t be afraid !” (34)

verses.text:
नलिन्यो ध्वस्तकमलास्त्रस्तमीनजलेचराः।
सखीमिव गतोत्साहां शोचन्तीव स्म मैथिलीम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: With their faded lotuses and frightened fishes and other aquatic creatures, the lotus-ponds, as it were, felt sorry for the princess of Mithilā as for a dispirited friend. (35)

verses.text:
समन्तादभिसम्पत्य सिंहव्याघ्रमृगद्विजाः।
अन्वधावंस्तदा रोषात् सीताच्छायानुगामिनः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Collecting from all sides, lions, tigers, as well as other beasts and birds angrily rushed behind on that occasion following the shadow of Sītā. (36)

verses.text:
जलप्रपातास्रमुखाः शृङ्गैरुच्छ्रितबाहुभिः।
सीतायां ह्रियमाणायां विक्रोशन्तीव पर्वताः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: While Sītā was being carried away by Rāvaṇa, mountains with their faces bathed in tears in the form of cataracts and with their arms uplifted in the form of peaks, screamed, as it were. (37)

verses.text:
ह्रियमाणां तु वैदेहीं दृष्ट्वा दीनो दिवाकरः।
प्रविध्वस्तप्रभः श्रीमानासीत् पाण्डुरमण्डलः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Seeing Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, being borne away by Rāvaṇa, the glorious sun itself felt wretched with its splendour totally eclipsed and its orb rendered pale. (38)

verses.text:
नास्ति धर्मः कुतः सत्यं नार्जवं नानृशंसता।
यत्र रामस्य वैदेहीं सीतां हरति रावणः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Righteousness is extinct, how then could truth prevail? Guilelessness is no more, nor is there kindness, now that Rāvaṇa is carrying away Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, and the consort of Śrī Rāma !” (39)

verses.text:
इति भूतानि सर्वाणि गणशः पर्यदेवयन्।
वित्रस्तका दीनमुखा रुरुदुर्मृगपोतकाः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: So did all living beings lament in multitudes. Even fawns shed tears with dejected looks, greatly alarmed. (40)

verses.text:
उद्वीक्ष्योद्वीक्ष्य नयनैर्भयादिव विलक्षणैः।
सुप्रवेपितगात्राश्च बभूवुर्वनदेवताः॥ ४१॥
विक्रोशन्तीं दृढं सीतां दृष्ट्वा दुःखं तथा गताम्।
तां तु लक्ष्मण रामेति क्रोशन्तीं मधुरस्वराम्॥ ४२॥
अवेक्षमाणां बहुशो वैदेहीं धरणीतलम्।
स तामाकुलकेशान्तां विप्रमृष्टविशेषकाम्।
जहारात्मविनाशाय दशग्रीवो मनस्विनीम्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Seeing Sītā fallen in great distress as aforesaid and uttering a loud cry, and looking at her again and again with eyes shorn of their lustre, the deities presiding over the forest found their limbs seized with a violent tremor through fear of Rāvaṇa. To his own destruction Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), however, carried away the aforesaid princess of the Videha territory, that strong-minded lady, who was crying in sweet accents : “Lakṣmaṇa, O Rāma !!” and repeatedly looking towards the earth’s surface, whose hair had got dishevelled and whose auspicious mark on the forehead had effaced. (41—43)

verses.text:
ततस्तु सा चारुदती शुचिस्मिता
विनाकृता बन्धुजनेन मैथिली।
अपश्यती राघवलक्ष्मणावुभौ
विवर्णवक्त्रा भयभारपीडिता॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Bereft of her own kin and failing to perceive both Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) and Lakṣmaṇa, the aforesaid princess of Mithilā for her part, who had beautiful teeth and was distinguished by a bright smile, was oppressed by the weight of fear and her face grew pale. (44)

verses.text:
खमुत्पतन्तं तं दृष्ट्वा मैथिली जनकात्मजा।
दुःखिता परमोद्विग्ना भये महति वर्तिनी॥ १॥
रोषरोदनताम्राक्षी भीमाक्षं राक्षसाधिपम्।
रुदती करुणं सीता ह्रियमाणा तमब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Distressed and greatly alarmed to see the aforesaid Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, of fearful eyes rising to the heavens, Sītā, a princess of Mithilā and daughter of Janaka—who was involved in a great risk (of losing her honour and chastity) and whose eyes had grown red through indignation and weeping—spoke to him as follows, crying piteously while being borne away through the sky : (1-2)

verses.text:
न व्यपत्रपसे नीच कर्मणानेन रावण।
ज्ञात्वा विरहितां यो मां चोरयित्वा पलायसे॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Do you not feel ashamed of this act, O vile Rāvaṇa—you, who, having stealthily abducted me, knowing me to be alone, are fleeing away like a coward? (3)

verses.text:
त्वयैव नूनं दुष्टात्मन् भीरुणा हर्तुमिच्छता।
ममापवाहितो भर्ता मृगरूपेण मायया॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Seeking to abduct me, surely it was you alone, O evil-minded fellow, who caused my husband to be lured away by an ogre appearing in the disguise of a deer through a conjuring trick, timid as you are. (4)

verses.text:
यो हि मामुद्यतस्त्रातुं सोऽप्ययं विनिपातितः।
गृध्रराजः पुराणोऽसौ श्वशुरस्य सखा मम॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Even the yonder aged Jaṭāyu, the king of vultures, a friend of my father-in-law, who actually strove to rescue me, lies killed there. (5)

verses.text:
परमं खलु ते वीर्यं दृश्यते राक्षसाधम।
विश्राव्य नामधेयं हि युद्धे नास्मि जिता त्वया॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Indeed the highest valour is seen in you in that I have not been won by you in a combat with my husband even after disclosing your name, O vile ogre ! (6)

verses.text:
ईदृशं गर्हितं कर्म कथं कृत्वा न लज्जसे।
स्त्रियाश्चाहरणं नीच रहिते च परस्य च॥ ७॥
verses.m: “How do you not feel ashamed even after perpetrating such a reproachful act as bearing away a woman, much more the wife of another, and that too in a lonely place where there is none to protect her? (7)

verses.text:
कथयिष्यन्ति लोकेषु पुरुषाः कर्म कुत्सितम्।
सुनृशंसमधर्मिष्ठं तव शौटीर्यमानिनः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “People will poclaim throughout the worlds the aforesaid act of yours—even though you pride yourself on your valour—as reproachful, extremely cruel and most unrighteous. (8)

verses.text:
धिक् ते शौर्यं च सत्त्वं च यत्त्वया कथितं तदा।
कुलाक्रोशकरं लोके धिक् ते चारित्रमीदृशम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Fie upon your valour and energy too, of which you spoke at that time. And accursed in the world is such conduct of yours, which brings reproach on your race! (9)

verses.text:
किं शक्यं कर्तुमेवं हि यज्जवेनैव धावसि।
मुहूर्तमपि तिष्ठ त्वं न जीवन् प्रतियास्यसि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Of course, what can be done just at this moment when you are flying with such speed? Halt you but for an hour or so and you will not return alive. (10)

verses.text:
नहि चक्षुःपथं प्राप्य तयोः पार्थिवपुत्रयोः।
ससैन्योऽपि समर्थस्त्वं मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Having reached the range of sight of those two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, you will surely not be able to survive even for an hour or so, no matter if you are followed by an army. (11)

verses.text:
न त्वं तयोः शरस्पर्शं सोढुं शक्तः कथंचन।
वने प्रज्वलितस्येव स्पर्शमग्नेर्विहंगमः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “You will in no way be able to bear the impact of their arrows any more than a bird is able to bear the impact of a blazing fire in a forest. (12)

verses.text:
साधु कृत्वाऽऽत्मनः पथ्यं साधु मां मुञ्च रावण।
मत्प्रधर्षणसंक्रुद्धो भ्रात्रा सह पतिर्मम॥ १३॥
विधास्यति विनाशाय त्वं मां यदि न मुञ्चसि।
येन त्वं व्यवसायेन बलान्मां हर्तुमिच्छसि॥ १४॥
व्यवसायस्तु ते नीच भविष्यति निरर्थकः।
नह्यहं तमपश्यन्ती भर्तारं विबुधोपमम्॥ १५॥
उत्सहे शत्रुवशगा प्राणान् धारयितुं चिरम्।
न नूनं चात्मनः श्रेयः पथ्यं वा समवेक्षसे॥ १६॥
मृत्युकाले यथा मर्त्यो विपरीतानि सेवते।
मुमूर्षूणां तु सर्वेषां यत् पथ्यं तन्न रोचते॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Therefore, duly considering your own welfare, you had better leave me alone, O Rāvaṇa ! Enraged by my abduction, my lord with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, will strive for your destruction if you do not let me go. Your sinister purpose, for which you seek to bear me away by force, O mean fellow, will undoubtedly prove infructuous. For if, when fallen into the clutches of an enemy, I fail to behold my husband, who vies with gods, I shall not be able to sustain my life for long. Surely you do not look to your own immediate good or your lasting good and, even as a man who has reached the hour of death relishes objects which run counter to his interests, you also do the same. As a rule, that which is good for one’s health does not find favour with all those who are about to die. (13—17)

verses.text:
पश्यामीह हि कण्ठे त्वां कालपाशावपाशितम्।
यथा चास्मिन् भयस्थाने न बिभेषि निशाचर॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I know you to be caught in the noose of Death about your neck indeed, in that you do not feel diffident in embarking on this risky adventure of abducting the virtuous wife of a hero, O prowler of the night ! (18)

verses.text:
व्यक्तं हिरण्मयांस्त्वं हि सम्पश्यसि महीरुहान्।
नदीं वैतरणीं घोरां रुधिरौघविवाहिनीम्॥ १९॥
खड्गपत्रवनं चैव भीमं पश्यसि रावण।
तप्तकाञ्चनपुष्पां च वैदूर्यप्रवरच्छदाम्॥ २०॥
द्रक्ष्यसे शाल्मलीं तीक्ष्णामायसैः कण्टकैश्चिताम्।
नहि त्वमीदृशं कृत्वा तस्यालीकं महात्मनः॥ २१॥
धारितुं शक्ष्यसि चिरं विषं पीत्वेव निर्घृण।
बद्धस्त्वं कालपाशेन दुर्निवारेण रावण॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Obviously you are vividly viewing trees as made of gold (an unmistakable sign of approaching death). Nay, you are going to see in the near future, O Rāvaṇa, the fearful river Vaitaraṇī, carrying a flood of blood in place of water as well as the dreadful grove known by the name of Asipatravana (a hell of this name depicted as consisting of a cluster of trees or shrubs with leaves sharp-edged as a sword) and will behold a dentate Śālmalī (a silk-cotton tree) containing flowers of heated gold and leaves of excellent cat’s eye gems and bristling with thorns of steel. Having done such a grievous wrong to the high-souled Śrī Rāma, you shall not be able to survive long any more than on drinking poison, O merciless ogre ! You are caught in the noose of Death, which is difficult to repulse, O Rāvaṇa ! (19—22)

verses.text:
क्व गतो लप्स्यसे शर्म मम भर्तुर्महात्मनः।
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण विना भ्रातरमाहवे॥ २३॥
राक्षसा निहता येन सहस्राणि चतुर्दश।
कथं स राघवो वीरः सर्वास्त्रकुशलो बली॥ २४॥
न त्वां हन्याच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैरिष्टभार्यापहारिणम्।
एतच्चान्यच्च परुषं वैदेही रावणाङ्कगा।
भयशोकसमाविष्टा करुणं विललाप ह॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Transferred to which place will you get shelter from the rage of my high-minded husband? How will the aforesaid Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, a mighty hero, who is adept in the use of all mystic missiles, not despatch with sharp arrows you, who are carrying away his beloved spouse?” Having uttered these and many other harsh words, while still etrapped by Rāvaṇa, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, who was fully possessed with fear and grief, wailed piteously: so the tradition goes. (23—25)

verses.text:
तदा भृशार्तां बहु चैव भाषिणीं
विलापपूर्वं करुणं च भामिनीम्।
जहार पापस्तरुणीं विचेष्टतीं
नृपात्मजामागतगात्रवेपथुः ॥ २६॥
verses.m: The villain, however, continued to bear away the lovely and youthful princess, who was talking much in a pathetic tone in the wake of crying, sore distressed as she was, and was struggling hard all the time to get released, although a tremor ran through his limbs. (26)

verses.text:
ह्रियमाणा तु वैदेही कंचिन्नाथमपश्यती।
ददर्श गिरिशृङ्गस्थान् पञ्च वानरपुङ्गवान्॥ १॥
verses.m: Not finding any saviour while being carried away by Rāvaṇa, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, for her part caught sight of five Vānara (monkey) chiefs sitting on a mountain-peak. (1)

verses.text:
तेषां मध्ये विशालाक्षी कौशेयं कनकप्रभम्।
उत्तरीयं वरारोहा शुभान्याभरणानि च॥ २॥
मुमोच यदि रामाय शंसेयुरिति भामिनी।
वस्त्रमुत्सृज्य तन्मध्ये निक्षिप्तं सहभूषणम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: The lovely lady with large eyes and other comely limbs took off from her person her silken upper garment, brilliant as gold, as well as her shining jewels. Having placed other articles of her wearing apparel in the said garment, the latter was dropped alongwith the jewels in the midst of the monkeys in the hope that they might break the news of her being carried away by Rāvaṇa to Śrī Rāma if he ever happened to meet them. (2-3)

verses.text:
सम्भ्रमात् तु दशग्रीवस्तत्कर्म च न बुद्धवान्।
पिङ्गाक्षास्तां विशालाक्षीं नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव॥ ४॥
विक्रोशन्तीं तदा सीतां ददृशुर्वानरोत्तमाः।
स च पम्पामतिक्रम्य लङ्कामभिमुखः पुरीम्॥ ५॥
जगाम मैथिलीं गृह्य रुदतीं राक्षसेश्वरः।
तां जहार सुसंहृष्टो रावणो मृत्युमात्मनः॥ ६॥
उत्सङ्गेनैव भुजगीं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रां महाविषाम्।
वनानि सरितः शैलान् सरांसि च विहायसा॥ ७॥
स क्षिप्रं समतीयाय शरश्चापादिव च्युतः।
तिमिनक्रनिकेतं तु वरुणालयमक्षयम्॥ ८॥
सरितां शरणं गत्वा समतीयाय सागरम्।
सम्भ्रमात् परिवृत्तोर्मी रुद्धमीनमहोरगः॥ ९॥
वैदेह्यां ह्रियमाणायां बभूव वरुणालयः।
अन्तरिक्षगता वाचः ससृजुश्चारणास्तदा॥ १०॥
एतदन्तो दशग्रीव इति सिद्धास्तथाब्रुवन्।
स तु सीतां विचेष्टन्तीमङ्केनादाय रावणः॥ ११॥
प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां रूपिणीं मृत्युमात्मनः।
सोऽभिगम्य पुरीं लङ्कां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्॥ १२॥
संरूढकक्ष्यां बहुलां स्वमन्तःपुरमाविशत्।
तत्र तामसितापाङ्गीं शोकमोहसमन्विताम्॥ १३॥
निदधे रावणः सीतां मयो मायामिवासुरीम्।
अब्रवीच्च दशग्रीवः पिशाचीर्घोरदर्शनाः॥ १४॥
यथा नैनां पुमान् स्त्री वा सीतां पश्यत्यसम्मतः।
मुक्तामणिसुवर्णानि वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च॥ १५॥
यद् यदिच्छेत् तदैवास्या देयं मच्छन्दतो यथा।
या च वक्ष्यति वैदेहीं वचनं किंचिदप्रियम्॥ १६॥
अज्ञानाद् यदि वा ज्ञानान्न तस्या जीवितं प्रियम्।
तथोक्त्वा राक्षसीस्तास्तु राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्॥ १७॥
निष्क्रम्यान्तःपुरात् तस्मात् किं कृत्यमिति चिन्तयन्।
ददर्शाष्टौ महावीर्यान् राक्षसान् पिशिताशनान्॥ १८॥
verses.m: In his flurry, however, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) did not at all perceive the aforesaid act of Sītā. The tawny-eyed monkey chiefs then beheld with unwinking eyes as it were (through wonder and compassion) that large-eyed Sītā crying loudly. Having passed beyond the Pampā lake, that ruler of ogres proceeded with his face towards the city of Laṅkā, taking the princess of Mithilā, who continued to cry all the time. Extremely delighted, Rāvaṇa bore in his arms his own death in the form of Sītā as one would carry in one’s arms a highly venomous female serpent with sharp fangs. Coursing through the air like an arrow shot from a bow, he quickly left clearly behind forests, rivers, mountains and lakes. Having reached the Indian ocean, the abode of Timis (a species of fish of an enormous size) and crocodiles, the seat of Varuṇa (the god of waters), which knows no depletion, and the resting-place of rivers, Rāvaṇa for his part passed clearly beyond it. While Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) was being carried away by Rāvaṇa, the ocean (the seat of Varuṇa) found its billows brought to a standstill and its fishes and large aquatic serpents rendered motionless due to fear of Rāvaṇa. At that moment Cāraṇas (the celestial bards) standing in the airspace uttered the following remark : “This act of bearing away Sītā marks the end of Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster.” The Siddhas too spoke likewise. Bearing in his arms Sītā, his death-incarnate, the said Rāvaṇa for his part entered the city of Laṅkā. Reaching the large city of Laṅkā, which contained well-ramified roads and whose gateways remained thronged with people, he entered his own gynaeceum. There Rāvaṇa lodged the celebrated Sītā, who was noted for the dark corners of her eyes and was seized with grief and infatuation—even as the demon Maya (the suzerain lord of Tripura) would shed his demoniac Māyā (conjuring trick). Nay, Rāvaṇa commanded fiendesses of terrible aspect as follows : “Take care that no unauthorized man or woman looks on Sītā. Pearls, gems and gold, articles of wearing apparel and ornaments—whatever she desires should be supplied to her that very moment in deference to my wishes according to her choice. Nay, I presume life is not dear to the ogress who utters any harsh word to her through ignorance or consciously.” Having instructed the aforesaid ogresses accordingly and sallying forth from that gynaeceum contemplating as to what should be done next, the powerful Rāvaṇa (the king of ogres) for his part granted interview to eight exceptionally powerful flesh-eating ogres. (4—18)

verses.text:
स तान् दृष्ट्वा महावीर्यो वरदानेन मोहितः।
उवाच तानिदं वाक्यं प्रशस्य बलवीर्यतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Having met and extolled them on the score of their strength and prowess, and blinded by the boon he had received from Brahmā, the exceptionally powerful Rāvaṇa spoke to them as follows : (19)

verses.text:
नानाप्रहरणाः क्षिप्रमितो गच्छत सत्वराः।
जनस्थानं हतस्थानं भूतपूर्वं खरालयम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Equipped with diverse weapons proceed at once from this place with all speed to Janasthāna, which was formerly the abode of Khara, but whose dwellings have since been laid waste by Rāma. (20)

verses.text:
तत्रास्यतां जनस्थाने शून्ये निहतराक्षसे।
पौरुषं बलमाश्रित्य त्रासमुत्सृज्य दूरतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Relying on your own manliness and strength and casting off fear at a distance, get yourself established in the said Janasthāna, which is now desolate, the ogres living there having been exterminated by Rāma. (21)

verses.text:
बहुसैन्यं महावीर्यं जनस्थाने निवेशितम्।
सदूषणखरं युद्धे निहतं रामसायकैः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The very powerful and large army stationed in Janasthāna has been wiped out on the battlefield alongwith Dūṣaṇa and Khara by the arrows of Rāma. (22)

verses.text:
ततः क्रोधो ममापूर्वो धैर्यस्योपरि वर्धते।
वैरं च सुमहज्जातं रामं प्रति सुदारुणम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “As a sequel to it a rage which was never known before has taken possession of me and is growing beyond the limits of forbearance. Nay, a very great and fierce enmity has since then been set up with Rāma. (23)

verses.text:
निर्यातयितुमिच्छामि तच्च वैरं महारिपोः।
नहि लप्स्याम्यहं निद्रामहत्वा संयुगे रिपुम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “I wish to put an end to the enmity by being quits with my great enemy, Rāma, and I shall not get a wink of sleep till I have slain the enemy in battle. (24)

verses.text:
तं त्विदानीमहं हत्वा खरदूषणघातिनम्।
रामं शर्मोपलप्स्यामि धनं लब्ध्वेव निर्धनः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “I shall have peace of mind now only after killing the slayer of Khara and Dūṣaṇa, as a destitute would on obtaining wealth. (25)

verses.text:
जनस्थाने वसद्भिस्तु भवद्भी राममाश्रिता।
प्रवृत्तिरुपनेतव्या किं करोतीति तत्त्वतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Information bearing on Rāma as to what he is doing should be correctly made available to me by you while staying in Janasthāna. (26)

verses.text:
अप्रमादाच्च गन्तव्यं सर्वैरेव निशाचरैः।
कर्तव्यश्च सदा यत्नो राघवस्य वधं प्रति॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Journey should be undertaken by all the rangers of the night with vigilance and an endeavour should always be made for the destruction of Rāma. (27)

verses.text:
युस्माकं तु बलं ज्ञातं बहुशो रणमूर्धनि।
अतश्चास्मिञ्जनस्थाने मया यूयं निवेशिताः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Your strength, of course, has been witnessed on many an occasion in the van of fight and hence you have been selected by me for being stationed in yonder Janasthāna.” (28)

verses.text:
ततः प्रियं वाक्यमुपेत्य राक्षसा
महार्थमष्टावभिवाद्य रावणम्।
विहाय लङ्कां सहिताः प्रतस्थिरे
यतो जनस्थानमलक्ष्यदर्शनाः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Receiving the command couched in endearing terms and full of deep meaning, nay, greeting Rāvaṇa and quitting Laṅkā, all the eight ogres thereupon set out towards the quarter in which lay Janasthāna, their body remaining invisible. (29)

verses.text:
ततस्तु सीतामुपलभ्य रावणः
सुसम्प्रहृष्टः परिगृह्य मैथिलीम्।
प्रसज्य रामेण च वैरमुत्तमं
बभूव मोहान्मुदितः स रावणः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Extremely rejoiced to secure Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, and having placed her within the four walls of his gynaeceum and having set up bitter enmity with Śrī Rāma, the aforesaid Rāvaṇa, for his part, who made people cry by his cruel deeds, felt happy through ignorance. (30)

verses.text:
संदिश्य राक्षसान् घोरान् रावणोऽष्टौ महाबलान्।
आत्मानं बुद्धिवैक्लव्यात् कृत्कृत्यममन्यत॥ १॥
verses.m: Having given instruction to the eight fierce ogres of inordinate strength to leave for Janasthāna, Rāvaṇa thought, due to perversity of intellect, that he had accomplished his object. (1)

verses.text:
स चिन्तयानो वैदेहीं कामबाणैः प्रपीडितः।
प्रविवेश गृहं रम्यं सीतां द्रष्टुमभित्वरन्॥ २॥
verses.m: Thinking of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), sore stricken as he was with darts of love, and being in a great hurry to see Sītā, he directly entered his delightful gynaeceum. (2)

verses.text:
स प्रविश्य तु तद्वेश्म रावणो राक्षसाधिपः।
अपश्यद् राक्षसीमध्ये सीतां दुःखपरायणाम्॥ ३॥
अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं दीनां शोकभारावपीडिताम्।
वायुवेगैरिवाक्रान्तां मज्जन्तीं नावमर्णवे॥ ४॥
मृगयूथपरिभ्रष्टां मृगीं श्वभिरिवावृताम्।
अधोगतमुखीं सीतां तामभ्येत्य निशाचरः॥ ५॥
तां तु शोकवशाद् दीनामवशां राक्षसाधिपः।
सबलाद् दर्शयामास गृहं देवगृहोपमम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Having duly entered that palace, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, for his part saw Sītā given over to woe in the mind of ogresses, her face bathed in tears, distressed as she was, nay, weighed down by the load of grief (she carried in her heart) and resembling a bark buffeted by blasts of wind and foundering in the ocean or a female deer strayed from the herd of deer and beset by hounds. Approaching the aforesaid Sītā, who sat with her face bent down (through humiliation and shame), afflicted as she was through grief, the night-stalker, Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, for his part, forcibly showed her, even though she was unwilling to see it, his palace resembling an abode of gods. (3—6)

verses.text:
हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधं स्त्रीसहस्रनिषेवितम्।
नानापक्षिगणैर्जुष्टं नानारत्नसमन्वितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: The palace was thickly set with mansions and seven-storeyed buildings, was occupied by thousands of women, inhabited by flocks of birds of every description and full of jewels of various kinds. (7)

verses.text:
दान्तकैस्तापनीयैश्च स्फाटिकै राजतैस्तथा।
वज्रवैदूर्यचित्रैश्च स्तम्भैर्दृष्टिमनोरमैः॥ ८॥
verses.m: It was supported on pillars of ivory, gold, crystal and silver, and studded with diamonds and cat’s-eye jewels and was pleasing to the sight as well as to the mind. (8)

verses.text:
दिव्यदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणम्।
सोपानं काञ्चनं चित्रमारुरोह तया सह॥ ९॥
verses.m: The palace resounded with the crash of large kettledrums and was decked with ornaments of refined gold. (In order to show her the palace) he ascended with her the magnificent stairway of gold. (9)

verses.text:
दान्तका राजताश्चैव गवाक्षाः प्रियदर्शनाः।
हेमजालावृताश्चासंस्तत्र प्रासादपङ्क्तयः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Along the stairway there were air-holes of ivory as well as of silver and above them ranged rows of palaces pleasing to look at and covered with trellises of gold. (10)

verses.text:
सुधामणिविचित्राणि भूमिभागानि सर्वशः।
दशग्रीवः स्वभवने प्रादर्शयत मैथिलीम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) showed Sītā (the princess of Mithilā) the floors in his palace paved with mortar and inlaid with gems and hence looking picturesque on all sides. (11)

verses.text:
दीर्घिकाः पुष्करिण्यश्च नानापुष्पसमावृताः।
रावणो दर्शयामास सीतां शोकपरायणाम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa also showed Sītā, who was given over to grief, spacious wells with staircases and ponds hemmed in with flowers of various kinds. (12)

verses.text:
दर्शयित्वा तु वैदेहीं कृत्स्नं तद्भवनोत्तमम्।
उवाच वाक्यं पापात्मा सीतां लोभितुमिच्छया॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having shown Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) the whole of that excellent palace, Rāvaṇa (whose mind was set on sin) for his part spoke as follows to Sītā with intent to enamour her : (13)

verses.text:
दश राक्षसकोट्यश्च द्वाविंशतिरथापराः।
वर्जयित्वा जरावृद्धान् बालांश्च रजनीचरान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Barring the aged ones and infant rangers of the night, there are other ten and twenty-two crores of ogres in my kingdom. (14)

verses.text:
तेषां प्रभुरहं सीते सर्वेषां भीमकर्मणाम्।
सहस्रमेकमेकस्य मम कार्यपुरःसरम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I am the lord, O Sītā, of all the aforesaid ogres of terrible deeds. One thousand of them remain at my beck and call for doing my work alone. (15)

verses.text:
यदिदं राज्यतन्त्रं मे त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्।
जीवितं च विशालाक्षि त्वं मे प्राणैर्गरीयसी॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The entire administration of this state of mine as well as my life, O large-eyed lady, stands consecrated to you. You are more valuable to me even than my life. (16)

verses.text:
बह्वीनामुत्तमस्त्रीणां मम योऽसौ परिग्रहः।
तासां त्वमीश्वरी सीते मम भार्या भव प्रिये॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Be my wife, O beloved Sītā, and as such the queen of all the numerous excellent women, who are my wives. (17)

verses.text:
साधु किं तेऽन्यथाबुद्ध्या रोचयस्व वचो मम।
भजस्व माभितप्तस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Accept my wholesome advice; what will you gain by thinking otherwise (fixing your mind on Rāma)? Therefore, look favourably on me; you ought to show grace to me, who am sore stricken with love. (18)

verses.text:
परिक्षिप्ता समुद्रेण लङ्केयं शतयोजना।
नेयं धर्षयितुं शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “This city of Laṅkā surrounded by the ocean, covers an area of eight hundred miles. It cannot be taken by storm even by gods and demons (taken together) including Indra, the ruler of gods. (19)

verses.text:
न देवेषु न यक्षेषु न गन्धर्वेषु नर्षिषु।
अहं पश्यामि लोकेषु यो मे वीर्यसमो भवेत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “I do not perceive in all the three worlds anyone, among the gods or the Yakṣas or the Gandharvas or the seers of Vedic Mantras, who may prove my equal in prowess. (20)

verses.text:
राज्यभ्रष्टेन दीनेन तापसेन पदातिना।
किं करिष्यसि रामेण मानुषेणाल्पतेजसा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “What will you do with the human Rāma of scant energy, who has been deprived of his sovereignty, is a pauper given to austerities and travels on foot? (21)

verses.text:
भजस्व सीते मामेव भर्ताहं सदृशस्तव।
यौवनं त्वध्रुवं भीरु रमस्वेह मया सह॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Accept me alone, O Sītā; I am a consort worthy of you. Youth is but fleeting, O timid lady; enjoy life with me here in Laṅkā. (22)

verses.text:
दर्शने मा कृथा बुदिं्ध राघवस्य वरानने।
कास्य शक्तिरिहागन्तुमपि सीते मनोरथैः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Do not harbour even the thought of beholding again in this life Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O lady of charming countenance ! What power has he to reach this place even in thought, O Sītā? (23)

verses.text:
न शक्यो वायुराकाशे पाशैर्बद्धुं महाजवः।
दीप्यमानस्य वाप्यग्नेर्ग्रहीतुं विमलाः शिखाः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “A very powerful wind cannot be bound with ropes in the sky nor can the smokeless flames of a blazing fire be seized. (24)

verses.text:
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां न तं पश्यामि शोभने।
विक्रमेण नयेद् यस्त्वां मद्बाहुपरिपालिताम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “In all the three worlds, viz., heaven earth and the intermediate region, I do not perceive a man who may snatch by dint of prowess you, who are protected by my arms, O beautiful lady ! (25)

verses.text:
लङ्कायाः सुमहद्राज्यमिदं त्वमनुपालय।
त्वत्प्रेष्या मद्विधाश्चैव देवाश्चापि चराचरम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Rule you over this vast dominion of Laṅkā. If you agree to this proposal of mine, those like me (viz., the ogres) as well as gods, nay, the entire mobile and immobile creation will automatically become your servants (inasmuch as they are all subservient to my will and I shall be at your beck and call). (26)

verses.text:
अभिषेकजलक्लिन्ना तुष्टा च रमयस्व च।
दुष्कृतं यत्पुरा कर्म वनवासेन तद्गतम्॥ २७॥
यच्च ते सुकृतं कर्म तस्येह फलमाप्नुहि।
इह सर्वाणि माल्यानि दिव्यगन्धानि मैथिलि॥ २८॥
भूषणानि च मुख्यानि तानि सेव मया सह।
पुष्पकं नाम सुश्रोणि भ्रातुर्वैश्रवणस्य मे॥ २९॥
विमानं सूर्यसंकाशं तरसा निर्जितं रणे।
विशालं रमणीयं च तद्विमानं मनोजवम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Nay,1 drenched with the water meant for bath and gratified on being relieved from fatigue, afford delight to me. Whatever sinful act was done by you in the past has been exhausted through exile in the forest. And enjoy here the fruit of such meritorious acts as stand to your credit. Share with me all these garlands emitting a heavenly fragrance as well as the excellent ornments that are available here, O princess of Mithilā. Moreover, there exists an aerial car, Puṣpaka by name, belonging to my (half-) brother, Kubera (son of Sage Viśravā), which shines brightly as the sun and was won by me in an encounter by sheer dint of superior strength, O lady of comely limbs ! Spacious and delightful, the said aerial car is swift as thought. (27—30)

verses.text:
तत्र सीते मया सार्धं विहरस्व यथासुखम्।
वदनं पद्मसंकाशं विमलं चारुदर्शनम्॥ ३१॥
शोकार्तं तु वरारोहे न भ्राजति वरानने।
एवं वदति तस्मिन् सा वस्त्रान्तेन वराङ्गना॥ ३२॥
पिधायेन्दुनिभं सीता मन्दमश्रूण्यवर्तयत्।
ध्यायन्तीं तामिवास्वस्थां सीतां चिन्ताहतप्रभाम्॥ ३३॥
उवाच वचनं वीरो रावणो रजनीचरः।
अलं व्रीडेन वैदेहि धर्मलोपकृतेन ते॥ ३४॥
आर्षोऽयं देवि निष्पन्दो यस्त्वामभिभविष्यति।
एतौ पादौ मया स्निग्धौ शिरोभिः परिपीडितौ॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Divert yourself with me in that car so long as it gratifies you, O Sītā ! Your flawless countenance, resembling a lotus and lovely to look at, does not look charming, oppressed as it is with grief, O lady with a beautiful face and other limbs !” Covering her moonlike face while Rāvaṇa was speaking thus, that lovely lady, Sītā, gently allowed her tears to flow. Rāvaṇa, the valiant prowler of the night, addressed the following words to the aforesaid Sītā, who was definitely ill at ease, her splendour having been bedimmed through anxiety, and was contemplating on Śrī Rāma: “Have done with bashfulness occasioned by transgrassion of the prescribed course of conduct in the shape of leaving one’s husband and accepting another. The tie of love which is going to be established with you by me, O queen, is permitted by the seers of Vedic Mantras, who allow marriage2 by force, giving it the name of Rākṣasa-Vivāha. These tender soles of yours are being lovingly pressed with my heads. (31—35)

verses.text:
प्रसादं कुरु मे क्षिप्रं वश्यो दासोऽहमस्मि ते।
इमाः शून्या मया वाचः शुष्यमाणेन भाषिताः॥ ३६॥
न चापि रावणः कांचिन्मूर्ध्ना स्त्रीं प्रणमेत ह।
